On-device (the real gate for sticky): open Settings on the wall-resolution viewport — the top bar, search, and category rail stay fixed while only the options pane scrolls; the topbar shows the current section name and it updates as you scroll through sections on a migrated category (e.g. Plugins: "Install" → "Installed plugins"); switching categories updates it; at the 768px breakpoint and on a short viewport the page remains fully scrollable/reachable. Light + dark theme both render.

docs.title: 6. Decomposition (for the plan)
docs.text:
1. Sticky app-shell layout — Settings.vue layout <style> rework + token cleanup. On-device-gated.
  2. Topbar section indicator + scroll-spy un-gate — SettingsTopBar.vue (replace breadcrumb with indicator) + Settings.vue (drop onCrumb, un-gate observer) + vitest.

docs.title: 7. Deferred / related
docs.text:
• The new P3 follow-up to align the ZIP-upload install path with no-restart behavior (from E2) is separate.
  • Dead dashboard cleanup (calvin-jat), regions editor (calvin-4k8), C1 polish (calvin-1te), calendar fullscreen (calvin-00s) — unrelated, own beads.

docs.title: Overnight autonomous sprint plan — 2026-06-29
docs.text: Context: User going to bed; granted autonomous execution with subagents (superpowers pipeline) to close multiple open issues. Branch feat/design-settings-cycle-c (PR #60). Push each completed, reviewed cycle. Acting as designer+approver; specs document decisions for morning review.

docs.title: Operating rules
docs.text:
• Preserve all data/behavior contracts: Pinia stores, API/service calls, instance_config_schema + PluginFieldRenderer, calendar/theme data colors, and the FROZEN keyboard action vocabulary (useKeyboardActions.js must not change). Rebuilds = UI/UX only; functionality preserved.
  • Per cycle: brainstorm → spec (docs/design/) → plan (docs/design/plans/) → subagent-driven execution → per-task spec+quality review → whole-branch review → on-device screenshot → push to #60.
  • New shell tokens/components only (no legacy tokens, no hardcoded hex except justified data colors). Stage explicit files only; NEVER stage .beads/ or frontend/public/test-calendar.ics. Commit trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>. Subagents never push.
  • Stop cleanly with a handoff on a genuine taste fork I can't responsibly resolve.

docs.title: Priority order (work top-down; do as many as the night allows)
Phase 0 — Safe, clear-correct (high confidence)
docs.text:
1. calvin-8ou (P1 bug) — breadcrumb/section indicator unreliable. Root-cause hypothesis: the IntersectionObserver uses the VIEWPORT root + rootMargin -70%, but after the E3 sticky app-shell, sections scroll inside .settings-content (offset ~150px under fixed chrome), so the detection band is misaligned. Fix: set observer root to the .settings-content element + tune rootMargin relative to it. Verify on-device across categories. DO FIRST.
  2. ZIP-install no-restart alignment (the P3 from E2 review) — management.py ZIP upload path: call load_plugin_types_for_single(manifest["id"]) + return requires_restart from manifest requirements.restart_required. Small, fully specified.
  3. calvin-jat (P3) — delete dead dashboard components (DashboardCategory + orphaned AppearanceTab/NotificationsTab/SettingsTab, etc.). VERIFY each is truly unreferenced before deleting; run suite.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Source-manager rebuilds (medium confidence; determinable pattern)
docs.text: 1. Shared source-manager pattern + calvin-5io (image/services) + calvin-03m (calendar sources/refresh) — design ONE shell-native source-list CRUD component (add/edit/remove/reorder; empty states; uses each domain's existing store actions), reuse for images, services, and calendar; calendar layers on per-source color (data color preserved) + refresh interval/refresh-now. Behavior preserved via existing stores.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Taste-heavy (lower confidence; build best-effort, morning review is the gate)
docs.text:
1. calvin-svo (P2) — installed-plugin browser rebuild (PluginManager/Card/Instances) shell-native. Preserve PluginFieldRenderer/schema forms, enable/config/test/uninstall/instances wiring. Flag prominently for review (user "unhappy" but cause unspecified — I'll pick a clean, defensible direction).
  2. calvin-1bp (P2) — keyboard mappings editor rebuild, UI only, action set FROZEN.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• calendar/image/services are all "source-list CRUD" → shared pattern decided (build once, reuse).
  • PluginInstaller (1255-line install flow), DisplayScheduleGrid, UpdatesTab, ClockBar editors remain restyled-not-rebuilt candidates ("probably more") — not in this sprint unless time allows; leave beads.
  • Progress tracked in .superpowers/sdd/progress.md (survives compaction).

docs.title: Calvin — Calendar sources + refresh editor rebuild (shell-native)
docs.text: Status: Design (autonomous sprint — designer decisions documented for morning review). Date: 2026-06-30 Bead: calvin-03m. Branch feat/design-settings-cycle-c. Builds on: the shell (SettingsSection/SettingRow/ToggleSwitch/NumberStepper/ConfirmModal), C1–E3.

docs.title: 1. Goal & scope
docs.text:
Rebuild CalendarSourcesTab.vue (724 lines, currently a CollapsibleSection-based form) into a clean shell-native CRUD editor for calendar sources, plus the global refresh control. Behavior preserved exactly — every store/API call, data shape, and the per-source data color stay as-is; only the UI/structure is rebuilt. The component stays at the same path and keeps the same props/emits, so ContentSettings wiring is unchanged.

Non-goals: no backend changes; no change to the calendar store/API; no shared "source-manager" abstraction (image/services are ordering-only and out of scope — see calvin-5io). Calendar data colors are NOT tokenized.

docs.title: 2. Contracts to preserve (verbatim — the rebuild MUST use these)
docs.text:
• Store useCalendarStore (@/stores/calendar): fetchSources(); updateSource(sourceId, fullUpdatedObject) — used for color / show_time / enabled, sends the whole updated source object; sources reactive ref.
  • API @/services/calendarApi: addCalendarSource(sourceObject) and deleteCalendarSource(sourceId) — called directly (not via store); each must be followed by a full fetchSources() re-fetch (the established sync flow).
  • Plugin types pluginsApi.getPlugins({ plugin_type: "calendar" }) → populate the type <select> (enabled calendar plugins; keep the hardcoded fallback list on API error).
  • Running status usePlugins().pluginInstances → derive each source's running dot by matching instance.id === source.id (read-only ●/○).
  • Per-source fields: id (created as `${type}-${Date.now()}`), type, name, ical_url, enabled, color (data hex — keep getColorValue named→hex normalization, default #2196f3; never a token), show_time (default true: treat show_time !== false as on).
  • Refresh: the global interval lives on props.config.calendarRefreshInterval (int 5–120); on change emit("update:config", { calendarRefreshInterval: value }) — NOT in the store. Component keeps defineProps({ config }) + defineEmits(["update:config"]).

docs.title: 3. New UI (shell-native), inside the existing Calendars SettingsSection panel
docs.text:
ContentSettings already wraps this component in <SettingsSection id="content-calendars" title="Calendars">, so the rebuild renders panel content (no new top-level section; no CollapsibleSection).

  1. Add a calendar source — a compact add form at the top:
  2. Type: a shell-styled <select> (dynamic calendar plugin types; fallback list). (A select, not SegmentedControl — the type set is open/dynamic.)
  3. Name: shell text input. URL: shell text input with the per-type dynamic placeholder/help text (preserve current per-type hints).
  4. "Add calendar" button (shell primary, --focus fill, ≥44px), disabled until name + URL non-empty. On add: build the source object (id `${type}-${Date.now()}`, color default, show_time true), calendarApi.addCalendarSource(...), then fetchSources(), then clear the form. Surface errors in a shell status line.
  5. Source list — per-source cards (--bg-2 + --line, ≥44px controls), one per sources entry:
  6. Header: name (--ink, --font-ui) + a type badge + running dot (●=--ok/○=--ink-3, derived).
  7. Color: <input type="color"> bound via getColorValue(source.color); on change → updateSource(id, { ...source, color: hex }). (The native color input value stays raw hex — data.)
  8. "Show times": ToggleSwitch bound to source.show_time !== false; on change → updateSource(id, { ...source, show_time: v }).
  9. Enabled: ToggleSwitch bound to source.enabled; on change → updateSource(id, { ...source, enabled: v }).
  10. Remove: a destructive button (--err) → opens ConfirmModal; on confirm → deleteCalendarSource(id) then fetchSources().
  11. Empty state (no sources): a shell --ink-3 hint.
  12. Refresh — a SettingRow ("Refresh interval", description) at the bottom of the panel with a NumberStepper (min 5, max 120, step 5) bound to config.calendarRefreshInterval, emitting update:config. Add a "Refresh now" action (shell button) that calls calendarStore.refreshEvents() — this surfaces an existing store method not previously exposed; show a brief "Refreshing…/Refreshed" status. (New affordance; behavior-additive, no contract change.)

All new chrome uses new shell tokens only; the per-source color and the getColorValue palette are data and stay as raw hex.

docs.title: 4. Testing
docs.text:
• Preserve/refresh any existing CalendarSourcesTab spec; rewrite assertions tied to the old CollapsibleSection structure.
  • New component tests (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mocked store/api — mirror existing settings component-test harnesses): add-source calls addCalendarSource then fetchSources; color change calls updateSource with the full object + new hex; show_time and enabled toggles call updateSource; remove (after confirm) calls deleteCalendarSource then fetchSources; refresh interval change emits update:config; "Refresh now" calls refreshEvents. Assert the data color is preserved (a source with a named color round-trips through getColorValue without tokenization).
  • Gates: full npx vitest run green; npx eslint src 0/0; grep — no legacy tokens/hex in the rebuilt file except the getColorValue data palette + the #2196f3 default (justified as data).
  • On-device (controller): add a source, edit its color, toggle show-times/enable, remove it; change the interval; click Refresh now.

docs.title: 5. Decomposition (for the plan)
docs.text:
1. Rebuild CalendarSourcesTab.vue — new shell-native template + script (preserving all §2 contracts), tokenized styles. One cohesive task (it's one component; the add-form, card list, and refresh row are interdependent).
  2. Tests — update existing + add the §4 behavior tests. (May fold into task 1 if the harness makes TDD natural; otherwise a second task.)

docs.title: 6. Notes
docs.text:
• getColorValue named→hex map and the #2196f3 default MUST be carried over verbatim (the backend may still return named colors).
  • Keep the add/delete → fetchSources() re-sync; keep updateSource sending the whole object.
  • Do not introduce CollapsibleSection; use flat shell structure within the existing panel.

docs.title: Design: shared ui/IconButton primitive
docs.text: Status: design approved; implementation pending (primitive only — no call-site migration this round). Bead: calvin-b97. Related: calvin-0wr (service regions adopt it), calvin-nxs (one-off header-button fix this supersedes). Depends on: the sizing-token vocabulary in docs/design/2026-07-04-ui-sizing-tokens.md.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The frontend has no shared button component. A catalog of the app found ~8 families of hand-rolled square/icon buttons spanning 28 / 32 / 44 / 46 / 48 / 64px, square and circle, with default / primary / ghost / danger / toggled / disabled variants and inconsistent a11y (some aria-label, some title only). This duplication is the root cause of visible mismatches (e.g. the calendar-vs-service header buttons, calvin-nxs) and of the service-region drift (calvin-0wr).

ui/IconButton.vue gives these one composable primitive built on the existing sizing-token vocabulary, so buttons stop drifting and new/changed code has one obvious thing to reach for. It follows the established ui/ primitive pattern (ToggleSwitch, SegmentedControl, SelectPill, NumberStepper).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In: build and unit-test frontend/src/components/ui/IconButton.vue with the full API below. Migrate zero call sites this round — existing buttons adopt IconButton opportunistically via calvin-0wr and follow-up tranches. This keeps the change small and verifiable without live visual QA.

Out: the pill triggers (SelectPill / ThemePicker — composite text+swatch+chevron), the hot-corner (bespoke, setting-driven gradient), ChipMultiSelect chips, and text action buttons (.btn-primary/.btn-secondary/.btn-danger, .settings-topbar__done). These are not icon buttons.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Single <button type="button"> root, so every aria-* attribute (e.g. aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, aria-pressed) and @click falls through natively — no prop plumbing for those.

<IconButton
  label="Close"          <!-- required → aria-label -->
  variant="default"      <!-- default | primary | ghost | danger  (default: default) -->
  size="sm"              <!-- sm | md | lg                          (default: sm) -->
  shape="square"         <!-- square | circle                       (default: square) -->
  :active="false"        <!-- lit/toggled state                     (default: false) -->
  :disabled="false"      <!--                                        (default: false) -->
  @click="onClick"
>
  <svg …/>               <!-- glyph / icon slot (required content) -->
</IconButton>

Props

prop type default notes label String (required) — becomes aria-label; standardizes the a11y inconsistency variant String "default" one of default/primary/ghost/danger; validated size String "sm" one of sm/md/lg; validated shape String "square" one of square/circle; validated active Boolean false lit/toggled modifier (e.g. tune-active, --on) disabled Boolean false reflected to the native disabled attribute

@click is the native button click via fallthrough; no explicit emits needed. Disabled buttons emit no click (native behavior).

Size → tokens

size box font-size sm min-width/height: 1.75rem (28px) 1.05rem md min-width/height: var(--touch-target) (44px) var(--fs-xl) (1.25rem) lg min-width/height: var(--control-height) (48px) 1.5rem

Shape: square → border-radius: var(--radius-sm) (8px); circle → border-radius: 50%.

Variant → token map

variant rest hover default bg --bg-2, border --line, color --ink border --focus-edge primary bg --focus, color --focus-ink, border --focus filter: brightness(1.08) ghost transparent bg, transparent border, color --ink-2 bg --bg-2, color --ink danger bg --bg-2, border --line, color --err border --err active (modifier) overlays color --focus + border --focus-edge —

Behavior - Base: inline-flex, centered, cursor: pointer, font-family: var(--font-ui), 1px solid border (color per variant), transition: background/border-color/color .2s. - :focus-visible → outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px. - disabled → opacity: .5; cursor: not-allowed; pointer-events: none. - @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) → transition: none. - Token-based sizing means it inherits the Settings-UI-size zoom automatically.

docs.title: Deferred (noted, not built)
docs.text: The touchControlSize-driven cluster (RegionControls .cbtn, Family D) uses sizes 36/42/50px that don't map to sm/md/lg. When Family D migrates (a follow-up tranche), add a CSS-var size escape-hatch (e.g. consumer sets style="--icon-size: …; --icon-font: …" and a size="custom" reads them). Not built now (YAGNI).

docs.title: Testing (TDD)
docs.text: frontend/tests/unit/components/ui/IconButton.spec.js (mirror existing ui/*.spec.js): 1. renders a <button> with aria-label = label. 2. applies the correct variant / size / shape / active / disabled classes for given props. 3. forwards @click; a disabled instance sets the disabled attribute and fires no click. 4. renders default-slot content. 5. aria-expanded (and other aria-*) passed by a consumer fall through to the <button>.

docs.title: Success criteria
docs.text:
• IconButton.vue exists, exercises every variant/size/shape/state via the token vocabulary, and passes its unit tests; lint/build green.
  • No call sites changed this round; the primitive is ready for calvin-0wr and follow-ups to adopt.

docs.title: UI sizing tokens — vocabulary & region-editor handoff
docs.text:
Status: contract agreed, implementation in progress (foundation lands in theme.css + ui/ primitives). Audience: the region-editor redesign (beads calvin-bvw) and anyone tokenizing component chrome. Related: calvin-bvw (parked on this scale), calvin-4d2 (regions-editor cohesion pass).

This doc is the single source of truth for the sizing token names and their baselines. Do not invent parallel token names — adopt the ones below verbatim.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
Calvin has a user-configurable "Settings UI size" (Settings → Dashboard → Appearance) that scales the settings/config interface only — text, every control, modals. The live dashboard is deliberately untouched: it keeps its own sizing (region touch controls via touchControlSize, clock bar via clockBarFontSize). A separate "Dashboard UI size" is a distinct future control.

  • Discrete presets (SegmentedControl), even 0.15 steps: Extra-compact 0.70 · Compact 0.85 · Default 1.0 · Large 1.15 · Extra-large 1.3 (labelled XS · S · M · L · XL).
  • Mechanism: zoom: var(--ui-scale) on the settings content root (.settings-scale in Settings.vue). zoom scales the whole settings subtree regardless of unit and is contained to it, so nothing leaks to the dashboard. --ui-scale is set on <html> at runtime by useUiScale and inherited down. Scale 1 is a no-op.
  • Persisted as a string preset key uiSize via /api/config; the key→factor map lives in frontend/src/styles/uiScale.js.

docs.title: Where the tokens fit
docs.text:
The scaling is the settings zoom above — not a per-token multiplier. The --fs-* / --space-* / --radius-* / --touch-target tokens below are the shared sizing vocabulary: one named scale for the settings shell and the region editor (calvin-bvw), replacing scattered magic numbers.

Every token's baseline equals the literal it replaces (rem baselines are the prior px ÷ 16). So adopting a token in place of its matching literal is a visual no-op — a safe, screenshot-diffable mechanical swap — while giving everything one coherent scale that the settings zoom then drives.

docs.title: Token vocabulary
docs.text:
Declared once in frontend/src/styles/theme.css :root (theme-independent — not duplicated into .dark).

Naming caution: the existing --text-* and --switch-* tokens are colors. The sizing scale therefore uses --fs-* (font-size) and --toggle-* (switch geometry) to avoid any confusion. --space-*, --radius-*, --touch-target, --control-height are new.

docs.title: Control sizing (scaled)
docs.text: Token Baseline Use --touch-target 44px The ~47 repeated min-height: 44px touch minimums --control-height 48px Pill trigger height, text-input height

docs.title: Toggle geometry (scaled)
docs.text: Token Baseline --toggle-w 56px --toggle-h 32px --toggle-knob 26px --toggle-inset 3px --toggle-travel calc(var(--toggle-w) - var(--toggle-knob) - 2*var(--toggle-inset)) → 24px @1

docs.title: Spacing scale (scaled)
docs.text: Token Baseline Token Baseline --space-3xs 0.25rem --space-lg 0.75rem --space-2xs 0.35rem --space-xl 1rem --space-xs 0.4rem --space-2xl 1.25rem --space-sm 0.5rem --space-3xl 1.5rem --space-md 0.6rem

docs.title: Type scale (scaled)
docs.text: Token Baseline Token Baseline --fs-micro 0.72rem --fs-base 1rem --fs-2xs 0.75rem --fs-lg 1.15rem --fs-xs 0.8rem --fs-xl 1.25rem --fs-sm 0.85rem --fs-control 14px (control label) --fs-md 0.9rem --fs-control-lg 15px (pill / input)

docs.title: Radius scale (scaled, except pill)
docs.text: Token Baseline Token Baseline --radius-xs 6px --radius-xl 12px --radius-sm 8px --radius-2xl 16px --radius-md 10px --radius-pill 999px (FIXED) --radius-lg 11px

docs.title: What stays FIXED (do not tokenize / do not scale)
docs.text:
• --radius-pill: 999px — a pill is a pill at any size (already clamps to half-height).
  • 1px borders / hairlines — scaling to 1.3px produces blurry sub-pixel lines.
  • 2px focus outlines + 2px offsets — an accessibility constant; keep consistent across sizes.
  • Box-shadow blur/spread — aesthetic, leave literal.
  • ch-based widths (2.5ch, 3.5ch) and border-radius: 50% — already self-proportional to their font.

Bespoke internal values that don't land on a scale (e.g. padding: 10px 18px, gap: 7px): don't mint a one-off token — wrap the literal inline as calc(10px * var(--ui-scale)). This preserves the exact baseline and still scales.

docs.title: What you get for FREE — no edits
docs.text: DashboardRegionsEditor.vue composes the shared primitives SelectPill, ToggleSwitch, SegmentedControl, NumberStepper. Once those primitives consume the tokens (foundation work, done by us), every control inside the editor scales automatically with zero edits to the editor file. That is precisely why the editor was parked on this scale.

docs.title: What YOU own — the editor's container chrome
docs.text:
The editor's own <style> block still hardcodes the wrapper radii, gaps/paddings, and font sizes listed in calvin-bvw. During the redesign, replace those literals with the tokens using this 1:1 map (mechanical find-replace, zero visual change at Default):

Editor literal Token 6px radius --radius-xs 8px radius --radius-sm 10px radius --radius-md 11px radius --radius-lg 12px radius --radius-xl 999px radius --radius-pill 0.35rem spacing --space-2xs 0.4rem spacing --space-xs 0.5rem spacing --space-sm 0.6rem spacing --space-md 0.75rem spacing --space-lg 0.75rem font --fs-2xs 0.8rem font --fs-xs 0.85rem font --fs-sm 0.9rem font --fs-md 1rem font --fs-base

Example — a region wrapper today: 

.preview-region { border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.5rem 0.6rem; gap: 0.4rem; font-size: 0.85rem; }
becomes: 
.preview-region {
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  padding: var(--space-sm) var(--space-md);
  gap: var(--space-xs);
  font-size: var(--fs-sm);
}
No behavioural change at Default; the whole panel now scales with the user's UI-size preference.

docs.title: Design guidance for the redesign
docs.text:
• Aim for the compact feel of RegionViewOptions.vue (the dashboard "tune" popover): 1.75rem triggers, 0.4rem gaps, 8–10px radii, rem-based. That is the reference "feel" the user likes.
  • Do not re-introduce hardcoded px for anything on the scale above — reach for a token so the editor honors UI-size.
  • The --region-calendar/-photos/-service accent colors and --focus-ink on-accent text are already in place; keep using them (no raw hex).

docs.title: Out of scope (this iteration)
docs.text: • Live-dashboard region-control cluster (RegionControls.vue) stays on its separate touchControlSize config and does not consume these tokens — it must remain independent for now. (Opting it in later is trivial once these tokens exist, but is a deliberate future decision, not part of this work.)

docs.title: CLV-9 admin auth: UI spec
docs.text: Status: ready to build. Source design: ~/.herdr-projects/reports/calvin/9/report.md §3 and §4. Mockups: mocks/clv-9/admin-auth.html. Rendered PNGs are in mocks/clv-9/png/ (fig-N.png, numbered in board order, A1 = fig-1 … C4 = fig-16). The mock board uses the real theme.css tokens. Where this doc and the mock disagree, this doc wins.

docs.title: 0. Ground rules
docs.text:
• No new visual language. Build only from existing tokens (--bg-*, --ink-*, --line*, --focus*, --ok/--warn/--err, --touch-target, --control-height, --space-*, --radius-*, --fs-*) and existing components: SettingsTopBar, SettingsSection, SettingRow, PhoneSetupCard, DialogScrim, the .security-btn / .security-btn--primary button styles in SecuritySettings.vue, and useNotificationsStore().notify for toasts.
  • The word is Sign in / Sign out everywhere. Never "log in" or "logout" in UI copy.
  • One field type: a password. There is no username field anywhere visible (see §6, password managers).
  • Copy in this doc is verbatim. Quotes, apostrophes (use ’ or ' consistently with the codebase: '), and full stops are part of the copy.
  • Touch targets: every button and the Show toggle are at least --touch-target (44px) tall. Password inputs are --control-height (48px) tall.

docs.title: 1. New pieces (component map)
docs.text: Piece Path What it is PasswordField frontend/src/components/ui/PasswordField.vue Label + <input type=password> + Show/Hide toggle + hint/error line. Used everywhere below. AuthLockScreen frontend/src/components/settings/auth/AuthLockScreen.vue The Settings lock screen (setup and sign-in variants, §2). AdminSignInDialog frontend/src/components/auth/AdminSignInDialog.vue The in-place dialog (§3). Mounted once in App.vue, driven by the auth store. AdminAccessSection frontend/src/components/settings/categories/security/AdminAccessSection.vue Security tab additions (§4). useRateLimitCountdown frontend/src/composables/useRateLimitCountdown.js Turns a 429 into a ticking m:ss string + locked boolean. Shared by all three forms.

docs.title: PasswordField
docs.text:
Props: modelValue, label, autocomplete (current-password or new-password), hint, error, disabled, revealed (v-model:revealed, so one toggle can drive two fields), showToggle (default true), inputId.

  • Input: full width, height --control-height, padding: 0 4.75rem 0 0.875rem (room for the toggle), background: var(--bg-2), border: 1px solid var(--line), border-radius: var(--radius-sm), font: 1rem var(--font-ui) (1rem, not --fs-control: iOS zooms on inputs under 16px).
  • Hover: border-color: var(--focus-edge). Focus: border-color: var(--focus) + box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--focus) 20%, transparent). This is the same as .security-origins__input.
  • Error: border-color: var(--err), aria-invalid="true"; the error text sits under the input in --fs-sm and --err and is linked with aria-describedby. The hint (if any) is in --ink-2 and is replaced by the error while one shows.
  • Show toggle: a text button inside the input on the right, min-width: var(--touch-target), height = input height minus 4px, transparent background, --ink-2, --fs-control weight 500. Its label is Show or Hide. It has aria-pressed and aria-controls = input id, and aria-label="Show password" / "Hide password". Toggling it keeps focus and caret in the input (@mousedown.prevent).
  • Attributes: autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false". Paste is always allowed (never @paste.prevent), so password managers work (WCAG 2.2 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication).
  • Focus: the input uses the focus ring above. The Show toggle and every button here get :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px }, matching .security-btn.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
Settings.vue renders AuthLockScreen instead of .settings-body while auth.status !== 'authenticated'. SettingsTopBar stays and gets a new locked prop. When it is true, the save pill and the "📱 Use your phone" button are hidden (the lock screen shows the phone hand-off itself) and only the wordmark, the location label "Settings" and Done remain. Done returns to the dashboard as it does today.

The search box and category rail are not rendered while locked. Deep links (?setting=…) are kept in the URL and honoured after sign-in.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Container: the area below the top bar, background: var(--bg-0), flex, centred both ways, padding: 24px.
  • Card: width: 26rem; max-width: 100%, padding: 2rem, background: var(--bg-1), border: 1px solid var(--line), border-radius: 16px (same as .settings-section__panel). Contents are left-aligned.
  • Lock icon: 44px circle, background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--focus) 14%, transparent), color: var(--focus), 20px stroke lock glyph (inline SVG, aria-hidden), 16px below. Hidden when the viewport is narrower than 480px or shorter than 600px.
  • Title <h1>: --fs-xl, weight 600, --font-ui, line-height 1.3, 6px below.
  • Lead <p>: 0.95rem, --ink-2, line-height 1.45, 20px below.
  • Fields: 16px apart. Primary button: full width, --control-height, 1rem text, .security-btn--primary look.
  • Recovery block: 20px above, a 1px --line-soft rule, then 16px padding-top. --fs-sm, --ink-2, line-height 1.5. File and env names in <code> (--font-data, 0.85em, --bg-0 chip, 4px radius).
  • Touch kiosk (useTouchCapability().isTouch): a row of card, then the "or" seam, then PhoneSetupCard (default size, 200px QR). The seam is a vertical 1px --line rule broken by the word "or" (--ink-3, --fs-md), with margin: 40px 32px. The kiosk's own field is the main path: tapping it brings up the on-screen keyboard (2026-10-29-on-screen-keyboard.md §6). The phone card is the alternative, and it is hidden while the keyboard is up.
  • Short kiosk (height < 600px, e.g. 800×480): card width: 22rem, padding: 1.25rem, no icon, recovery block hidden, lead 12px below. PhoneSetupCard compact, stacked (QR above text), and hint="" so only title + URL show. Seam margin 24px 16px. See A7.
  • Not touch (laptop/desktop): card only, centred. No phone card.
  • Phone width (< 480px): card full width with a 16px page gutter, aligned to the top (24px from the top bar), padding: 1.5rem 1.25rem, no icon. No phone card (they are on the phone). See A3 to A6.
  • isTouch is true on a phone too. Decide between "kiosk" and "phone" on width: show the phone card only when isTouch && viewport width ≥ 720px.

docs.title: States
docs.text:
S0. Checking. While GET /api/auth/status is pending: render nothing for 300ms, then a centred line "Checking…" in --ink-2, 0.95rem. No spinner.

S1. Status failed (network error / 5xx). The card shows (A8): - Title: Can't reach Calvin - Lead: Settings can't check whether you're signed in. Check that the server is running and this device is on the same network. - Button: Try again (primary, full width). It refetches status. While refetching the label is Checking… and the button is disabled. - No fields, no phone card, no recovery block.

S2. Setup (configured: false) (A1, A6) - Title: Choose an admin password - Lead: Anyone on your network who knows it can change Calvin. The dashboard stays open to everyone. - Field 1: label Password, autocomplete="new-password", hint At least 8 characters., with the Show toggle. The toggle reveals both fields (v-model:revealed shared). - Field 2: label Repeat password, autocomplete="new-password", no toggle (showToggle=false). - Button: Set password. While submitting: Setting password…, disabled, both fields disabled. - Recovery footnote (always visible, not collapsible): If you forget it, delete admin-auth.json from Calvin's data folder, or set CALVIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD, then restart Calvin. - Client validation never runs while typing. It runs on blur of a non-empty field (field 1: length; field 2: match) and again on submit, in this order: 1. Password shorter than 8 characters (count code points: [...value].length): error on field 1, Use at least 8 characters. 2. Fields differ: error on field 2, The passwords don't match. Focus moves to the first field with an error. Errors clear when that field next changes. Don't trim. Spaces and any characters are allowed. - Success (200): the store sets authenticated. Settings renders normally at the deep-linked or last category. Toast (notify, type success): Admin password set. - 409 (someone configured it first) → go to S3 sign-in with a warn banner in place of the lead (A5): Someone else set the admin password a moment ago. Sign in with it, or ask them for it. Clear the typed passwords. Focus the password field. - 422 / 400 from the server (length rule disagreement): show the server's detail as the field 1 error. Fallback: Use at least 8 characters. - Network error: error banner above the button, Couldn't reach Calvin. Check the connection and try again. The fields keep their values.

S3. Sign in (configured: true, not authenticated) (A2 to A5) - Title: Sign in to Settings - Lead: Enter the admin password for this Calvin. - Field: label Admin password, autocomplete="current-password", Show toggle. - Button: Sign in / while submitting Signing in… (disabled, field disabled). - Recovery: a <details>, collapsed by default. Summary Forgot the password? (--ink, underlined, min-height --touch-target). Body: Someone with access to the server deletes admin-auth.json from Calvin's data folder and restarts Calvin. Settings then asks for a new password. Or set CALVIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD and restart. That password always wins. - Empty submit: field error Enter the admin password. (no request sent). - Wrong password (401, any code other than admin_required/setup_required): field error That's not the admin password. Keep the value, select it all, keep focus (A3). - Rate limited (429): see §5. Error banner above the field (A4). - Network error: same banner as S2. - Success: same as S2, with no toast (signing in needs no announcement).

Status changes underneath. If status comes back configured: false while S3 shows (someone deleted the file and restarted), the next submit gets setup_required. Switch to S2 with the warn banner Calvin's admin password was reset. Choose a new one.

docs.title: 3. In-place sign-in dialog (401 admin_required outside the lock screen)
Trigger
docs.text:
A response interceptor on the default axios instance and on services/api.js. On status 401 && data.code === 'admin_required' it calls auth.requestSignIn({ action }) and rejects the original promise as usual, so the caller's own error handling still runs. The caller must not show its own error toast for this case: give the rejected error a flag err.adminRequired = true that callers can skip on. data.code === 'setup_required' opens the dialog in its no-password variant (D2). The interceptor ignores 401s from /api/auth/* (those are form errors, §2).

action is derived from the request URL in one map in the auth store. That map is the only place copy is chosen:

Request verb (title) gerund (lead) phone settingId POST /api/system/reboot reboot Rebooting Calvin device-reboot POST /api/system/update* update Updating Calvin maintenance-updates anything else continue This change null (Settings landing)

Inside Settings (a session expired because the password was changed elsewhere), the same dialog opens over Settings. Unsaved edits on screen are kept. Don't bounce to the lock screen.

Only one dialog at a time. Further 401s while it is open update nothing.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• DialogScrim blur (z 999) + panel (z 1000), role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby = title.
  • Panel: background: var(--bg-1), border: 1px solid var(--line), border-radius: 14px, box-shadow: 0 18px 50px -16px var(--shadow-hover), padding: 1.5rem. This is the same look as .settings-phone.
  • Narrow (no phone card): width: min(30rem, calc(100vw - 32px)), centred. At < 480px wide it sits at the bottom: bottom: 16px, centred horizontally (B2 to B4), so the phone keyboard pushes it up rather than covering it.
  • Touch kiosk (isTouch && width ≥ 720px): width: min(56rem, calc(100vw - 32px)), padding: 1.75rem, 3-column grid 1fr auto 1fr: form, "or" seam (margin: 8px 24px), PhoneSetupCard compact stacked (QR above text) with setting-id from the action map (B1). Buttons stretch to equal width at --control-height.
  • Buttons, right-aligned on narrow: Cancel (.security-btn) then the primary.

docs.title: States
docs.text:
D1. Sign in (B1, B2) - Title: Sign in to {verb}. For "continue" the title is Sign in to continue. - Lead: {gerund} needs the admin password. - Field Admin password (as in S3). - Buttons: Cancel, Sign in / Signing in…. - Kiosk phone card: title {Verb} from your phone ("Continue from your phone" for the generic case), hint Signing in on your phone doesn't unlock this screen. Open this address, sign in, and {verb} from there. Generic hint: Signing in on your phone doesn't unlock this screen. Open this address and sign in there. (Why: the cookie is per browser. Signing in on the phone grants the phone, not the kiosk. The QR must lead to where the action lives on the phone.) - Wrong password, empty submit, 429, network: exactly as S3, inside the dialog. - Success: close the dialog, return focus to the element that was focused before it opened, toast (success): Signed in. {Verb} again to continue. (generic: Signed in. Try again to continue.). Never auto-replay the request. Reboot and update are destructive and the person should choose again.

D2. No password set (setup_required) (B3) - Title: No admin password yet - Lead: {gerund} needs an admin password, and none has been set. Choose one in Settings first. - No field. Buttons: Cancel, Open Settings (routes to /settings, which shows S2). - Kiosk: phone card as in A1 (title Set it up from your phone, settingId null).

Dismiss: Cancel, Escape, or a scrim tap. All three discard the typed password.

docs.title: 4. Settings › Security: Admin access
docs.text:
A new first section in SecuritySettings.vue: <SettingsSection id="security-admin" title="Admin access">, above "Sealed mode". Add a registry destination security-admin (keywords: password, sign out, admin, lock) so search and ?setting=security-admin work.

Row 1, a SettingRow: - Label: a 8px --ok dot + Signed in on this device - Description: Signing out here doesn't sign out other devices. - Control: Sign out (.security-btn). It calls POST /api/auth/logout and Settings immediately shows S3. No confirmation, because it is reversible. While pending: Signing out…, disabled. If it fails on the network, still clear local auth state and show S3 (the cookie is HttpOnly, so the server is the source of truth and the next status call settles it).

Row 2, a SettingRow: - Label Admin password. Description: Changing it signs out every other device. - Control: Change password (.security-btn). Tapping it expands the form below the row and hides this button. Focus moves to Current password.

Change form (inside the same panel, padding: 0.25rem 1.25rem 1.25rem, top rule --line-soft) (C1): - Two PasswordFields side by side at ≥ 720px (grid 1fr 1fr, gap 16px, max-width: 40rem), stacked below: - Current password (autocomplete="current-password", own Show toggle) - New password (autocomplete="new-password", own Show toggle, hint At least 8 characters.) - Buttons, left-aligned: Cancel (collapses the form and clears it), Change password (primary) / Changing password…. - Validation on submit: empty current → Enter your current password.; new < 8 → Use at least 8 characters.; new === current → Choose a password different from the current one. - Wrong current (401 from /api/auth/password with a non-admin_required code): error on Current, That's not the current password. - 401 admin_required (this session was signed out meanwhile): the global dialog (§3) handles it, and the form keeps its values. - 429: the §5 banner between the fields and the buttons. Fields and the primary button are disabled (C4). - Success: collapse the form, show ✓ Password changed. Other devices were signed out. in --ok, --fs-md, weight 500, role="status", in the row's description area. It stays until you leave the tab (C3). This device stays signed in (the server re-issues its cookie). - Phone width: SettingRow stacks (control full width, C2). While the form is open, hide both rows' descriptions to save height (C4).

docs.title: 5. Rate limit (429), shared
docs.text:
• The wait comes from the Retry-After response header (seconds). Fallback: data.retry_after, then 60. Backend ask: the login, setup and password endpoints must send Retry-After on 429.
  • useRateLimitCountdown(seconds) exposes locked and remaining formatted m:ss (0:47, 2:00, 15:00). It ticks with setInterval(1000) against an absolute deadline (Date.now() + s*1000) so a background tab doesn't drift. It is cleared on unmount.
  • UI: an error banner above the field(s) (above the buttons on the change form): Too many wrong passwords. Try again in {m:ss}. The banner role="status" updates the text each second, but the live region must not announce every tick. Put aria-live="polite" on a visually hidden copy that is set once at lock and once at unlock (You can try again now.).
  • While locked: inputs and the primary button are disabled. Cancel and Show stay enabled. At 0 the banner disappears, the inputs re-enable, and focus returns to the password input.
  • Banner style (also used for warn and network): flex, 12px 14px padding, --radius-md, 1px border, --fs-md, line-height 1.45.
  • err: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--err) 8%, var(--bg-1)), border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--err) 40%, transparent)
  • warn: the same with --warn, 10% / 45%.
  • Text stays --ink. The colour is only in the tint and the border, so contrast holds in both themes.

docs.title: 6. Keyboard and accessibility
docs.text:
• Every variant is a real <form>; Enter submits. KeyboardHandler already ignores keydown in INPUT, so dashboard shortcuts won't fire while typing. Don't add exceptions there.
  • Lock screen: on non-touch, autofocus the first field. On touch, do not autofocus: the kiosk's on-screen keyboard would pop up unasked and cover the phone card, and a phone would jump the page.
  • Dialog: focus trap (Tab cycles inside). Initial focus on the password field on non-touch, and on the dialog title (tabindex=-1) on touch. Escape = Cancel. On close, restore focus to the opener.
  • Password managers: each password form includes a visually hidden <input type="text" name="username" autocomplete="username" value="admin" readonly tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"> so saved passwords attach to one consistent account. Nothing about it is visible.
  • Errors: aria-invalid + aria-describedby on the field, and focus goes to the first invalid field. Banners use role="status" (warn) or role="alert" (network error). The 429 banner follows §5.
  • The QR <img> keeps PhoneSetupCard's alt text. The URL stays as selectable text for screen readers.
  • Settings UI-size zoom (--ui-scale on .settings-page) applies to the lock screen automatically. Check it at 1.25.
  • Reduced motion: none of this animates except DialogScrim's existing fade, which already respects it.

docs.title: 7. Notes for the coordinator / builders (found while designing)
docs.text:
1. Kiosk typing depends on the on-screen keyboard spec (its own issue). Until that lands, the kiosk variants still work through the phone card. Nothing in this spec has to wait for it.

  2. The dashboard ⋯ menu has no Reboot or Update today. AdminOverflow.vue offers Settings, Lock layout and Hide controls. regionsLocked and showUI are display keys, so they stay public. The only dashboard-side admin action is the keyboard reboot combo in KeyboardHandler.vue, and it calls fetch("/api/system/reboot"), not axios, so the interceptor never sees its 401. Either move it to axios, or have it call auth.requestSignIn({ action }) itself on a 401 admin_required. On a kiosk with no pointer, that dialog then needs the phone path (B1), which is exactly why it is there.

  3. Retry-After on 429 (§5) is a backend requirement the report doesn't state.
  4. The Settings › Security registry subtitle becomes Admin password · allowed origins · network access.
  5. Tests (vitest): lock screen renders S2 vs S3 from status; 409 switches S2 → S3 with the banner; 429 disables the form and the countdown reaches 0 and re-enables; interceptor opens the dialog for admin_required and not for /api/auth/login 401s; dialog never replays the request; the action map picks verb/settingId by URL.

docs.title: Deployment-aware System + kiosk software (CLV-19)
docs.text: Status: spec, rescuing the still-useful parts of PR #110 ("Deployment-aware Maintenance settings tab", calvin-ebl, July 2026) onto today's Settings. Mockup: mocks/clv-19/clv-19.html, PNGs in mocks/clv-19/png/ (s1.png … s4.png). Built only from existing tokens and components. Owner decision (§4): container self-restart is not built.

docs.title: 1. Gap analysis: PR #110's five ideas against develop
docs.text: # #110 idea Verdict Where it is on develop What's left 1 GET /api/system/environment with deployment and capability flags Done (#129, calvin-hhok) backend/app/api/routes/system.py:270 returns deployment, host_control, capabilities {update, restart, reboot}, update_instructions. frontend/src/composables/useSystem.js:19-57 loads it once per page. Nothing structural. #110 split restart into backend and frontend flags; develop has one restart. That's enough once the frontend row is renamed (§3.3). 2 Deployment-aware tab: git update UI only where it works, host-update hint in Docker, restart rows per capability Mostly done (#129 + CLV-2 + CLV-17) UpdatesTab.vue:3 shows "How to update" in containers. MaintenanceSettings.vue:21-35 hides the restart rows when deployment === "docker" or host_control === false. Partly missing: (a) the rows are gated on host control, not on capabilities.restart, so a native Pi with host control but no systemctl/helper shows buttons that answer 500; (b) "Restart frontend" actually restarts calvin-kiosk.service (the kiosk browser, see scripts/restart-calvin-services.sh:39), and its label says otherwise. 3 "Restart backend" in Docker: SIGTERM itself after a 200, compose brings it back Missing, needs an owner decision system.py:46 _reject_in_container refuses it with 409. See §4. 4 "Kiosk agents" fleet section: version vs available bundle, online dot, Update / Updating… / needs OS update, hidden with no kiosks Partly done KiosksSettings.vue:48-63 has the per-kiosk Update / Updating… / "needs OS update" controls, and stores/kiosks.js:48-56 has triggerUpdate and fetchAvailableAgentVersion. Missing: no versions are shown anywhere, there is no fleet summary or "update all", and nothing in System says kiosks are behind. Wrong: every error… status is labelled "needs OS update", but the updater also reports rollbacks (deploy/kiosk-agent/update-kiosk.sh:550, "rolled back to previous version"). 5 Registry destinations and docs Partly obsolete, partly missing CLV-17 already added maintenance-system (System › Restart) and the "docker/image/pull" style keywords. Missing: a kiosks-software destination. docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md:174-190 should mention the summary row. The "Updates · agents · diagnostics" subtitle is obsolete (it conflicts with CLV-17's subtitle and the new placement).

docs.title: 2. Where the kiosk fleet view lives: Kiosks, with one pointer from System
docs.text:
Decision: in Kiosks, not System. System is about this server (its version, its restart, its backups). Kiosks is already the per-device home: the cards there have the online dot, last seen and the Update button. A second fleet list in System would duplicate state and controls. Instead:

  • Kiosks gets a "Kiosk software" summary at the top of its list, versions on every card, and fixed states (§3.1–3.2).
  • System › Updates gets one pointer row, shown only while at least one kiosk can be updated (§3.4).

docs.title: 3.1 Kiosks › "Kiosk software" summary row
docs.text:
Placed in KiosksSettings.vue inside SettingsSection id="kiosks-list", above the kiosk cards and below the intro or "+ Add kiosk" button. It is a SettingRow (existing shell component).

Shown only when at least one registered kiosk reports an agent version (k.agentVersion != null). Browser-only kiosks (?kiosk=name) have no agent. With none, the row is omitted, so an all-in-one or browser-only setup sees no noise.

Inputs: availableVersion from fetchAvailableAgentVersion(), and the kiosks with an agent. Let behind = agent kiosks with agentVersion !== availableVersion that aren't blocked, where blocked means the last update failed because the kiosk's OS is too old (§3.2, "needs a newer OS"). Retrying those can't succeed, so they are never counted or included in Update all. Let updating = kiosks with agentUpdateRequested. When every out-of-date kiosk is blocked, the row shows the "all up to date" state's sibling: No kiosk can be updated right now. {n} need(s) a newer OS first.

State Label Description Control Manifest not loaded yet Kiosk software Checking for updates… none Manifest failed (availableVersion == null after load) Kiosk software Couldn't check for kiosk updates. The kiosks keep working. Try again (.btn) All up to date Kiosk software All kiosks are up to date ({v}). none Some behind, none updating Kiosk software {n} of {total} kiosks can be updated to {v}. (1 → 1 kiosk can be updated to {v}.) Update all (.btn--primary) Updating Kiosk software Updating {n} kiosk(s)… They restart their screen when done. Update all, disabled, label Updating…
  • {v} = the available version, shown as the first 7 characters in --font-data (versions are commit hashes). {total} counts only agent kiosks.
  • Update all calls store.triggerUpdate(id) for each kiosk in behind that is online. Offline ones get the request too: the flag waits for their next poll, as today. The row then refreshes the list. No confirmation, because updates are safe (rollback is automatic).
  • If any triggerUpdate rejects: a notify error toast Couldn't start the update on {id}. The others continue.

docs.title: 3.2 Kiosk card: version line and update states
docs.text:
Each kiosk-card keeps its layout (id, online dot, hostname · seen). A third meta line is added under kiosk-card__meta, in the same style (--fs-sm, --ink-2), only for kiosks with an agent:

State Version line Button row (existing kiosk-card__update-row) Up to date Kiosk software {cur} · up to date none Update available Kiosk software {cur} · {v} available Update Requested Updating to {v}… Updating… (disabled) Failed: Python too old (agentUpdateStatus starts with error and the message contains python) Kiosk software {cur} · update needs a newer OS in --warn Update hidden. A --fs-sm line: Reinstall this kiosk with a current Raspberry Pi OS, then update. Failed: other (error, for example rollback) Kiosk software {cur} · last update failed, kept this version in --err Try again (same onUpdate) No agent (agentVersion == null) no line none
  • {cur} = the kiosk's agentVersion, first 7 characters, --font-data.
  • The existing "needs OS update" span is removed. The rows above replace it.
  • Backend need (small): the kiosk list must expose the agent's failure message, not just error…. Add agentUpdateMessage (the updater's message field, already written by update-kiosk.sh:268) to GET /api/kiosks. Until it lands, treat every error as "other".
  • Touch: Update, Try again and Update all have min-height: var(--touch-target).
  • Phone width (< 480px): the summary SettingRow stacks (control full width), and the cards already stack.

docs.title: 3.3 System › Restart (MaintenanceSettings.vue)
docs.text:
• Gate the restart rows on environment.capabilities.restart === true, not on deployment/host control. Keep today's fallback: when the environment request failed (environment == null), show the rows.
  • Rename Restart frontend → Restart kiosk browser, with description Restarts the browser on this Pi's screen. The server keeps running. (It restarts calvin-kiosk.service.) Confirm dialog: title Restart the kiosk browser?, message The screen goes blank for a few seconds., button Restart browser.
  • Restart backend → label Restart Calvin server, description Restarts Calvin. Screens reconnect on their own in about 15 seconds. Confirm: title Restart the Calvin server?, message Settings and screens lose connection for about 15 seconds., button Restart server.
  • Reload UI stays visible always (it is client-side, MaintenanceSettings.vue:157).
  • When the restart rows are hidden in a container, add one --fs-sm --ink-2 line under Reload UI: To restart the server, restart the Calvin container from Docker (Unraid: Docker tab). Show it only when deployment === "docker".

docs.title: 3.4 System › Updates: pointer to kiosk updates
docs.text:
Under the existing Updates content, a SettingRow, only while behind.length > 0 (behind as defined in §3.1): - Label Kiosk software. Description {n} kiosk(s) can be updated to {v}. - Control: Open Kiosks (.btn). It routes to /settings?setting=kiosks-software.

It reads the same kiosks store, so it is never out of sync with §3.1. It doesn't update anything itself.

docs.title: 3.5 Registry and docs
docs.text:
• New destination kiosks-software: label Update kiosk software, path Kiosks / Kiosk software, category: "kiosks", section kiosks-list. Keywords: kiosk, agent, update, software, version, bundle, fleet.
  • Add keywords kiosk update, agent to maintenance-updates.
  • No subtitle changes (CLV-17's stay).
  • docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md "Kiosk agent self-update": the flow starts at "Settings → Kiosks → Kiosk software → Update all (or Update on one kiosk)". Mention the System pointer.

docs.title: 4. Container self-restart
docs.text:
Decision (owner, 2026-10-29): A, not built. Containers are restarted from Docker. In a container, System › Restart shows only Reload UI and the one-line Docker pointer (§3.3). Options B and C below are recorded for context and are out of build scope.

Background. CALVIN_HOST_CONTROL guards actions on the machine (reboot, systemd, the update script, display power). A container's self-exit touches only its own process, so it isn't host control. But it only works if Docker restarts the container, and Calvin can't check that from inside (no Docker socket, by design).

  • docker/docker-compose.yml:23 sets restart: unless-stopped, so compose installs come back.
  • The Unraid template (deploy/unraid/calvin.xml) sets no restart policy (<ExtraParams/> is empty), and its Overview tells users to restart from the Docker tab. A self-exit there could leave Calvin stopped until someone opens Unraid. (Unverified on a real Unraid box: confirm the policy dockerMan applies.)

Options

  • A. Don't build it (chosen). Containers keep restarting from Docker; §3.3 adds the one-line pointer. Restarts are rarely needed now: plugin installs are live and config is hot.
  • B. (Not built.) Build it behind its own opt-in. A separate setting CALVIN_SELF_RESTART=1, not a host-control exception. It defaults on only in docker/docker-compose.yml (next to restart: unless-stopped). The Unraid template gets it plus --restart=unless-stopped in ExtraParams. GET /api/system/environment adds capabilities.restart_self. POST /api/system/restart-backend in a container then returns 200 and, after the existing _BACKEND_RESTART_DELAY_SEC, sends SIGTERM to its own PID. Code placement: a new require_self_restart() beside require_host_control() in backend/app/utils/host_control.py, so the two guards read side by side and can't be confused. UI: the Restart Calvin server row (§3.3) shows when restart_self is true. Confirm message: Calvin restarts its container. Docker starts it again in a few seconds. If it doesn't come back, start it from Docker.
  • C. (Not built.) Build it with no opt-in. Not recommended: it silently strands Unraid installs that lack a restart policy.

docs.title: 5. Tests
docs.text:
Frontend (vitest) - Kiosks summary: hidden with no agent kiosks; each §3.1 state's copy; Update all calls triggerUpdate once per behind kiosk; one rejection shows the toast and the rest still run; singular and plural copy. - Kiosk card: each §3.2 state, including the python-vs-other error split from agentUpdateMessage and the fallback to "other" when the field is missing. The "needs OS update" span is gone. - System: restart rows follow capabilities.restart (true → shown, false → hidden, env null → shown); the new labels and confirm copy; the container pointer line appears only for docker. - System › Updates pointer appears only while a kiosk is behind and routes to kiosks-software. - Registry: kiosks-software resolves to the Kiosks category, and the destination id snapshot gains exactly one id.

Backend (pytest) - GET /api/kiosks includes agentUpdateMessage from the stored status.

docs.title: Keyboard layout picker on the keyboard itself (CLV-21)
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/clv-21/clv-21.html, PNGs mocks/clv-21/png/l1.png … l3.png. Frontend only. Amends the on-screen keyboard spec (2026-10-29-on-screen-keyboard.md §4, "Keyboard layouts").

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text: The layout setting (Settings › Screen & keyboard › Keyboard layout) sits behind the admin lock, and the {layout} key only exists when extra layouts are set. So on the lock screen, the setup screen and the sign-in dialog, you type a password on whatever layout the device guessed, with no way to change it. That's the one place a wrong layout hurts most.

docs.title: 2. Decision
docs.text:
The layout key is always on the keyboard, on every field, and it opens a layout picker. It isn't limited to lock screens: the problem is "I can't reach the setting", and that's true for any field until you're signed in. One consistent key is easier to learn than one that comes and goes.

  • Tap the layout key:
  • with extra layouts set → cycle (as today);
  • with no extras → open the picker.
  • Long-press the layout key (≥ 500ms), or tap the active-layout label on the space bar → always open the picker. The space-bar label makes the picker discoverable without knowing about long-press.
  • Independent of the app language, as before: the picker lists layouts, never UI languages.

docs.title: 3. The layout key and space bar
docs.text:
• {layout} is now in the bottom row of every letter layout (default, url, email), not only with extras: {numbers} {layout} {accents} {space} …. For url and email, it goes after {numbers}.
  • The label is the active layout's code (EN, SV, …), as today. aria-label: with extras, Switch keyboard layout, now {name}; without, Keyboard layout: {name}. Opens the list. aria-haspopup="true".
  • The space bar always shows the active layout's name (--ink-3, --fs-sm), not only with extras. That tells you on a lock screen which layout you're typing on. Tapping the space bar types a space; only a tap on the label text opens the picker. The label is its own button inside the key, at least 44×32px. aria-label: Change keyboard layout.

docs.title: 4. The picker (an in-keyboard layer)
docs.text:
The picker replaces the keyboard's rows inside the keyboard panel. It isn't a popover, so it never covers the field or the form, and the panel keeps its height (--osk-height is unchanged).

  • Heading row (--fs-md, --ink-2, left): Keyboard layout.
  • A grid of option buttons, 4 columns (2 at panel widths under 480px). Each option is ≥ 44px tall and uses the standard key style:
  • Default ({main name}): uses the layout set in Settings (or the device's suggestion). Shown first.
  • English, Svenska, Suomi, Norsk, Dansk, Deutsch, Français, each with its code in --font-data --ink-3 after the name (for example "Svenska SV").
  • The active choice uses the Shift-active style (color-mix(in srgb, var(--focus) 16%, var(--bg-2)), border-color: var(--focus)) and aria-pressed="true".
  • Bottom row: abc (back to letters without changing anything), right-aligned, function-key style.
  • Choosing an option switches immediately and returns to the letter layer. Focus and caret stay in the field (same pointerdown.prevent rule as all keys).
  • Panel under 260px tall (800×480 → 216px): heading 22px, the option codes are hidden, the first option reads Default ({main code}) (for example "Default (EN)"), and the bottom row is 44px. 8 options in 4 columns still fit at ≥ 44px each.
  • role="group", aria-label="Keyboard layout"; options are <button>s.

docs.title: 5. What the choice means
docs.text:
• Picking a named layout saves it on this device in localStorage["calvin-osk-device-layout"]. It is honoured even if it isn't the main or an extra layout. Today's code only accepts a stored layout that is in [main, ...extras] (useOnScreenKeyboard.js:156-160). Change that check to "any valid layout id".
  • Migration: the old localStorage["calvin-osk-layout"] key was written on every device by the previous watch(activeLetterLayout, …, { immediate: true }), so it is not evidence of a device choice. Do not read it (especially now that any valid id is honoured, which would pin every upgraded kiosk to its old main layout). Remove it on load; devices start from Settings again.
  • Default ({main name}) removes the device choice (removeItem), so the device follows Settings again.
  • Cycling with extras: the order is [main, ...extras]. If the active layout isn't in it (a device choice), the first tap goes to main.
  • Nothing is written to server config, so it works signed out (the lock screen, the setup screen and the sign-in dialog) and needs no admin.
  • Settings › Keyboard layout stays the default for devices that haven't chosen. Under it, a --fs-sm --ink-2 line, shown only on a device with its own choice: This screen uses {name}, chosen on the keyboard. with a text button Use default, which removes the device choice.

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• {layout} is present in the default, url and email layouts with no extras, and its label is the active code.
  • Tap with no extras opens the picker; tap with extras cycles; long-press (500ms, fake timers) opens the picker in both cases.
  • The space-bar label is always rendered; tapping the label opens the picker; tapping the rest of the key types a space.
  • Picker:
  • lists Default + 7 layouts in order, and the active one has aria-pressed;
  • choosing writes calvin-osk-device-layout and returns to letters; Default removes the key;
  • a pre-existing legacy calvin-osk-layout is ignored and removed, and does not pin the layout;
  • abc changes nothing;
  • focus stays in the input.
  • A stored layout outside [main, ...extras] is honoured; cycling from it goes to main.
  • It works while signed out (AuthLockScreen with the OSK visible): no config write is attempted.
  • Settings shows the "chosen on the keyboard" line only when the device has its own choice; Use default clears it.

docs.title: On-screen keyboard (OSK) for touch kiosks: UI spec
docs.text: Status: ready to build as its own issue. It goes with CLV-9 (admin auth) and should land with it or just after, because CLV-9's kiosk lock screen uses it. Mockups: mocks/osk/osk.html, with PNGs in mocks/osk/png/ (k1.png … k7.png). Real theme tokens. Where this doc and the mock disagree, this doc wins.

docs.title: 1. Why, and why this approach
docs.text:
People must be able to use Settings on the kiosk itself, including signing in. Kiosks have a touchscreen and no keyboard.

  • System keyboard: rejected. Calvin kiosks run Chromium on X11 (calvin-x.service → startx). The Pi's own keyboard, squeekboard, is Wayland-only, and even there Chromium often doesn't show it automatically. The X11 keyboards (onboard, matchbox-keyboard) are unreliable with Chromium. All of them would mean changes to the Pi image, and Calvin couldn't control them.
  • Still true after the Wayland research (docs/research/2026-10-29-kiosk-wayland.md on develop, calvin-98dq): that plan moves Pi 4/5 to Wayland + labwc and keeps Pi 3 on X11. So the fleet will run both stacks, and only an in-app keyboard behaves the same on both.
  • Chosen: an in-app keyboard built on simple-keyboard (MIT, framework-agnostic, actively maintained, currently 3.8.x). Pin an exact version that is at least two weeks old. Use it only as the renderer (layouts, layers, key events). Calvin owns when it shows, how text is inserted, and how it looks. Frontend only: no backend or Pi changes.

docs.title: 2. Pieces
docs.text: Piece Path What it is OnScreenKeyboard frontend/src/components/ui/OnScreenKeyboard.vue Teleported to body, mounted once in App.vue. Wraps simple-keyboard. useOnScreenKeyboard frontend/src/composables/useOnScreenKeyboard.js Global state: enabled, visible, target (the focused element), layout, height. Owns the focus listeners and text insertion. calvin-osk theme inside OnScreenKeyboard.vue (scoped + :deep) Replaces hg-theme-default. Don't import simple-keyboard's default theme CSS beyond its base layout rules. Setting Device › Keyboard: onScreenKeyboard config key 'auto' \| 'on' \| 'off', default 'auto'.

docs.title: 3. When it shows
docs.text:
Enabled when: - onScreenKeyboard === 'on', or - onScreenKeyboard === 'auto' and useTouchCapability().isTouch and viewport width ≥ 720px. Phones and tablets under 720px keep their own system keyboard.

Targets: a global focusin listener on document. The target is an <input> of type text, search, url, email, password or number (or one with no type), or a <textarea>, that is not readonly or disabled and has no data-osk="off" ancestor. Native pickers (time, date, color, range, checkboxes) never get it.

Show: on focus of a target. Also when an already-focused target is tapped again after the keyboard was hidden (a click on target). Never open on pointerdown: on touch the browser focuses the field with the mouse events it sends after touchend, and a keyboard that opened earlier has already moved the field out from under the finger, so it never gets focus (CLV-114). Hide: - the Hide key (calvin-q9m7): it records the dismissal for that field, so the rest of the same tap (touchend, then WebKit's compatibility mouse events) and later focus churn cannot reopen it. A fresh tap on the field, a refocus after the field has actually lost focus (Tab or programmatic focus), or the ⌨ Keyboard button clears the dismissal. Hiding moves the button under the finger, so the click that ends the Hide tap must not press it; that guard is the gesture that hid (a press is a new gesture), not a time window, so the button works again immediately; - a tap outside both the keyboard and its field (calvin-q9m7): hides and blurs the field. WebKit leaves a focused input focused when a non-focusable element is tapped, so no focusout arrives there; the tap is not prevented, so a real control under the finger still receives its click. A <label> of the focused field counts as that field, a drag or scroll is not a tap, and the tap's origin is kept long enough for its delayed compatibility click (cog/WPE adds a tap delay) before a drag can discard it; - focus moving to a non-target element or to nothing (wait one requestAnimationFrame before deciding, so focus jumping between two fields doesn't flicker); - route change; - Escape on a physical keyboard; - a trusted physical keypress in the target (event.isTrusted and not from the OSK). That means someone has a real keyboard, so stay hidden until the next focus.

Never steal focus. Set simple-keyboard's preventMouseDownDefault: true, plus @pointerdown.prevent on the keyboard root, so the input keeps focus and caret while keys are tapped.

No autofocus anywhere on touch (CLV-9 §6 stands). The keyboard appears only when someone taps a field.

docs.title: 4. Layouts
docs.text:
Five layouts. The layout is chosen from the target when it gets focus. Tokens in braces are function keys.

default (text, search, password, textarea)
q w e r t y u i o p {bksp}
a s d f g h j k l {enter}
{shift} z x c v b n m , . {shift}
{numbers} {accents} {space} - {hide}

url (type=url) and email (type=email; "@" replaces "/" and ":" is dropped)
q w e r t y u i o p {bksp}
a s d f g h j k l {enter}
{shift} z x c v b n m - _ {shift}
{numbers} / : {space} . .com {hide}          email: {numbers} @ {space} . .com {hide}

symbols ({numbers} from any letter layout)
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0 {bksp}
@ # $ % & * - + ( ) {enter}
{abc} ! " ' : ; / ? _ = {abc}
{abc} {space} . , {hide}

accents ({accents}; Shift gives capitals)
å ä ö æ ø é è ü ñ ß {bksp}
á à â ê ë í ï ó ô ú {enter}
{shift} ç õ œ ã ' ` ~ ^ ¨ {shift}
{abc} {space} . , {hide}

numeric (type=number, or inputmode=numeric/decimal), 4×4 grid, 440px wide, centred
1 2 3 {bksp}
4 5 6 -
7 8 9 .
{hide} 0 , {enter}

docs.title: Keyboard layouts (the letter layer)
docs.text:
The keyboard layout is independent of the app language. It is its own setting. It never follows, reads or changes the language Calvin's UI is shown in, and changing the UI language never touches it. The owner's own setup is an English UI with a Swedish keyboard, and that must take zero extra effort. Everywhere in UI copy and code it is called a layout (oskLayout), never a "language".

Only the letter layer (and its Shift capitals) changes with the layout. The symbols, accents and numeric layers are shared. Each layout keeps its letters where people expect them:

en  English   q w e r t y u i o p {bksp}        / a s d f g h j k l {enter}     / {shift} z x c v b n m , . {shift}
sv  Svenska   q w e r t y u i o p å {bksp}      / a s d f g h j k l ö ä {enter} / {shift} z x c v b n m , . - {shift}
fi  Suomi     same as sv
no  Norsk     q w e r t y u i o p å {bksp}      / a s d f g h j k l ø æ {enter} / {shift} z x c v b n m , . - {shift}
da  Dansk     q w e r t y u i o p å {bksp}      / a s d f g h j k l æ ø {enter} / {shift} z x c v b n m , . - {shift}
de  Deutsch   q w e r t z u i o p ü {bksp}      / a s d f g h j k l ö ä {enter} / {shift} y x c v b n m , . ß {shift}
fr  Français  a z e r t y u i o p {bksp}        / q s d f g h j k l m {enter}   / {shift} w x c v b n é è ç à {shift}

Bottom row: {numbers} {layout} {accents} {space} {hide}. For en it is {numbers} {layout} {accents} {space} - {hide}, and for fr it is {numbers} {layout} {accents} , {space} . {hide}. Amended by CLV-21: {layout} and the space-bar layout name are always present, and the key opens a layout picker. The url and email layouts use the active layout's first two rows unchanged. Their third row is the active layout's row-3 letters a–z only (accented letters and punctuation dropped), followed by - _, because hyphens and underscores are common in addresses. Their bottom row is their own (above):

en, sv, fi, no, da   {shift} z x c v b n m - _ {shift}
de                   {shift} y x c v b n m - _ {shift}
fr                   {shift} w x c v b n - _ {shift}
  • Layout key {layout}: label = the active layout's code in capitals (EN, SV, FI, NO, DA, DE, FR), width 1×, function-key style. aria-label = Switch keyboard layout, now {layout name}. Each tap moves to the next layout in the order: main layout, then the extra layouts in list order. Amended by CLV-21: without extras a tap opens the layout picker instead, and a long-press always does. The space bar always shows the active layout's name (--ink-3, --fs-sm, as in K6); its label opens the picker. Neither ever shows the UI language.
  • The active layout survives hiding and showing. An explicit choice is remembered per device in localStorage (calvin-osk-device-layout, wrapped in try/catch) and resets to the main layout if that entry stops being valid. Amended by CLV-21: a device choice is honoured even when it isn't the main or an extra layout, and the legacy calvin-osk-layout key is removed on load because older builds wrote it on every device.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
• Shift is one-shot: tap, type one capital, back to lowercase. Tapping Shift twice within 400ms locks caps until Shift is tapped again. Shift keys show k--on while active. Letter keys show capitals while Shift is active.
  • Backspace repeats when held: after a 500ms delay, every 60ms.
  • {numbers} = ?123, {abc} = abc, {accents} = åäö, .com types .com.
  • Space has no label.
  • Enter label: if the target is inside a <form> with a visible button[type=submit] (or the first .btn--primary / .security-btn--primary in it), use that button's text (for example Sign in, Set password). Otherwise Enter. On the numeric pad it is always Done.
  • Enter behaviour: dispatch keydown + keyup Enter on the target. If the keydown wasn't defaultPrevented and the target has a form, call form.requestSubmit(). For a <textarea>, insert \n. On numeric Done, also hide the keyboard. (Existing handlers like @keyup.enter="add" in SecuritySettings keep working.)

docs.title: 5. Text insertion
docs.text: Don't use simple-keyboard's internal input buffer (it loses the caret on mid-string edits). Handle onKeyPress(button) yourself: - Character: replace target.value.slice(selectionStart, selectionEnd) with the character, put the caret after it, then dispatch new Event('input', { bubbles: true }) so v-model updates. - {bksp}: delete the selection, or the code point before the caret ([...str]-aware, so å and emoji don't split). - type=number and type=email don't support selectionStart: treat them as append and delete-last. - Respect maxlength. - No key-preview bubbles (so keys aren't magnified over a password). The pressed state is the only feedback.

docs.title: 6. Layout and look
docs.text:
• Position: position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: 1100 (above dialogs at 1000 and the scrim at 999). Teleported to body, so it is not affected by the Settings --ui-scale zoom and is always the same physical size.
  • Height: min(300px, 45dvh). 4 rows at 1280×720 is 300px; at 800×480 it is 216px. Publish the live height as --osk-height on :root (0px when hidden).
  • Panel: background: var(--bg-0), border-top: 1px solid var(--line), box-shadow: 0 -10px 30px -18px var(--shadow-hover), padding: 10px 12px 12px, rows gap: 8px (6px and 8px padding when height < 260px).
  • Keys: min-height: 44px, rows share the height equally. background: var(--bg-2), border: 1px solid var(--line), border-radius: var(--radius-sm), box-shadow: 0 1px 0 var(--line), font: 400 1.25rem var(--font-ui) (1.05rem when height < 260px), color: var(--ink). In the light theme --bg-2 is white on a --bg-0 panel, so the keys read clearly (white-on-white is the trap to avoid).
  • Function keys: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 6%, var(--bg-0)), color: var(--ink-2), var(--fs-md) weight 500. Width 1.5×. Icons for Backspace, Shift and Hide are 22px stroke SVGs, and each has an aria-label (Backspace, Shift, Hide keyboard).
  • Enter: 2× wide, background: var(--focus), color: var(--focus-ink), weight 600.
  • Space: 6× wide.
  • Pressed: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--focus) 22%, var(--bg-2)), translateY(1px), no shadow.
  • Shift active / caps locked: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--focus) 16%, var(--bg-2)), border-color: var(--focus).
  • Motion: slide up transform: translateY(100%) → 0, 180ms ease-out. Hide 120ms ease-in. Under prefers-reduced-motion, no transition.

docs.title: Making room (every page)
docs.text:
• .settings-content (the scroll container) gets padding-bottom: var(--osk-height). After showing, scroll the target into view: target.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' }) within the visible area.
  • Fixed dialogs (AdminSignInDialog, ConfirmModal, InstanceModal, .settings-phone) centre within calc(100dvh - var(--osk-height)). Put this rule in a shared class, for example top: calc((100dvh - var(--osk-height)) / 2), and apply it to each.
  • Add nothing to the dashboard. It has no text fields, and dialogs over it follow the rule above.

docs.title: CLV-9 lock screen and dialog while the keyboard is up (K1, K3)
docs.text:
• The "or" seam and PhoneSetupCard are hidden. The auth card centres in the area above the keyboard.
  • When 100dvh - 64px - --osk-height < 320px (the 800×480 kiosk), the card also hides its icon, title, lead, recovery block and primary button, and shows only the field (and any error or 429 banner). Enter carries the submit label.
  • In the sign-in dialog the phone half is hidden and the dialog shrinks to its narrow form.

docs.title: 7. Settings (Device › Keyboard, K7)
docs.text:
Three new rows at the top of the Keyboard section, all SettingRows built from existing primitives:

  1. On-screen keyboard (SegmentedControl), config onScreenKeyboard: 'auto' (default) / 'on' / 'off'.
  2. Description Shows a keyboard on the screen when you tap a text field. Auto turns it on for touch screens.
  3. Options Auto / Always / Off.
  4. Keyboard layout (SelectPill), config oskLayout: unset (default) | en | sv | fi | no | da | de | fr.
  5. Description The letters the on-screen keyboard uses. Separate from the language Calvin is shown in.
  6. Options English, Svenska, Suomi, Norsk, Dansk, Deutsch, Français, each named in its own language, never translated.
  7. Default (unset): a one-time browser hint, never the UI language. The first time a device needs a layout, map navigator.language once (sv* → sv, fi* → fi, nb*/nn*/no* → no, da* → da, de* → de, fr* → fr, anything else → en) and cache the result in localStorage (calvin-osk-layout-hint), so it doesn't change later on that device. While unset, the pill shows that layout with the suffix (suggested), for example "Svenska (suggested)". Once someone picks a layout, oskLayout is saved and the hint is never used again. Calvin's UI language setting, if one is ever added, is never an input here.
  8. Also switch to (ChipMultiSelect), config oskExtraLayouts: string[], default [].
  9. Description Adds a key to the keyboard that switches between these and {main layout name}.
  10. Options: every layout except the current main one. When the main layout changes, drop it from the extras.
  11. The chips save in list order, and that list order is the switching order, so the existing component works unchanged.
  12. Rows 2 and 3 are dimmed and disabled while row 1 is Off. Settings remain editable from a phone either way.
  13. These are ordinary config keys, global like the other Device settings. Per-kiosk overrides are out of scope.

Add registry keywords: keyboard, on-screen, typing, osk, layout, keyboard layout, language, svenska, åäö. ("language" stays a search keyword only, so people who think of it that way still find it.)

Not covered here: the layout of a physical USB keyboard plugged into a kiosk. That is an OS setting (xkb, through the display agent) and would be its own issue.

docs.title: 8. Accessibility
docs.text:
• The keyboard root has role="group" and aria-label="On-screen keyboard", and every key is a <button type="button" tabindex="-1"> (it is a pointer input device, not a tab stop; a physical keyboard hides it anyway).
  • Typed characters reach the real input, so screen readers announce them the same way they would from a hardware keyboard.
  • Password fields: no previews, no logging of key presses (logDebug must not print key values).
  • Contrast: key text --ink on --bg-2 and Enter --focus-ink on --focus use the existing token pairs, which already meet AA in both themes.

docs.title: 9. Tests (vitest + @vue/test-utils)
docs.text:
• Focusing a text input when enabled shows the keyboard. A time input, a readonly input, or a data-osk="off" area doesn't.
  • auto on a non-touch or < 720px viewport → never shown. off → never shown. on → shown on desktop.
  • Insertion at the caret in the middle of a string, Backspace over a selection, å as one code point, maxlength respected, and input dispatched so v-model updates.
  • One-shot Shift resets after one letter; a double tap locks.
  • Enter: in a form → requestSubmit is called; with a @keyup.enter handler → the handler runs; the Enter label takes the form's primary button text.
  • A trusted physical keydown hides it. Blur to body hides it after rAF. Moving focus between two fields keeps it visible.
  • --osk-height is set on show and reset to 0px on hide.
  • Layout: sv puts å/ö/ä on the letter layer; Shift capitalises them. {layout} is absent with no extras, and with extras it cycles main → extras → main. The key and space-bar labels show the layout code and name. Unset oskLayout resolves once from navigator.language and caches it.
