Changing the UI language (or document.documentElement.lang) never changes the layout. Removing the active layout from Settings falls back to the main layout.

docs.title: One phone-setup prompt on the dashboard (CLV-20)
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/clv-20/clv-20.html, PNGs in mocks/clv-20/png/ (p1.png … p4.png). Frontend only.

docs.title: 1. Problem and recommendation
docs.text:
Today every empty region renders EmptyState (frontend/src/components/ui/EmptyState.vue), and on touch each one embeds its own PhoneSetupCard (EmptyState.vue:15). On the default dashboard, calendar and photos are both empty, so the screen shows two (or three) QR codes that say the same thing.

Recommendation: unify it, but not as one blocking overlay in every case. Two modes, chosen from what the screen shows:

  1. Welcome (first run): every content region on the screen is empty. One non-modal welcome card centred over the dashboard owns the phone hand-off: a short checklist of what's missing, one QR and Not now. Regions behind it shrink to one quiet "what's missing" line.
  2. Gaps (later): some regions have content. No card covers real content. Empty regions keep their normal empty state (message, help, button), but the QR appears once per screen, in the largest empty region, deep-linked to the missing thing when only one is missing.

Why not a single overlay always? Later, the screen is mostly working content. A card over it would hide the calendar to report one missing photo source. An in-region prompt says the same thing exactly where the gap is.

docs.title: 2. Definitions
docs.text:
• Content region: a region of the active dashboard screen whose kind is calendar, photos or service. Clock bar and plugin status items don't count.
  • Setup-empty: a region showing its setup empty state, meaning nothing is configured:
  • calendar: "No calendars yet" (CalendarView.vue:83)
  • photos: "No photos yet" (PhotoSlideshow.vue:63)
  • service: "No web services yet", renamed No web pages yet below (WebServiceViewer.vue:173)

Not setup-empty: loading, offline/stale, "service unavailable", or "no events this week". Those keep their own states and never trigger a prompt. - Mode: welcome when every content region on the active screen is setup-empty and the card hasn't been dismissed on this device (§5). gaps when at least one region is setup-empty otherwise. none when nothing is missing. - Phone hand-off shown = useTouchCapability().isTouch && viewport width ≥ 720px (the same rule as CLV-9's lock screen). Phones and laptops never see a QR: they can already type.

docs.title: 3. Architecture
docs.text:
• New composable useSetupPrompt() (frontend/src/composables/useSetupPrompt.js), module-level state:
  • report(regionKey, { kind, settingId, area }) / clear(regionKey), called by EmptyState when it renders a setup empty state (new prop setup: true on the three call sites above) and on unmount. area is the region's pixel area from a ResizeObserver on the EmptyState root.
  • contentRegionCount, set by LayoutManager from the active screen's layout.
  • Computed mode, missing (kinds in layout order), qrOwner (regionKey with the largest area, ties → first in layout order) and qrSettingId (the single missing kind's settingId, else null → /settings, which lands on Content since CLV-17).
  • New component SetupWelcomeCard.vue (frontend/src/components/dashboard/), mounted once in LayoutManager.vue and shown when mode === "welcome".
  • EmptyState changes:
  • showPhone becomes isTouchHandoff && mode === "gaps" && qrOwner === myKey, so the QR shows once per screen.
  • In welcome mode, render quiet (§4.3).
  • QR deep link = qrSettingId (not the region's own settingId), so it is correct when several are missing.
  • Fix while here: WebServiceViewer.vue:176-180 still says "No web services yet" / "Add a web service" / plugins-services from before CLV-17. It becomes No web pages yet / Add a web page / content-services, matching CLV-17's names. Its help line is already current and stays.

Settings ids: calendar content-calendars, photos content-images, service content-services.

docs.title: 4.1 Welcome card (mode welcome), P1, P3, P4
docs.text:
Container: position: absolute, centred in the dashboard area below the clock bar, z above the regions but no scrim, and not modal. The clock bar, ⋯ menu and keyboard shortcuts keep working. width: min(46rem, calc(100% - 32px)), padding: 1.75rem, background: var(--bg-1), border: 1px solid var(--line), border-radius: 16px, box-shadow: 0 18px 50px -16px var(--shadow-hover). role="region", aria-labelledby = its title. It takes no focus on appear.

Layout: a 2-column grid (1fr auto, gap 28px) when the phone hand-off is shown; otherwise 1 column.

Left column: - Title <h2> (--fs-xl, 600): Let's set up Calvin - Lead (0.95rem, --ink-2): - with hand-off: Add what this screen shows. Typing is easier on your phone. - without: Add what this screen shows. - Checklist (bordered list, --line 1px, radius 12px, rows ≥ 3.5rem, --line-soft dividers). One row per content kind present on this screen, in layout order: - Calendars / Photos / Web pages, each with the sub-line Not added yet (--fs-xs, --ink-3). - Button: Add here on a touch kiosk, Add elsewhere (.btn; on phone width the first row's button is .btn--primary). It routes to /settings?setting=<settingId> (the CLV-9 lock screen shows first if needed). - A kind that gets configured while the card is open: its row shows ✓ Added (--ok, --fs-sm) in place of the button. When all rows are added, the regions have content, so mode becomes none and the card fades out (200ms, none under reduced motion). - Not now (ghost button: no border, --ink-2), below the list. See §5.

Right column (only with the phone hand-off), 15rem wide: - QR 180px (white plate, 8px radius), for settingsLink(serverUrl, qrSettingId) (utils/serverUrl.js). - Set it up from your phone (600), hint Scan the code or open this address on the same network. (--fs-sm, --ink-2), then the URL (--font-data, 0.78rem, overflow-wrap: anywhere). - While auth.status === "setup" (no admin password yet, CLV-9): a line under a --line-soft rule, Your phone asks you to choose an admin password first. (--fs-xs, --ink-2). - Implement this column by extending PhoneSetupCard with a stacked variant (QR above text, no border, no background), not by copying it.

Fit rules (800×480, P3): when the dashboard area is under 520px tall, drop the lead, the sub-lines and the QR hint, use QR 132px, title Let's set up Calvin, and change the phone title to Or use your phone. padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem, gap: 18px, width: calc(100% - 24px).

Phone width (< 480px, P4): 1 column, docked at the bottom (bottom: 16px), no QR, buttons Add.

docs.title: 4.2 Gaps mode (P2)
docs.text:
• Each setup-empty region shows today's EmptyState: message, help and the action button.
  • Exactly one of them, the qrOwner, also shows the compact PhoneSetupCard (132px QR), with the hint shortened to Typing is easier there. and the URL for qrSettingId.
  • If the owner region is too small for the QR (the existing @container (max-height: 360px) rule hides it), the QR moves to the next-largest empty region that fits. If none fits, there is no QR, and the buttons still work.
  • No dismissal in this mode: it isn't intrusive and it disappears once the gap is filled.

docs.title: 4.3 Quiet region (behind the welcome card)
docs.text: EmptyState with quiet: only the message, in --ink-3, 1rem, weight 500. No help, no button, no QR. It stays legible around the card's edges, so the screen still says what's missing.

docs.title: 4.4 Interaction with other phone hand-offs
docs.text:
• Settings lock screen and AdminSignInDialog (CLV-9) keep their own QR. They are other surfaces (Settings, or a modal over the dashboard). When AdminSignInDialog is open over the dashboard, the welcome card stays under the scrim. No change there.
  • Settings › "📱 Use your phone" stays.
  • On-screen keyboard: the welcome card has no text fields, so it never brings up the keyboard. Add here opens Settings on the kiosk, where the OSK takes over.
  • Hidden controls (showUI off): the welcome card still shows (it is setup, not chrome), but its buttons are hidden and only the QR remains on touch. Without the hand-off it shows the checklist without buttons, plus the line Open Settings on a phone or computer to add these.

docs.title: 5. Dismissal and persistence
docs.text:
• Not now hides the welcome card on this device only: localStorage["calvin-setup-welcome-dismissed"] = "1" (try/catch; if storage fails, it hides for this page load only). It is per device because a wall kiosk and the phone that set it up shouldn't hide each other's prompts.
  • After dismissal, the screen behaves like gaps mode: the full empty states return, with one QR per screen. The setup path is never lost.
  • The flag clears itself when the device later sees mode none (everything configured), so a fresh empty screen (for example, after removing all sources) greets again.
  • Not per server, so nothing is written to config and no admin is needed. The dashboard is public (CLV-9 §3).

docs.title: 6. Accessibility
docs.text:
• The card is a landmark region, not a dialog: no focus trap and no autofocus. Tab reaches it in DOM order after the clock bar.
  • Checklist buttons have accessible names Add calendars, Add photos, Add web pages (visible text stays short).
  • The QR <img> has alt="QR code for {url}" (existing PhoneSetupCard behaviour), and the URL is selectable text.
  • ✓ Added changes are announced by an aria-live="polite" line: Calendars added.
  • Contrast uses existing token pairs in both themes. The QR keeps its white plate in Backlit.

docs.title: 7. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• useSetupPrompt:
  • welcome only when every content region on the screen reports setup-empty;
  • gaps with any content present;
  • none with nothing missing;
  • qrOwner is the largest area, ties go to layout order;
  • qrSettingId is the single missing settingId, or null with two or more.
  • EmptyState: renders quiet in welcome; exactly one QR across three empty regions in gaps; the QR is hidden on non-touch or < 720px; the QR moves to the next region when the owner is under 360px tall.
  • SetupWelcomeCard:
  • checklist rows follow the screen's kinds in layout order;
  • Add here vs Add by device;
  • the routes per settingId;
  • ✓ Added when a kind gets configured;
  • the admin-password line only while auth is setup;
  • the fit rules under 520px; the phone docking.
  • Dismissal:
  • Not now sets the flag and switches to gaps rendering;
  • the flag clears on mode none;
  • a storage exception hides for the page load only.
  • WebServiceViewer: the new copy and content-services deep link.
  • Loading, offline and "service unavailable" states never report setup-empty.

docs.title: Settings categories reorganisation: spec
docs.text:
Status: approved by the owner, ready to build as its own issue. Land it after the CLV-9 follow-ups and the keyboard-layout work (calvin-sjhb), because it moves the same Settings files. Mockup: mocks/settings-reorg/reorg.html (PNG: mocks/settings-reorg/png/r1.png).

Frontend only. No setting is added, removed or renamed in config. Sections move between categories; a few section titles and category labels change.

docs.title: 1. Why
docs.text:
• Display mixed four jobs: the physical screen (orientation, flip, rotation), layout (screens & regions), looks (theme, typeface) and touch controls. Its name also clashed with Device › "Display power", so "turn the screen off at night" had two plausible homes.
  • Adding a source happened in two places. Calendars and photos were added in Content Sources, but web pages were added under Plugins ("Add a web service") and ordered back in Content.
  • Device was a grab-bag. "Notifications" is the key-press feedback overlay (keyboard), and "Hardware" is only version numbers (they belong next to Updates).
  • Clock Bar was a whole category for three short sections.
  • 8 categories needed about 650px of rail height. 7 fit in about 560px.

docs.title: 2. The new categories (rail order)
docs.text:
Category ids are kept where a category survives, so stored state, deep links and tests keep working. Only clock-bar goes away.

# id Label Subtitle Icon 1 content Content Calendars · photos · web pages 📦 2 dashboard Dashboard Screens · clock bar · theme · touch 📐 3 device Screen & keyboard Orientation · power · keyboard 🖥️ 4 kiosks Kiosks Per-device settings 📺 5 plugins Plugins Install · manage 🔌 6 maintenance System Updates · backup · diagnostics ⚙️ 7 security Security Admin password · allowed origins · network access 🔒
  • defaultSettingsCategoryId becomes "content". A first visit lands where setup starts.
  • isKnownSettingsCategory gets an alias map { "clock-bar": "dashboard" }, so a stored settings_category or an old link with clock-bar opens Dashboard instead of falling back.

docs.title: 3. Section moves (exact)
docs.text:
Section ids (SettingsSection id=…) don't change. Only their parent category, their order, and in a few cases their title change.

Content (ContentSettings.vue), unchanged order, one retitle and one addition: 1. content-calendars Calendars 2. content-calendar-display Calendar display 3. content-photos Photos 4. content-images Image sources 5. content-services, retitled Web pages & services. Add a button Add a web page (.btn--primary style used elsewhere in Content) in the section header row, above ServicesTab. It opens the same flow the plugins-services destination opens today (the add-instance modal for the web-service plugin); reuse it, don't fork it. When there are no service instances, the section shows the existing empty-state pattern with that button.

Dashboard (DisplaySettings.vue, rename the file DashboardSettings.vue): 1. regions Screens & regions 2. clock-bar-clock, retitled Clock 3. clock-bar-layout, retitled Clock bar layout 4. clock-bar-items, retitled Clock bar items 5. appearance Appearance (Theme, Theme mode, Typeface, Settings UI size, Display name), unchanged 6. kiosk-touch, retitled Touch & controls (all of its rows stay, including Touchscreen and Dashboard size)

Move the three clock-bar sections' markup and logic out of ClockBarSettings.vue into a component ClockBarSections.vue rendered inside Dashboard. Delete the clock-bar category component and its v-if in Settings.vue.

Screen & keyboard (DeviceSettings.vue): 1. layout (from Display), retitled Screen orientation: Orientation, Flip 180°, Apply display rotation 2. device-power, retitled Screen power 3. device-keyboard Keyboard (on-screen keyboard, layout rows, keyboard type & mappings, reboot combo) 4. device-notifications, retitled Key-press feedback (same rows: Enable feedback, Feedback style, Auto-hide delay) 5. ~~device-hardware~~, which moves to System

Kiosks: unchanged.

Plugins (PluginsCategory.vue): sections unchanged (plugins-install, plugins-installed). Only the subtitle changes, and the plugins-services destination moves to Content (§4).

System (MaintenanceSettings.vue): 1. maintenance-updates Updates 2. device-hardware (from Device), retitled Versions & status: Backend version, Frontend version, System status 3. maintenance-system, retitled Restart 4. maintenance-backup, maintenance-restore, maintenance-auto-backup (BackupSettings), unchanged 5. maintenance-diagnostics Diagnostics

Security: unchanged (security-admin, security-sealed, security-origins).

docs.title: 4. Registry (settingsRegistry.js)
docs.text:
• Destination ids stay the same: QR codes, EmptyState buttons, search and the CLV-9 links (?setting=device-reboot, maintenance-updates, …) keep working.
  • Update category, path and tabKey for the moved destinations:
destination id new category new path dashboard-layout device Screen & keyboard / Screen orientation dashboard-regions dashboard Dashboard / Screens & regions dashboard-ui dashboard Dashboard / Appearance dashboard-kiosk dashboard Dashboard / Touch & controls clock-bar-appearance dashboard Dashboard / Clock clock-bar-items dashboard Dashboard / Clock bar items content-* content Content / … (path prefix "Content", not "Content Sources") plugins-services content Content / Web pages & services (tab: "content-services"), label Add a web page device-power device Screen & keyboard / Screen power device-keyboard, device-reboot device Screen & keyboard / Keyboard device-notifications device Screen & keyboard / Key-press feedback device-hardware maintenance System / Versions & status maintenance-* maintenance System / …
  • tabKey follows the new category (each category's existing key; the clock-bar key goes away).
  • Keywords: keep all existing ones, and add the old names so search still finds things by what people remember: "display" on Dashboard and Screen orientation, "clock bar" on the clock sections, "device" and "hardware" on Versions & status, "maintenance" on System, "notifications" on Key-press feedback, "content sources" on Content.

docs.title: 5. Copy that names categories
docs.text: Every user-facing string that names a Settings place must use the new names. Grep frontend/src for Content Sources, Clock Bar, Clock bar, Maintenance, Device ›, Display ›, Settings ›. One known case: the photos empty state says "Upload photos in Settings › Content Sources › Image sources." That becomes Upload photos in Settings › Content › Image sources. Update docs/ user guides that name categories in the same PR.

docs.title: 6. Layout and behaviour
docs.text:
• No visual change to the rail or sections beyond labels: same CategoryRail, SettingsSection and SettingRow. The measured rail scrolling from fix/settings-rail-overflow stays.
  • Scroll-spy (settingsSectionSpy) and the top-bar location label pick up the new titles automatically. Check that the eyebrow for Dashboard's clock sections reads "Clock", "Clock bar layout", "Clock bar items".
  • Phone width: unchanged (the rail stacks above the content).

docs.title: 7. Tests
docs.text:
• Registry: every destination's category exists; no destination points at clock-bar; the destination ids set is identical before and after (snapshot the id list); plugins-services resolves to Content.
  • isKnownSettingsCategory("clock-bar") resolves to dashboard; the default category is content.
  • Settings.vue: ?setting=device-reboot opens Screen & keyboard and scrolls to Keyboard; ?setting=device-hardware opens System › Versions & status; ?setting=clock-bar-items opens Dashboard.
  • Each category component renders its sections in the order in §3 (assert the section id order).
  • Search: "clock bar", "display", "maintenance" and "notifications" still return results.
  • Existing category specs (DisplaySettings.spec.js, ClockBarSettings.spec.js, DeviceSettings.spec.js, MaintenanceSettings.spec.js, ContentSettings.spec.js) move with their sections.

docs.title: API keys (CLV-32)
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/clv-32/clv-32.html, PNGs mocks/clv-32/png/a1.png … a3.png. Settings › Security. Copy follows the settings audit §5 (2026-10-30-settings-copy-audit.md). MCP is CLV-33 and out of scope here.

docs.title: 1. Placement
docs.text:
A new SettingsSection API keys (id="security-api-keys") in SecuritySettings.vue, right after Admin access and before Sealed mode: both are about who may act as admin.

  • Registry destination security-api-keys, label API keys. Keywords: "api", "api key", "token", "bearer", "home assistant", "script", "automation".
  • Security subtitle: Admin password · API keys · allowed sites.
  • Intro line under the title (--fs-sm, --ink-2): Let apps and scripts, like Home Assistant, use Calvin without the admin password. Give each one its own key.

docs.title: 2. Scopes
docs.text:
The three scopes are a ladder. Each one includes the one before:

Scope Label Description (verbatim) read Read See calendars, photos, settings and status. Can't change anything. admin Admin Everything Read can, plus change settings and content, like signing in as admin. host Host control Everything Admin can, plus restart Calvin, reboot this machine and install updates.

Backend note: the UI assumes host ⊇ admin ⊇ read. Host actions also stay behind CALVIN_HOST_CONTROL (require_host_control): a host key can't do more than the server allows. If the backend keeps host separate (host routes only), the Host control description becomes Only restart Calvin, reboot this machine and install updates. Nothing else changes.

Host control looks dangerous on purpose: - Its option card has a 1px --err border once selected, --err 6% tint, and a ⚠ before the label. - The description is followed by Anyone with this key can reboot the machine Calvin runs on. (--err, --fs-xs, 500). - Selecting it adds a required checkbox under the cards: I understand this key can reboot this machine. Create key stays disabled until it's ticked. Changing the scope away clears the tick. - Unavailable when GET /api/system/environment reports host_control: false (Docker, or the setting is off): - the card is disabled (opacity: .55, aria-disabled); - its description becomes Not available: this Calvin doesn't control its machine.; - it can't be selected. - While the environment is loading or unknown (null), the card stays enabled; the backend still refuses.

docs.title: 3.1 Empty (mock A1, left)
docs.text: EmptyState-style block inside the section (no QR): - No API keys yet. - Create one to let Home Assistant or a script read or change Calvin. - Button Create key (.btn--primary).

docs.title: 3.2 Create (mock A1, right)
docs.text:
Create key opens an inline form in the section (same pattern as Change password, not a modal: the OSK and phone layouts already work there). It replaces the button; the list stays below.

  • Name text field, required, max 40 characters, placeholder Home Assistant. Hint: So you know which app uses it. It must be unique (case-insensitive) among active keys. Error: You already have a key called {name}. Empty on submit: Give the key a name.
  • What it can do: a <fieldset> with that <legend>. Three radio cards in a row (stacked under 600px), each ≥ 44px tall, with label + description from §2. Default selection: Read.
  • The host checkbox (§2) when Host control is selected.
  • Buttons: Create key (.btn--primary) and Cancel (ghost). While saving: Creating…, disabled.
  • On a touch kiosk (isTouch and width ≥ 720), one hint line above the buttons: Easier on the computer where you'll paste it: the key is only shown once. It doesn't block anything.
  • Errors: a failed POST shows Couldn't create the key. Try again. under the buttons and keeps the form. A 401 opens the CLV-9 sign-in dialog, as everywhere.

docs.title: 3.3 Show once (mock A2)
docs.text: After a successful create, the form is replaced by a result panel. Border 1px --focus, radius 12px, padding 1.25rem: - Title Copy your key now (--fs-md, 600). - You won't be able to see it again. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one. (--fs-sm, --ink-2) - The secret is in a read-only <input> (--font-data, 0.95rem, full width, aria-label="New API key for {name}"). It selects all on focus and on tap. - Copy button beside it: - Clipboard API available (navigator.clipboard and a secure context): write the secret, then label ✓ Copied for 2s, announced via aria-live="polite": Key copied. - Otherwise (plain-HTTP LAN, the usual case): select the input and try document.execCommand("copy"). On success, the same ✓ Copied. On failure, the button reads Select and copy and the hint Press Ctrl+C (or long-press → Copy) to copy the selected key. shows. - A usage line (--fs-xs, --ink-2): Send it as Authorization: Bearer <key> (code style). - Done (.btn). It discards the secret from memory and returns to the list with the new key at the top. Leaving the section or Settings also discards it. The secret is never put in the store, localStorage, the URL or logs. - No QR code: a secret shouldn't sit on a wall screen as a scannable image.

docs.title: 3.4 List (mock A3)
docs.text: One row per active key, newest first, as SettingRows: - Label: the key's name, followed by a scope chip: - Read and Admin: --ink-2 text, 1px --line; - Host control: --err text, 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--err) 45%, var(--line)), ⚠ prefix. - Description: {prefix}… (--font-data, the first 8 characters the backend returns as prefix) · Created {date} · Last used {relative} or Never used. Date format: "30 Oct", with the year if not the current year. Relative times: "just now", "12 min ago", "3 h ago", "2 days ago", then the date. - Host key on a server without host control: the extra line Host actions are blocked: this Calvin doesn't control its machine. (--ink-3). - Action: Revoke (.btn, --err text). Phone: the row stacks (:stacked="isPhone"). - Below the rows: Create key (.btn) to open §3.2 again. - Load failure: Couldn't load API keys. + Try again. Loading: three 3.5rem skeleton rows.

docs.title: 3.5 Revoke (mock A3, dialog)
docs.text:
ConfirmModal: - title Revoke "{name}"? - message Apps using this key stop working right away. This can't be undone. - confirm Revoke key (.btn-danger), cancel Cancel.

On success, the row is removed and the live region says {name} revoked. On failure, the dialog closes and the row shows Couldn't revoke this key. Try again. (--err, --fs-xs).

docs.title: 4. Data contract (for the backend lane)
docs.text:
• GET /api/auth/keys → { keys: [{ id, name, scope, prefix, createdAt, lastUsedAt | null }] }. Never the secret or the hash.
  • POST /api/auth/keys { name, scope } → { key: {…same…}, secret }. The only time the secret is sent. 409 on a duplicate name, 422 for an unknown scope, 403 for host when host control is off.
  • DELETE /api/auth/keys/{id} → 204.
  • All three require an admin session (cookie), not a key: a key can't mint or revoke keys. Say so in the API docs; the UI needs no copy for it.
  • prefix = the first 8 characters of the secret (e.g. clv_7Hq2), stored in clear for identification.

docs.title: 5. Accessibility
docs.text:
• The scope cards are a native radio group in a fieldset/legend, with arrow-key navigation. Disabled Host control is announced with its reason (its description is the aria-describedby).
  • The host checkbox is a real <input type="checkbox"> with its label.
  • The result panel takes focus on its title (tabindex="-1") so screen readers announce Copy your key now.
  • Danger isn't colour-only: ⚠ and the explicit sentence carry it too.
  • Touch targets are ≥ 44px (cards, Copy, Revoke). The on-screen keyboard works in the Name field (it's a normal text input).

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• Empty state renders and Create key opens the form.
  • Form:
  • Name required, ≤ 40, and the duplicate-name error; default scope Read;
  • Host control shows the warning sentence and checkbox, and Create stays disabled until it's ticked;
  • switching scope clears the tick;
  • Host control is disabled with the "Not available" copy when the environment says host_control: false, and enabled when the environment is null.
  • Create success shows the show-once panel with the secret, and focus moves to its title. Done clears it: the secret is no longer in the DOM or component state, and the list has the new key first.
  • Copy: the clipboard path shows ✓ Copied and announces it; the execCommand fallback works; the double failure shows Select and copy and the Ctrl+C hint.
  • List: the scope chip for each scope; the prefix, created and last-used formats (including "Never used"); the blocked-host line.
  • Revoke: the confirm copy; confirm → DELETE, row removed, announced; failure → inline error.
  • A 401 on any call opens the sign-in dialog; a create failure keeps the form values.
  • No secret ever reaches localStorage, sessionStorage or the logger (spy on them).

docs.title: Chips, tags and page tabs
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/chips/chips.html, PNGs mocks/chips/png/t1.png, t2.png. Frontend only, no behaviour change.

docs.title: 1. What's wrong
docs.text:
There are about 20 hand-rolled chip/badge/pill styles. Together they use six radii (4px, --radius-sm, 11px, 12px, 20px, pill), font sizes from 0.62rem to 14px, and weights from 400 to 700: - event-detail__tag, api-keys__chip, tab-badge, sre-orient-badge, setting-scope-chip; - .chip in RegionInspector and in ScreenInspector; - instance-count-badge, pi-count, theme-badge-small, theme-selected-badge, pc-badge; - plugin-type-badge-small, plugin-installed-badge, kbt-conflict-badge, cvo-default-chip, screen-card__badge, …

Worst cases: 1. Editor page tabs (.sre-tab, mock T1 "before"): - a pill holding two lines ("Home" / "All screens"); - an orange square dot on every tab that means nothing; - the active state is only a white fill with a shadow on a near-white background; - + is a dashed circle; - two lines in a rounded pill look cramped and wobble in height. 2. Inspector headings as chips: Page settings and Region in "Home" use a bold, letter-spaced, uppercase pill as the heading (.chip.screen, .chip.region with --focus-glow). A heading shouldn't look like a tag. 3. Plugin type badges (plugin-type-badge-small.type-*) use hard-coded Material colours (#e3f2fd/#1976d2 …). They ignore the theme and break in Backlit. A type is not a status, so it shouldn't be coloured. 4. color: white / font-weight: bold literals (tab-badge, theme-selected-badge) instead of tokens. 5. The mono uppercase eyebrow inside cards ("PAGES SHOWN", "START PAGE" in the screen page) uses the same style as the section titles outside the cards, so the hierarchy flattens. 19 uppercase rules exist in settings alone.

docs.title: 2. One Tag component
docs.text:
frontend/src/components/ui/Tag.vue, a non-interactive label: <span class="tag" :class="[tone, {count}]">.

Prop Values Default tone neutral, ok, warn, err, focus neutral count boolean: tabular mono digits, min-width = height, centred false icon an mdi path, 12px, before the text none

Tokens first. Add a tag block to frontend/src/styles/theme.css (shared by both themes; only the colour tokens differ per theme):

--tag-height: 1.25rem;            /* 20px */
--tag-pad-x: var(--space-xs);
--tag-gap: var(--space-2xs);
--tag-radius: var(--radius-sm);
--tag-fs: var(--fs-2xs);
--tag-weight: 500;
--tag-tint: 10%;                  /* tone background mix */
--tag-edge: 35%;                  /* tone border mix */
--tag-ink: 75%;                   /* tone text mix toward --ink */

Tag.vue uses only these and the existing colour tokens (--ink-2, --line, --ok, --warn, --err, --focus, --ink, --font-ui, --font-data). It has no hex, rgb or px literals.

Base style (all tones): - display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--tag-gap); - height: var(--tag-height); padding: 0 var(--tag-pad-x); border-radius: var(--tag-radius); - font: var(--tag-weight) var(--tag-fs)/1 var(--font-ui), no uppercase, no letter-spacing; - white-space: nowrap.

Tones: - neutral: color: var(--ink-2), border: 1px solid var(--line), background: transparent. - ok / warn / err / focus: - color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--{tone}) var(--tag-ink), var(--ink)) (keeps ≥ 4.5:1 on --bg-1 in both themes); - background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--{tone}) var(--tag-tint), transparent); - border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--{tone}) var(--tag-edge), var(--line)). - count: font-family: var(--font-data), font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, min-width: var(--tag-height), justify-content: center, padding 0 var(--space-2xs).

Mapping (replace each with <Tag>; delete the old CSS):

Old New setting-scope-chip (This screen) Tag neutral pc-badge, plugin-type-badge-small.type-* (plugin kind) Tag neutral, plain kind words. No per-type colours plugin-installed-badge Tag ok Installed; .plugin-update-available → Tag warn Update api-keys__chip / --host Tag neutral / Tag err with ⚠ icon instance-count-badge, pi-count, tab-badge Tag count (active tab: tone focus) kbt-conflict-badge Tag count tone="warn" theme-badge-small Tag neutral event-detail__tag Tag neutral (it stays mono only if it's an id; otherwise UI font) sre-orient-badge Tag neutral screen-card__badge (warn text) Tag warn

Not tags (interactive; they keep their components): ChipMultiSelect toggle chips, SegmentedControl, filter rows, SelectPill. theme-selected-badge (✓ on a theme card) stays a round check, using --focus/--focus-ink tokens instead of white. ConnectionStatus and the settings top-bar save pill stay pills: they're status indicators with their own specs.

docs.title: 2.1 Token rule for the touched components
docs.text:
Every component this spec touches (the tag call sites, .sre-tab*, the inspector headings, ThemeSelector, PluginInstaller, PluginCard, TabNavigation, KeyBindingTile, CalendarViewOptions) leaves with: - no hex/rgb/hsl colour literals and no white/black (use --focus-ink, --ink, --bg-*); - no font-weight: bold (use 600) and no raw font-size in px/rem (use --fs-*); - radii only from --radius-* (or --tag-radius), spacing from --space-*.

Tab sizes use tokens too: add --tab-height: 2.75rem (= --touch-target) and --tab-indicator: 2px.

docs.title: 3. Editor page tabs (mock T1)
docs.text: Underline tabs, one line each: - The row is 44px tall, with border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line) across the context strip. Tabs scroll horizontally when they overflow, with fade masks at the ends. - A tab is a <button role="tab">: padding 0 12px, height 44px, no background, no border, no radius. - Name: --fs-sm, 500, --ink-2. - Where it shows, on the same line after 8px: --fs-xs, 400, --ink-3. Text is Kitchen, Hallway or All screens, or Not shown in --warn-mixed ink. Truncated with an ellipsis at 16ch; the full text is in title and in the accessible name: "Home, shown on Kitchen and Hallway". - Hover: name --ink. - Active: name --ink, 600; a 2px --focus bar on the bottom edge (inset 0 12px); aria-selected="true". - Dimmed (not on the previewed screen, #156 §3.4): 50% opacity, unchanged. - The orange square dot is removed. - + Page: a ghost text button at the end of the row: mdiPlus 16px + Page, --ink-2, height 44. Not a dashed circle. aria-label="Add page". - On phone (CLV-47 Phone class), the screens text drops; the name stays.

docs.title: 4. Inspector headings (mock T1)
docs.text:
Replace the chip-heading with a real heading: - Page selected: <h3> Page (--fs-md, 600, --ink), then on the same line --fs-sm --ink-3 · Home. - Region selected: <h3> Region + · in Home. - Clock bar selected: Clock bar + · on Home.

The .chip.screen / .chip.region CSS is deleted.

docs.title: 5. Eyebrows
docs.text: The mono uppercase eyebrow (--font-data, uppercase, letter-spaced) is only for section titles outside cards (the SettingsSection title, the editor's stage tag). Inside a card, sub-labels use the normal field-label style (--fs-sm, 600, --ink, sentence case): for example Pages shown, Start page on the screen page, and Shows, Calendar in the region inspector. Audit the 19 text-transform: uppercase rules under components/settings, keep only section titles and the stage tag, and convert the rest.

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• Tag: renders each tone's class, count sets mono and min-width, icon renders, no uppercase style.
  • Token lint (a vitest that reads the touched .vue files): no hex/rgb/hsl colour literals, no white/black, no font-weight: bold, and no px/rem font-size in their <style> blocks. Tag.vue uses only var(--tag-*) and colour tokens.
  • Page tabs: one line; active has aria-selected and the underline class; the screens text truncates with the full text in title; no .sre-tab-dot; + Page has its label; the phone class hides the screens text.
  • Inspector heading text per selection (Page · Home / Region · in Home / Clock bar · on Home).
  • Screen page sub-labels are not uppercase.

docs.title: Connection status on the dashboard
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/connection/connection.html, PNG mocks/connection/png/n1.png. Frontend only.

docs.title: 1. Today
docs.text:
• BarActionCluster.vue shows two indicators side by side:
  • ConnectionIndicator ("📡 Offline" / "⚠️ No Connection");
  • a status dot reading "Checking..." / "Healthy" / "Error", titled "Backend: …". When the server is down, both show at once.
  • The only explanation is a title tooltip ("Backend server unreachable. Using cached data."). Touch screens never show it.
  • navigator.onLine === false is reported as "No internet connection". But Calvin runs on the LAN: the screen is off the network, and the internet may be fine.
  • Nothing says how old the shown data is. lastBackendCheck already holds the last successful check, so the data for this exists.
  • One failed /api/health check (3s timeout, every 30s) flips the state, so a single slow response makes it flicker.
  • The cluster lives in the clock bar. With controls hidden and Keep the clock bar when hidden off, an offline wall screen shows no sign at all.

docs.title: 2. One indicator: ConnectionStatus.vue
docs.text:
It replaces ConnectionIndicator and the status dot in BarActionCluster. The "Healthy" dot is removed: when things work, nothing shows.

States (from connection store):

State Rule Shows OK backend reachable nothing Starting no check finished yet nothing for the first 5s; then Connecting… (--ink-2, no icon) Server unreachable 2 consecutive failed checks pill Can't reach Calvin · data from {time} Screen offline navigator.onLine === false pill No network · data from {time} (immediately, no debounce) Back the first success after an unreachable/offline state ✓ Connected (--ok) for 3s, then nothing
  • {time} = lastBackendCheck as HH:MM (12/24h per Time format). Not today → Tue 14:02. Older than 6 days → 12 Oct. With no successful check yet this load, the pill drops the "· data from" part.
  • Retry backoff after a failure: 5s, 10s, 30s, then every 30s (today: always 30s). Coming back from navigator.onLine false triggers an immediate check.

Look: pill, height 32px (28px on a vertical clock bar, which shows the icon only plus the time below it), padding 0 12px, --bg-1, 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn) 55%, var(--line)), --radius-pill. mdiCloudOffOutline (unreachable) or mdiLanDisconnect (offline) at 16px in --warn, then the text in --fs-sm --ink. It's --warn, not --err: a wall display shouldn't shout, and the data is still shown.

docs.title: 3. Tap to explain
docs.text:
The pill is a <button>. Tapping it opens a small popover anchored to it (20rem; --bg-1, 1px --line, radius 12px, shadow as the welcome card):

  • Unreachable:
  • Title Can't reach Calvin.
  • This screen is showing what it last got at {time}. It keeps trying on its own.
  • Check that the Calvin server is on and that this screen is on the same network.
  • Button Try now: runs checkBackend(), shows Checking… while it runs; on failure, Still can't reach it.
  • Offline:
  • Title This screen is offline.
  • It isn't connected to the network. Check its Wi-Fi or cable.
  • Showing what it last got at {time}.
  • Try now, as above.
  • The popover closes on Escape, an outside tap, or reconnecting (which then shows ✓ Connected). Targets ≥ 44px.

docs.title: 4. Where it shows
docs.text:
• In the clock bar, at the same spot as today's cluster.
  • When the clock bar isn't visible (hidden with the controls, or a page without one): a floating pill, fixed 16px from the bottom-left corner (top-left if the show-controls corner is bottom-left), only while not OK. It ignores Hide controls: this is status, not chrome (like the CLV-20 welcome card).
  • Settings keeps its own save-status pill and is out of scope.

docs.title: 5. Accessibility
docs.text:
• A visually hidden role="status" aria-live="polite" line announces changes: Can't reach Calvin. / This screen is offline. / Connected again.
  • The pill's name is its visible text. The popover is role="dialog" aria-labelledby its title; focus moves to Try now and returns to the pill on close.
  • Meaning isn't carried by colour alone: icon + words.
  • No words "backend", "healthy", "error" or "internet".

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• OK shows nothing; Starting shows nothing until 5s, then Connecting….
  • One failed check shows nothing; two show the unreachable pill with the time of the last success; backoff runs 5s, 10s, 30s, 30s.
  • offline event → offline pill immediately; online → immediate check.
  • Back → ✓ Connected for 3s, then nothing.
  • Time format: today HH:MM in 12h/24h; another day "Tue 14:02"; over 6 days "12 Oct"; no success yet → no "data from".
  • Popover: copy per state; Try now calls checkBackend and shows its outcome; Escape and outside tap close it; it closes on reconnect.
  • With the clock bar hidden, the floating pill shows only while not OK, and avoids the show-controls corner.
  • No "Healthy"/"Backend"/"No internet" text is rendered.

docs.title: Content and plugins: one place for every source
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/content-plugins/content-plugins.html, PNGs mocks/content-plugins/png/p1.png … p3.png. Frontend only, except §6. Same shape of fix as 2026-10-30-screens-and-kiosks-setup.md: give each thing one home.

docs.title: 1. The jobs, and how they go today
docs.text: Job Today Add a Google/iCal calendar Content › Calendars: its own inline form (Type, Name, URL). Plugins › the calendar plugin card only says Manage calendar sources Add Immich photos Content › Image sources has Add photos (upload) and a drag-to-order list, but no add. Go to Plugins › Installed › filter Image › Immich card › + Add {label} → modal Edit or remove that Immich source Plugins only. Content lists it but only lets you drag it Add a web page Content › Web pages: Add a web page opens the modal of the first enabled service plugin. With Mealie enabled first, that's Mealie's form (AddWebPageButton.vue: plugins.find(p => p.type === "service" && p.enabled)) Add Mealie recipes Plugins › Service › Mealie card › add. It then appears in Content › Web pages & services, drag only Weather in the clock bar Install/enable in Plugins, add it there, then Dashboard › Clock bar items to show its tile, plus Show plugin info on Install a plugin Plugins › Install: type a GitHub URL and branch, List Plugins, tick, install. Nothing is prefilled. A ⚠️ Server Restart Required box with sudo systemctl restart calvin-backend can still show, though installs are live

docs.title: 2. Findings
docs.text:
1. A source has two homes. Calendars are managed in Content. Photo sources and web pages are listed in Content but managed in Plugins. Every plugin card in Plugins also lists its own sources. So you look in two places, and each place has only half the actions.
  2. Three different add flows for the same idea: a custom calendar form, an "Add a web page" shortcut that picks an arbitrary service plugin (a real bug), and the plugin card's + Add for everything else.
  3. You add by plugin, but you think by what you want to see. "I want photos from Immich" means knowing that Immich is an image plugin, finding its card under a type filter, and adding there.
  4. Plugin-engine words reach the family: "Instance Name" (the modal's name field), the type badge image/service/backend, "Installed Plugins", "statusbar", "List Plugins".
  5. Installing assumes a developer.
  6. It's GitHub-URL first, with no default catalog.
  7. The restart notice contradicts live install (CLAUDE.md: "Install is live — no restart").
  8. "Local path" is a dev-mode option, so it's fine where it is.
  9. The ordering lists look like the main thing. In Content › Image sources and Web pages, the only control is a drag handle. That makes order look like the main setting, while add/edit/remove live elsewhere.

docs.title: 3.1 Content owns every source
docs.text:
Rule: a source (a plugin instance) is added, edited, turned on/off, ordered and removed only in Content. Plugins never lists sources.

Content sections become one per thing you see, in this order:

  1. Calendars: calendar sources + Calendar display (unchanged rows from the audit).
  2. Photos: photo sources (Local photos with Add photos upload, Immich, …) + the photo rows (Show each photo for, Fit photos, Shuffle, Photo frame when idle).
  3. Web pages & apps: every service source (iframe pages, Mealie, Home Assistant cards, …).
  4. Clock bar info: sources whose plugin only has a clock-bar tile (weather, …). The Dashboard › Clock bar items list stays as the show/hide and order control and links here for adding. (A service source with both a page and a tile lists under Web pages & apps, and its tile shows in Clock bar items.)

Every section has the same list (mock P1), built as one component, SourceList.vue, for all four: - A row per source: - drag handle (only where order matters: Photos rotation, Web pages & apps; not Calendars, which merge); - status dot (running / error / off), using the existing running field; - name, and under it {provider} · {summary}, e.g. "Immich · 2 albums", "Google Calendar · Family", using getInstanceSummary; - Calendars only: the colour swatch; - an enabled toggle; - Edit, which opens InstanceModal; - ⋯ (Remove, with confirm). - One Add … button per section: Add a calendar, Add photos from…, Add a web page or app, Add clock bar info. It opens the provider picker (§3.2). - Error state on a row: --err dot and the summary replaced with the plugin's error text (truncated to one line, full text in the Edit modal). - Empty section: the CLV-20 empty-state copy for that kind (unchanged), plus the Add button.

Calendars switch to the shared flow. The custom inline form (CalendarSourcesTab.vue) is replaced by the provider picker + InstanceModal (calendar plugins already declare instance_config_schema). The calendar-only row extra (colour) stays on the row; Show event times lives in the Edit dialog so every row keeps exactly one toggle. "Check for new events every" stays as the section's last row.

docs.title: 3.2 Provider picker
docs.text: A small dialog (DialogScrim + panel, 30rem, mock P1 right). Title: Add a calendar / Add photos from… / Add a web page or app / Add clock bar info. - One tile per enabled plugin of that kind: plugin name, its one-line description from metadata, and an icon if the plugin ships one (otherwise its first letter on --bg-0). Tiles are ≥ 56px tall. - Photos also lists Upload from this device first (opens the existing PhotoUpload picker). - Web pages lists the iframe plugin first as Web page (any address). - Installed but turned off: tile at 55% with Turn on (enables the plugin, then continues). - Footer link: Get more in Plugins › (opens Plugins › Install, filtered to that kind). - Exactly one candidate → skip the picker and open its InstanceModal straight away. This fixes the "Add a web page opens Mealie" bug by construction. - Choosing a tile opens InstanceModal for that plugin. On save, it closes and the new row is highlighted (--focus outline, 1.5s).

docs.title: 3.3 Plugins is about the add-ons themselves
docs.text:
Plugins keeps two sections: Installed and Install (Installed first: that's the common visit).

Installed (mock P2): one compact card per plugin, no source lists: - Name, a plain-word kind chip (Calendar, Photos, Web page & app, Clock bar, Theme, Background), and the version. - One line: Used by 2 sources (a link to that Content section, with the section's rows for this provider highlighted), Not used yet, or, for themes, Choose it in Dashboard › Appearance. - Enabled toggle. Turning off a plugin that has sources asks: Turn off {name}? Its {n} sources stop showing until you turn it back on. - Settings (only if the plugin has plugin-level settings), Update when one is available, Uninstall. Uninstall with sources: Uninstall {name}? Its {n} sources are removed too. (.btn-danger Uninstall). - The filter becomes the same plain kinds as the chips, with All first.

Install (mock P3): - From the Calvin catalog first: the official calvin-plugins repository is prefilled and listed on open (no URL to type), with search and kind filter. Each row: name, description, kind chip, Install / Installed ✓ / Update. - From another GitHub repository: a collapsed disclosure with today's URL + branch fields, List plugins. - Local path: unchanged, dev mode only. - After install, the row offers Add a source (opens the provider flow for that plugin in Content). - Remove the restart notice if the backend never sets requiresRestart for contract-1.0 installs (it's live). If there's a real remaining case (a failed live load), the copy becomes Calvin needs a restart to finish installing {name}. with the System › Restart link, and no shell command.

docs.title: 3.4 Words
docs.text:
• A plugin instance is a source everywhere. InstanceModal field Instance Name → Name, placeholder from the plugin's instance_label or e.g. Family photos. Modal title: Add {instance_label} / Edit {name}.
  • Type badges never show raw types. The mapping is calendar → Calendar, image → Photos, service → Web page & app (or Clock bar when it has only a statusbar schema), theme → Theme, backend → Background.
  • "Installed Plugins" → Installed. "List Plugins" → List plugins. "statusbar" never appears.

docs.title: 3.5 Clock bar
docs.text: Dashboard › Clock bar items stays the place to show, hide and order tiles. Its empty state (No installed plugins expose a clock bar tile.) becomes No clock bar info yet. + Add clock bar info (opens §3.2 for that kind, in Content). Show plugin info (the audit row) is removed: each tile already has its own toggle in Clock bar items, so the global switch only duplicates them.

docs.title: 3.6 Service sources: placed, not merged
docs.text:
Calendars and photos are feeds: every source merges into any calendar or photos region. A service source (web page, Mealie, Home Assistant…) is placed: it only shows once it's put in a region (service:{id} in the page editor). So adding one isn't enough on its own, and Content has to say where each one is placed.

  • Where it shows, on each Web pages & apps row, after the summary:
  • On Home, Week (page names, linking to the editor on that page);
  • or Not on any page yet + text button Put it on a page.
  • Put it on a page opens Pages & regions on the active page in place mode:
  • a banner Choose a region for Recipes;
  • tapping a region sets its content to this source (an empty region directly; a filled one asks Replace {current} with Recipes?);
  • Cancel leaves it unplaced.
  • After adding a service source, the new row is highlighted and shows Put it on a page as a .btn--primary, so the next step is obvious.
  • Clock-bar-only sources (a plugin with statusbar_schema and no display_schema) need no placing. On add, their tile is switched on in Clock bar items, and the row says In the clock bar or Hidden from the clock bar (with a link to Clock bar items).
  • A service with both a page and a tile: the row shows both, e.g. On Home · in the clock bar.
  • Background plugins (backend) have no sources. Their settings stay on their card in Plugins, which says Works in the background. No sources to add.
  • Remove on a placed source warns: Remove Recipes? It's on Home and Week; those regions become empty.

docs.title: 3.7 Installing from the picker (decision D)
docs.text:
Installing and managing add-ons stays in Plugins: updates, uninstall, turning off, other repositories, local path. Discovering an add-on is bridged into the picker, because "I want photos from Immich" shouldn't end at "go to another category":

  • The provider picker (§3.2) gets a second group, From the Calvin catalog. It lists catalog plugins of that kind that aren't installed: name, description, Install.
  • Install asks once: Install Immich? It adds an add-on to your Calvin server. You can remove it in Plugins. (Install / Cancel). It then shows progress in the tile (Installing…), and on success continues straight into that plugin's add form. On failure the tile shows the error and See details in Plugins ›.
  • Only the official catalog appears here. Other GitHub repositories and local paths are Plugins only: installing third-party code should be a deliberate visit.
  • If the catalog can't be reached, the group is simply absent; Get more in Plugins › stays.

docs.title: 4. Owner decisions
docs.text:
Approved 2026-10-30: A, B, C and D.

  • A. Sources live only in Content (Plugins shows "Used by n sources" links, not the lists). Recommended.
  • B. Calendars use the shared add/edit flow (retire the custom form). Recommended: one flow to learn and maintain.
  • C. Remove "Show plugin info" in favour of the per-tile toggles. Recommended.
  • D. Install official-catalog plugins from the Content picker (§3.7); management stays in Plugins. Recommended.

docs.title: 5. Phasing
docs.text:
1. Bug + words (no decision needed): fix AddWebPageButton to open the provider picker (or the iframe plugin when it's the only one); "Instance Name" → "Name"; plain kind chips; the restart notice check.
  2. Content owns sources (A, B): SourceList + the provider picker in all four sections, placement lines and place mode (§3.6); Plugins cards slimmed.
  3. Install catalog-first, the clock bar change (C) and catalog install from the picker (D, §3.7).

docs.title: 6. Data needed
docs.text:
• The plugin catalog: the backend already enumerates a GitHub repo (List Plugins). Phase 3 needs a default repo setting (pluginCatalogRepo, default the official repo) and the frontend calling enumerate on open. No new endpoint.
  • Optional plugin icon: PluginMetadata.icon (a file in the plugin's frontend/ or an emoji string). If it's absent, the UI uses the first letter. It's a contract addition, so it's optional and has no loader change beyond passing it through.

docs.title: 7. Tests (vitest), phases 1–2
docs.text:
• Add a web page:
  • with iframe + Mealie enabled, the picker lists both and the iframe one is first;
  • with only iframe, its modal opens directly;
  • it never opens a non-iframe plugin's modal without a choice.
  • SourceList, for each kind:
  • rows show the provider · summary, the status dot, the toggle, Edit and Remove;
  • drag only on Photos and Web pages & apps;
  • the calendar row keeps its colour, with exactly one toggle (Show event times is in Edit);
  • the error row shows the plugin error;
  • empty uses the CLV-20 copy plus Add.
  • Provider picker:
  • lists the enabled plugins of the kind, plus Upload for Photos;
  • a disabled plugin offers Turn on;
  • a single candidate skips the picker;
  • "Get more in Plugins ›" deep-links with the kind filter.
  • Plugins card:
  • no source lists;
  • "Used by n sources" links to the Content section with highlight;
  • the turn-off and uninstall confirms include the source count;
  • themes link to Appearance.
  • Service placement: rows show the page names or Put it on a page; place mode sets the region content, asks before replacing, and Cancel changes nothing; a clock-bar-only add switches its tile on; Remove warns with the page names.
  • Words: no "Instance", raw type badge or "statusbar" text in Settings.

docs.title: Default is a screen
docs.text: Status: spec (owner agreed 2026-10-30). Frontend only. Follow-up to 2026-10-30-screens-and-kiosks-setup.md (built in #165).

docs.title: 1. Decision
docs.text: The All screens card and the loose All screens · Display / Power / Touch & keyboard sections go away. In their place is a Default screen, edited on the same page as any other screen. - Screens follow Default for every setting they haven't changed (live, as today; not copied at creation). - A new screen follows Default from the moment it connects, so it picks up whatever Default says now. - Any browser that isn't a set-up screen (a phone, a laptop) also uses Default.

docs.title: 2. Screens category
docs.text: Only the list remains (plus Kiosk software and + Add a screen, unchanged): - Default card first, solid border, no online dot: - title Default; - line 1: Used by new screens and by browsers that aren't set up as a screen; - line 2: Landscape · off 23:00–06:30 · keyboard Auto, plus · 2 screens have their own settings when any do (a count of screens with ≥ 1 override, not of settings). - Then one card per screen, as today, with an extra line when it has overrides: 3 settings changed. - This browser card, last, only on a browser that isn't a set-up screen (!getKioskId()): - title This browser; - line {n} settings just for this browser or Same as Default. It replaces the This screen chip rows that sat in the All screens sections.

docs.title: 3. The Default page
docs.text: The same component and sections as a screen page (#165), opened from the Default card: - Pages: which pages browsers and new screens show, and the start page (the global availableScreens / defaultScreenId). Edit pages opens the editor previewing Any browser. - Display, Power, Touch & keyboard: today's All-screens rows, unchanged. - Default-only rows, with no per-screen override, marked by a --fs-xs --ink-3 line Applies to every screen: Timezone, Reboot button combo, Keyboard layout (each device can still pick its own layout on the keyboard, CLV-21), Also switch to. - No Software section, no status header, and no reset links (it is the default). - Screen now (turn this screen on/off now) leaves the Default page and the Screens list. The server's own display control moves to System › Restart as This server's screen with Turn off · Turn on: it calls /system/display/power/*, which drives the server's own display, so it is shown only when /system/environment reports capabilities.reboot (host control) and the deployment has a display. Each kiosk's own page instead gets a Screen now row (calvin-ydzz): Turn on now · Turn off now writes a screenNow override for that kiosk as { power, setAt }. The display agent ends it at the first schedule boundary after setAt, computed in the screen's own timezone; Follow schedule removes it.

docs.title: 4. A screen page
docs.text:
• Per row: Same as Default (--ink-3), or Changed here (--ink, 600) · Reset to default (text button; removes that override). This replaces "Same as all screens" / "Only this screen" / "Use the shared setting".
  • Page footer, when the screen has any override:
  • Reset everything to default (.btn). Confirm: Reset Hallway to the default? / Its 3 changed settings go back to the default. Its name stays. / Reset / Cancel. Removes every override key except displayName.
  • Use these as the default (.btn, ghost). Confirm: Make Hallway's settings the default? / Default and every screen that follows it will use Hallway's {list of changed settings}. / Make default. It writes the override values into the global config, then removes them from Hallway (it now matches Default). Name and pages are not copied.

docs.title: 5. Editing Default when screens differ
docs.text:
When a Default row changes and some screens override that same key, an inline note appears under the row for 10s (and until dismissed): - Hallway keeps its own Orientation., or with several, Hallway and Kitchen keep their own Orientation.; - text button Change them too, which removes that key's override on those screens.

No note when no screen overrides the key.

docs.title: 6. This browser page
docs.text:
Opened from the This browser card. Only the per-browser rows (the settings audit §2 and CLV-27 storage): - Touchscreen; - On-screen keyboard (with the CLV-27 learned state and Show it again); - Settings text size, which is listed here too (its row stays in Dashboard, where it's found by size).

Each uses Same as Default / Changed here · Reset to default like a screen.

docs.title: 7. Words
docs.text: "All screens", "Same as all screens", "Only this screen" and "Use the shared setting" are gone. The words are Default, Same as Default, Changed here and Reset to default. Search keywords for the Default page: "all screens", "default", "shared".

docs.title: 8. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• The Screens list shows Default first with the override summary, screen cards with "{n} settings changed", and This browser only without a kiosk id.
  • The Default page has the screen-page sections; default-only rows show "Applies to every screen"; no Software or reset links; Edit pages previews Any browser.
  • Screen page: "Same as Default" / "Changed here · Reset to default"; Reset everything removes all overrides except displayName after the confirm.
  • Use these as the default: writes the overridden values globally, clears them on that screen, leaves name and pages alone.
  • Editing a Default key that screens override shows the note with their names; Change them too removes those overrides; no note when nobody overrides it.
  • Screen now is gone from the Default page; each kiosk page's Screen now writes a screenNow override { power, setAt }. The agent ends it at the first schedule boundary after setAt (its own clock and zone), and Follow schedule removes it. The server's own display control appears in System only with host control; it calls /system/display/power/*.
  • Old deep links to the All-screens destinations (device-power, device-keyboard, layout) open the Default page at that section.

docs.title: Display settings: household, source or region
docs.text:
Status: spec (owner agreed 2026-10-30). Frontend only. Every display setting gets exactly one home, picked by what it describes:

It describes… Home Examples the household / locale Content, global week starts on, weekend days, time format, holidays one source that source's row (Content) colour, show times, address, refresh how one region looks that region, in Pages & regions (and on-dashboard controls) calendar view, week numbers, events per day, photo fit

No setting lives in two places. Region settings have no global default layer.

docs.title: 1. Calendar
docs.text:
• Content › Calendar basics (renamed from Calendar display) keeps: Week starts on, Weekend days, Time format, Highlight holidays.
  • Content › Calendars gets a Where calendars show list (§5) instead of a bare pointer.
  • Removed from Content: Show week numbers, Events per day.
  • Region inspector, calendar section, after Weeks ahead:
  • Week numbers: ToggleSwitch, writes view.weekNumbers (already read by CalendarView.vue).
  • Events per day: SelectPill Auto · 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 6 · 8, writes view.maxVisibleEvents (null = Auto). Auto fits as many event rows as the day cell's measured height allows (row height from the rendered chip; at least 1), and shows "+N more" for the rest.
  • On the dashboard: the calendar's existing view controls (calendar-header__controls) get a ⋯ with Week numbers on/off. Events per day stays in the editor (it's set once, not toggled).

Upgrade: on first load after the change, every calendar region without its own view.weekNumbers / view.maxVisibleEvents gets today's global showWeekNumbers / maxVisibleEvents. Do it once (flag displaySettingsMigrated: true in config), then stop reading the global keys.

docs.title: 2.1 Smart fit isn't built yet
docs.text: PhotoSlideshow.vue "smart" never measures the region. It assumes every photo region is a ~30% side panel (containerAspect hardcoded to 0.59 landscape / 1.7 portrait). In a full-width region, or in photo-frame fullscreen on a landscape screen (aspect ~1.78), nearly every photo compares as "wider than 0.59" and gets cover. A portrait photo then shows as a cropped band. Also, Fill and Crop both render object-fit: cover, so they are the same option.

docs.title: 2.2 Smart, for real
docs.text:
• Measure the photo area with a ResizeObserver: containerAspect = width / height, updated on resize and when entering or leaving fullscreen / photo frame.
  • Per photo, with r = imageAspect / containerAspect:
  • 0.8 ≤ r ≤ 1.25 → fill (cover): at most ~20% is cropped;
  • otherwise → whole photo (contain) over a blurred backdrop: the same image, object-fit: cover, filter: blur(28px) brightness(.55), scaled 1.1 to hide blur edges, aria-hidden. No black bars.
  • image.width/height missing → load the image and use its naturalWidth/naturalHeight. Until then, show it contain.
  • Reduced data: the backdrop reuses the loaded image (no second request).

docs.title: 2.3 Where Fit lives
docs.text:
• Fit photos moves to the region inspector, photos section: SelectPill Smart · Whole photo · Fill · Centre (Crop removed; it was Fill). It writes view.fit; missing = Smart. Whole photo also gets the blurred backdrop.
  • Photo frame (fullscreen when idle) always uses Smart: it's a different shape from any region.
  • Stays in Content › Photos (they're about the collection's rhythm, and photo frame uses them too): Show each photo for, Shuffle photos, Photo frame when idle, Start after.
  • Upgrade: copy the global imageDisplayMode into each photos region's view.fit once (same flag). crop → fill.

docs.title: 3. Content stays the hub (§5 applies to every kind)
docs.text: Content loses three rows (week numbers, events per day, photo fit) and gains a view of where each kind shows. Content answers "what Calvin shows, and where"; the editor answers "how this region looks". So Content isn't downgraded: it becomes the place you start, and every look setting is one tap away from it.

docs.title: 4. Web pages & apps, and the clock bar
docs.text: No moves. When tapped is already per region. Address, zoom and refresh are per source. The clock bar's show and position are already per page, and its look stays global.

docs.title: 5. "Where it shows" in each Content section
docs.text: Under the source list of Calendars, Photos and Web pages & apps, a compact list headed Where {kind} show (--fs-sm, 600): - One line per region of that kind, across all pages: {page} · {region label}, then a summary of its look in --ink-2: - Calendars: Month · week numbers · Auto events / Agenda, 7 days; - Photos: Smart fit; - Web pages & apps: the source name. It also lists which sources the region shows when it doesn't show all of them: Family, School. - Each line is a button (≥ 44px) that opens Pages & regions on that page with that region selected. - None: Not on any page yet. + Put it on a page (the place mode from the content & plugins spec §3.6). - For Web pages & apps, this replaces nothing: the per-row placement line (content & plugins §3.6) stays, and this list is the region view of the same thing.

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• Content › Calendar basics has no week-number or events-per-day rows.
  • Where it shows: one line per region of the kind with its look summary and source filter; a tap opens the editor with that region selected; none → Put it on a page.
  • The region inspector writes view.weekNumbers and view.maxVisibleEvents. Auto fits the rows to the cell height (mock height → count) and shows "+N more".
  • The on-dashboard ⋯ toggles week numbers for that region only.
  • Migration copies the globals into regions without their own values, runs once (flag), and maps crop → fill.
  • Smart fit:
  • a 16:9 container with a 3:2 photo → fill;
  • a 16:9 container with a 2:3 photo → contain plus backdrop;
  • a 9:16 container with a 16:9 photo → contain plus backdrop;
  • a resize recomputes it;
  • missing dimensions fall back to naturalWidth/Height.
  • Fit options: no Crop; Whole photo renders the backdrop; photo frame uses Smart whatever the region's fit is.

docs.title: Pages & regions editor on phones and small kiosks
docs.text: Status: spec (no mockup yet). Frontend only. ScreenRegionEditor.vue has no responsive rules: the preview is fixed at 560px (DEVICE_MAX), the inspector rail is 340px, and moving the clock bar uses HTML5 drag, which touch doesn't trigger. On a phone (~390px), the screen we recommend for setup, and on the 800×480 kiosk, the editor overflows.

docs.title: 1. Size classes
docs.text:
Measured on the modal with a ResizeObserver (not media queries, so a kiosk with the OSK open counts too):

Class When Layout Wide width ≥ 1024 and height ≥ 640 Today's layout, plus the fitted device (§2) Compact otherwise, and width ≥ 600 Modal full-screen (inset: 0, radius 0); rail 280px; header subtitle hidden; the orientation badge moves under the device as a caption Phone width < 600 One column: header, page tabs, Preview on, stage, inspector sheet (§3)

docs.title: 2. The device fits the stage
docs.text: Replace DEVICE_MAX with a fit: device = the largest box of the screen's aspect ratio that fits the stage minus a 16px padding (and minus the stage tag/caption). Minimum 200px on the long side. Region labels shrink with --fs-xs under 320px.

docs.title: 3. Phone
docs.text:
• Header: Pages & regions + ×.
  • Page tabs: one horizontally scrolling row (each tab ≥ 44px tall), with + at the end.
  • Preview on: a full-width row under the tabs.
  • Stage: fills the width; the device is fitted (§2). The mismatch banner stacks its button under the text.
  • Inspector sheet, at the bottom over the stage:
  • Peek: 64px, showing the selection, Page · Home or Region · Calendar, plus a ⌃ chevron.
  • Open: 65% of the height, with a drag handle and the inspector content scrolling inside. The stage refits into the remaining height, so the selected region stays visible.
  • Selecting a region opens the sheet. Tapping the peek toggles it. Dragging the handle down, or tapping the stage's empty area, closes it to peek.
  • 200ms slide; none under reduced motion.
  • role="region", aria-label="Inspector"; the chevron is a button labelled Show settings / Hide settings.

docs.title: 4. Touch
docs.text:
• Dividers (.sre-resizer, RegionNode handles): on a coarse pointer, the hit area grows to 28px across, with a visible 4×34px grip centred in it. Pointer events already work with touch.
  • Clock bar: on a coarse pointer, or in Compact/Phone, it isn't draggable and shows no drop zones. Tapping it selects Clock bar in the inspector, where Position (already in ScreenInspector) moves it. The tooltip "Drag to reposition the clock bar" changes to Tap to change the clock bar.

docs.title: 5. On-screen keyboard
docs.text: The modal gets dialog-above-osk, so on a kiosk with the OSK open it shrinks to the space above the keyboard and the size class re-evaluates (usually to Compact). The page-name field stays in view (scrollIntoView on focus, block: "nearest").

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• The size class comes from the modal size: 1280×720 Wide, 800×480 Compact, 390×844 Phone; the OSK height moves a kiosk from Wide to Compact.
  • Device fit: the aspect ratio is kept, and it never overflows the stage at 390, 800 or 1280 widths; minimum 200px.
  • Phone sheet: peek shows the selection; selecting a region opens it; the chevron toggles it; tapping empty stage closes it; reduced motion has no transition.
  • Coarse pointer: the clock bar isn't draggable, a tap selects it, and Position moves it; the divider hit area is 28px.
  • dialog-above-osk is applied.

docs.title: On-screen keyboard: off switch and hardware-keyboard auto (CLV-27)
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/clv-27/clv-27.html, PNGs mocks/clv-27/png/k1.png (K1) and k2.png (K2 + K3). Frontend only, using the existing kiosk overrides API (no backend or agent change). Amends the on-screen keyboard spec (2026-10-29-on-screen-keyboard.md §3) and uses the This screen scope from the settings audit (docs/design/2026-10-30-settings-copy-audit.md §2, PR #150).

docs.title: 1. Decision
docs.text:
• One setting per screen: Auto · On · Off. It is the existing onScreenKeyboard key, now scoped to the screen.
  • Auto learns from typing. On a touchscreen, the keyboard shows until someone types a real character on a physical keyboard. After that it stays hidden on that screen until someone asks for it again.
  • There is always a way back. On any touchscreen, when a text field is focused and the keyboard is hidden for any reason (Off, learned, or hidden with ⌄), a ⌨ Keyboard button shows. Tapping it opens the keyboard. This matters most on the admin password screen, where you can't reach Settings without typing.

docs.title: 2. Detection signal
docs.text:
Use the browser: a trusted, printable key press in a text field. Don't use the kiosk agent, and don't use navigator.keyboard.

A key press counts as physical typing when all of these hold: - event.isTrusted: the OSK dispatches synthetic events (isTrusted === false), so it never counts; - the target is an OSK target field (isOskTarget); - event.key is one printable character (key.length === 1, not a space) and no Ctrl, Alt or Meta is held.

That excludes what a remote or button box sends (arrows, Enter, Escape, media and F-keys), so Calvin's button bindings never switch the keyboard off.

Why not the agent (/proc/bus/input/devices)? - Many USB remotes, air-mice and HDMI-CEC bridges register as full keyboards. evdev can't tell them apart from a real one, so Auto would wrongly hide the keyboard on remote-driven kiosks. - It only covers Pi kiosks running the agent, not laptops or tablets. - Unplug detection needs polling, an agent update, a new API and a fleet rollout, and it still has the remote problem.

Typing is the one signal that proves someone here types on a keyboard, which is the question Auto asks. It can't see an unplug, so the way back (§4) also clears what Auto learned.

navigator.keyboard only offers layout maps and lock. It has no "is a keyboard connected" signal.

docs.title: 3. Behaviour by mode
docs.text:
Mode Focus a text field (touchscreen) Physical typing ⌨ Keyboard button Auto (default) Shows the keyboard, unless this screen has learned a hardware keyboard Hides it now and learns: localStorage["calvin-osk-hardware-seen"] = "1" Shown while hidden. Tap → keyboard opens and the learned flag is removed On Always shows Hides it for this field only (today's behaviour). Doesn't learn Shown after ⌄ or typing hid it Off Never shows by itself — Shown. Tap → keyboard opens for this field only. The mode stays Off
  • Auto on a non-touch screen (or narrower than 720px) never shows the keyboard and never shows the button, as today. On and Off keep their meaning everywhere.
  • The learned flag is per browser and is always stored in localStorage (try/catch; if storage fails, it lasts for the page load). It is learned while signed out, so it must not need the admin.
  • Physical typing while the keyboard is open hides it within the same keydown, and the typed character still lands in the field (don't call preventDefault).

docs.title: 4. The ⌨ Keyboard button
docs.text:
• When: touchscreen (isTouch), an OSK target field has focus, and the keyboard isn't visible. It hides on blur and when the keyboard opens. It is never shown on non-touch screens: they have a keyboard.
  • Where: position: fixed, right: 16px, bottom: 16px (plus env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). z-index: 1100, the OSK panel's layer, above dialogs and their scrim at 1000 (AdminSignInDialog, ConfirmModal).
  • Look: a pill, height 48px, padding 0 16px, --bg-1, 1px --line, --radius-md, box-shadow: 0 6px 18px -8px var(--shadow-hover). mdiKeyboardOutline 20px --ink-2 + Keyboard (--fs-sm, 500, --ink).
  • Behaviour: pointerdown.prevent (focus and caret stay in the field, like every OSK key). Tap → show the OSK for the focused field (in Auto, also remove calvin-osk-hardware-seen). <button type="button" aria-label="Show on-screen keyboard">.
  • Appear: 120ms fade, none under reduced motion. No auto-hide timer.
  • Fields inside [data-osk="off"] get no button either.

docs.title: 5. Admin password screen (lock, setup, sign-in dialog)
docs.text: No special case: the rules above apply. In practice: - Learned/Off → focusing the password field shows ⌨ Keyboard bottom-right (mock K1). One tap opens the keyboard, and the CLV-21 layout key and picker are inside it as usual. - Someone typing on a hardware keyboard never sees the OSK, which is the point. - The layout picker only affects the on-screen keyboard. A hardware keyboard types with the kiosk OS's keymap. CLV-27 doesn't change that, and no copy on these screens mentions it.

docs.title: 6. The setting
docs.text:
Screen & keyboard › On-screen keyboard (section name from the audit, §3.3). It stays next to its layout rows, not in Dashboard › Touch & focus: one place for everything about that keyboard. Search keywords add "hardware keyboard", "physical keyboard", "turn off keyboard".

Row (mock K2): - Label On-screen keyboard + This screen chip. SegmentedControl Auto · On · Off. - Description, by state: - Auto, nothing learned: Shows on touchscreens when you tap a text field. Typing on a real keyboard hides it on this screen. - Auto, learned: Hidden here because a keyboard was used. + text button Show it again (removes the flag). - On: Shows whenever you tap a text field. - Off: Never shows by itself. On a touchscreen, tap Keyboard by a field to open it.

Storage (the "This screen" model, shared with audit §2): - On a kiosk (getKioskId() set): write the kiosk override onScreenKeyboard via PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides. That endpoint replaces the whole object, so GET it, merge the key and PUT it back. The kiosk already receives merged config, so the composable reads configStore.onScreenKeyboard unchanged. An admin can also set it from a phone (below). - On any other browser: localStorage["calvin-osk-mode"]. It falls back to the server value when it's missing or unreadable. - The global server key stays the default for screens without their own value. It is no longer shown as a row: the row edits this screen. - Build one helper, useScreenSetting(key) (frontend/src/composables/useScreenSetting.js), returning { value, set, scope: "kiosk" | "browser" }, so audit §2 (Touchscreen, Settings text size) reuses it.

Kiosks › {kiosk} (mock K3): a new CollapsibleSection Touch & keyboard, after Display hardware, with On-screen keyboard Auto · On · Off. It uses the same override labels as the audit §3.5 (Same as all screens / Only this kiosk + Use the shared setting). When the audit's §2 lands, Touchscreen joins this section. The learned flag isn't visible here (it lives in the kiosk's browser).

docs.title: 7. Accessibility
docs.text:
• The button is a real <button> in the tab order after the focused field's form. Its name is Show on-screen keyboard.
  • When the OSK hides because of physical typing, announce nothing: the user caused it and is typing.
  • Show it again announces On-screen keyboard will show again. via the settings aria-live region.

docs.title: 8. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• isPhysicalTyping(event, target) predicate (named and exported, like isTrustedKeyInTarget): true for a trusted "a" in a target. False for untrusted, arrows, Enter, Escape, F5, Space, Ctrl+A, and a key on a non-target.
  • Auto: physical typing hides and sets calvin-osk-hardware-seen; the next focus doesn't show the keyboard; the button shows; tapping it shows the keyboard and removes the flag.
  • On: physical typing hides for this field only, the next focus shows again, and no flag is set.
  • Off: focus never shows; the button shows on touch; a tap opens for this field and the mode stays Off.
  • Non-touch: no button in any mode; Auto never shows.
  • Button: pointerdown default prevented and focus stays in the input; hidden on blur and while the OSK is visible; renders above an open AdminSignInDialog; absent inside [data-osk="off"].
  • Lock screen with the flag set: password field focus → button visible → tap → OSK with the layout key.
  • Storage: localStorage throws → mode falls back to the server value; the flag lasts for the page only.
  • useScreenSetting: with a kiosk id it PUTs merged overrides; without one it writes localStorage; it reads the server default when unset.
  • Settings row: the four description states; Show it again clears the flag. Kiosks row: inherit/override labels and Use the shared setting removes the key.

docs.title: Setting up what each screen shows
docs.text: Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/screens-setup/screens-setup.html, PNGs mocks/screens-setup/png/s1.png … s3.png.
