Builds on the settings audit (2026-10-30-settings-copy-audit.md) and the CLV-17 reorg (2026-10-29-settings-categories-reorg.md). The preview-orientation bug is fixed separately in PR #155.

docs.title: 1. The job, and how it goes today
docs.text:
The job: "The kitchen screen shows the calendar page, the hallway one shows photos and is mounted in portrait."

Today that takes four places:

Step Where Design the layouts Dashboard › Screens & regions › Open editor (modal) Check how it looks on the hallway Pi Same editor, Preview as (until #155, it ignored the kiosk's rotation) Choose which layouts each Pi shows, and its start layout Kiosks › select card › {id} — Content Set portrait, upside down, rotate output Kiosks › Display hardware (drawer) for one Pi, or Screen & keyboard › Screen orientation for "everyone" Power schedule, idle off, touch, keyboard Screen & keyboard for everyone; Kiosks for one Pi (schedule and keyboard only) Room name in the clock bar Screens › a screen › Name (per screen)

The editor itself is solid. The problems are around it.

docs.title: 2. Findings
docs.text:
1. "Screen" means two different things. "Screens & regions", "Screens shown", "Default screen" and the editor's "This screen" mean a dashboard layout. "Screen & keyboard", "Screen power", "Screen timeout" and the audit's This screen / Same as all screens mean a physical display. On the Kiosks page, both meanings sit in adjacent rows ("Screens shown" just above "Same as all screens").
  2. One Pi's settings are split across three categories. Physical defaults live in Screen & keyboard, per-Pi exceptions in Kiosks, and the room name in Dashboard. The same row (Orientation, Power schedule) appears in two categories, with nothing linking them.
  3. The editor doesn't know about the Pis.
  4. Its tabs don't say which Pi shows which layout.
  5. The "isn't set to show" warning says "assign it in Kiosks", but that word isn't a link (<span class="link">).
  6. The preview is always 5:3 or 3:5, whatever the Pi's real screen is (800×480 and 1080×1920 look very different).
  7. Upside down turns the preview upside down. On the real screen the picture is the right way up: that's the point of the setting.
  8. The Kiosks page doesn't show the layouts. "Screens shown" is a row of name chips. You can't see what a Pi will look like, and the "add more screens" hint points to another category in plain text.
  9. Pis have no name of their own. A card shows the install id (hall-pi) and hostname. The room name that would identify it ("Hallway") is one global value.
  10. Its own vocabulary: "‹inherited from global›", "Reset content to global", "Global default".

docs.title: 3.1 Words (owner decision A)
docs.text:
• A dashboard layout is a page: "Pages & regions", "Pages shown", "Start page", the editor's Page inspector.
  • A physical display is a screen, as in the audit. "Kiosk" stays only where it's about installing the Pi software ("Add a screen" → the Raspberry Pi kiosk install steps).
  • Config keys don't change (dashboardScreens, availableScreens, defaultScreenId); only UI copy and docs do.

docs.title: 3.2 One place per screen (owner decision B)
docs.text:
Kiosks and Screen & keyboard merge into one category, Screens (📺, subtitle "Pages · rotation · power · touch"). That makes 6 categories: Content · Dashboard · Screens · Plugins · System · Security.

The Screens category (mock S1): - All screens card first: the shared settings every screen uses unless it has its own. Today's Screen & keyboard rows split by what they're about (decision C): - here, things about the screen itself: orientation, upside down, rotate output; power schedule, turn off when idle, reboot combo (it restarts the Pi, so it sits under Power); touchscreen, on-screen keyboard, keyboard layout (how text is typed on this screen, and per-screen per CLV-21/27); - to Dashboard, things about operating the dashboard: Remote & buttons (button bindings) and key-press feedback move to a Dashboard section Focus & remote, next to Focus light and Dim other regions. Those rows only matter to someone driving the dashboard with a remote or arrow keys, and the focus light is what those buttons move. They're the same on every screen, and no screen overrides them. - Then one card per screen: - its name (§3.3) and the id in --font-data --ink-3; - online/offline; - a thumbnail of its start page, drawn in its own orientation (the editor's region boxes at 96px, no live content); - a one-line summary, e.g. 2 pages · portrait · off 23:00–06:30; - the kiosk software line (CLV-19, unchanged). - + Add a screen (today's AddKioskPanel).

Selecting a card opens that screen's page (mock S2). It's a sub-view with a back link ‹ Screens, not more sections stacked under the list. On a phone the list hides; on a kiosk width it's a two-pane layout (list 320px, detail the rest). Sections: 1. Name: one field, Name, description Shown in this screen's clock bar. It writes the override displayName (§3.3). 2. Pages: - the pages as a list of thumbnails (same 96px drawing), each with a checkbox Show and a radio Start here; - button Edit pages, which opens the editor previewing this screen (§3.4); - with one page only: Only one page so far. + Edit pages (replaces the plain-text hint). 3. Display: - Orientation, Upside down, Rotate the screen output; - a live 160px preview of the start page in this orientation beside them, which updates as you change them. 4. Power: Screen on/off schedule, Turn off when idle. 5. Touch & keyboard: Touchscreen (once audit §2 lands), On-screen keyboard (CLV-27). 6. Software: kiosk software version and Update (CLV-19 card actions, moved here from the list card's second row).

Every row in 1–5 uses the audit §3.5 pattern: Same as all screens (--ink-3), or Only this screen (--ink, 600) followed on the same description line by · and the text button Use the shared setting. The control stays alone on the right, so the row fits at 50% width. The per-section "Reset … to global" buttons go away.

Search (settingsRegistry.js): the device-* and kiosks* destinations move under screens, with the old ids aliased like CLV-17 did (device → screens, kiosks → screens), so deep links and phone QR codes keep working.

docs.title: 3.3 A screen's name is its room name
docs.text: displayName is already a config key and kiosks already get merged config. A screen's Name is just that key in its overrides: - The Screens card, the editor's preview picker and the clock bar on that Pi all show it. - With no override, the card falls back to the hostname, then the id; the clock bar shows nothing for a screen with no name. - There is no global room name (CLV-84). A browser that isn't a known screen shows no room name, and a one-time migration copies an existing global value onto every screen without a Name, then clears the global key (CLV-111). With no screens registered yet, the global key is kept until a later startup can copy it.

docs.title: 3.4 The editor knows the screens (mock S3)
docs.text:
• Preview on (renamed from "Preview as"): options are Any browser (the shared settings) and then each screen by name. It opens preselected:
  • on a kiosk → that kiosk;
  • from a screen's Edit pages → that screen;
  • otherwise → Any browser.
  • Orientation and size come from the screen.
  • Orientation and upside down come from its overrides (#155).
  • The device's aspect ratio comes from the screen's reported viewport (§4). Without a report, use 16:9 (or 9:16 in portrait).
  • The badge reads e.g. Portrait · 1080×1920 · mounted upside down. Upside down no longer rotates the preview: the badge only says it.
  • With Any browser, a two-option toggle Landscape · Portrait previews either orientation without saving.
  • Page tabs show their screens.
  • Under each tab name, a --fs-xs --ink-3 line: Kitchen · Hallway, All screens, or Not on any screen.
  • While previewing a screen, tabs it doesn't show are drawn at 50% opacity.
  • The mismatch banner works. "Hallway doesn't show "Photos"." + button Show it on Hallway, which adds the page to that screen's availableScreens override (GET, merge, PUT) and dismisses the banner. The plain-text "Kiosks" is gone.
  • The note under the stage stays: Previewing on Hallway · edits change the shared "Photos" page. Pages are shared; only which pages a screen shows is per screen.

docs.title: 4. Data needed
docs.text:
• Viewport report: the kiosk frontend adds vw/vh (window.innerWidth/innerHeight at load and on resize, debounced 2s) to its existing kiosk config fetch (configPath()). The registry stores viewport: {w, h} on KioskDB (new nullable JSON column, Alembic migration) and returns it in GET /kiosks.
  • Overrides in the list: GET /kiosks also returns each kiosk's overrides. The list then renders names, thumbnails and summaries without N extra requests, and the editor (#155) can read them without a fetch. Override payloads are already size-capped. Agent-only keys (the update flag) are stripped.

docs.title: 5. Phasing
docs.text:
1. Builder integration (§3.4 + §4), the page/screen wording (decision A), and §3.3 names. No category change. This fixes the job's worst step: you see what each screen will really show.
  2. Screens category (decision B, §3.2): moves rows, adds the sub-view, aliases ids.

Phase 1 is useful on its own. Phase 2 only moves things.

docs.title: 6. Owner decisions
docs.text:
Approved 2026-10-30: A, B and C. C answers the owner's question "should keyboard really be there?".

  • A. Rename dashboard "screens" to "pages" in the UI (keys unchanged). Recommended: it ends the double meaning at its source.
  • B. Merge Kiosks + Screen & keyboard into one Screens category (7 → 6) with an "All screens" card and a page per screen. Recommended: one Pi's settings end up in one place.
  • C. Keyboard placement (§3.2): the on-screen keyboard and its layout stay with Screens; remote buttons and key-press feedback go to Dashboard › Focus & remote; the reboot combo goes under Screens › Power.

docs.title: 7. For CLV-31 (audit build, in flight)
docs.text: Phase 2 waits for CLV-31. To avoid redoing its work, CLV-31 should: - Use "page" for layouts in any string it touches (decision A). For example, the audit's Orientation description becomes Which way the screen is mounted. Pages & regions decides how regions stack., and "Screens shown" / "Default screen" become Pages shown / Start page. - Use "Only this screen", not "Only this kiosk", for the audit §3.5 override label. The rest of §3.5 is unchanged (Same as all screens, Use the shared setting). Kiosk section titles use the name from §3.3 when it's set, otherwise the id: {name} · Screen on/off schedule. - Leave rows where they are. Don't move Touchscreen, Remote & buttons or key-press feedback between categories; phase 2 does that (§3.2, decision C). The audit's Dashboard split (Controls / Touch & focus) stays as specced. Phase 2 then renames Touch & focus to Focus & remote when Touchscreen leaves and the remote rows arrive.

docs.title: 8. Tests (vitest), phase 1
docs.text:
• Preview on:
  • preselects the kiosk on a kiosk, and the screen from Edit pages;
  • uses the screen's orientation and viewport ratio, falling back to 16:9 / 9:16;
  • upside down shows in the badge and doesn't rotate the device;
  • with Any browser, the Landscape · Portrait toggle changes the preview and writes nothing.
  • Page tabs: the screens line for each case (named screens, all, none), and dimming while previewing a screen.
  • Mismatch: Show it on Hallway PUTs merged overrides with the page added and the banner disappears; a failed PUT keeps the banner and shows Couldn't update Hallway. Try again.
  • Names: the card, the picker and the clock bar show the override displayName; the fallback order is hostname, then id.
  • Backend: the config fetch with vw/vh stores the viewport; GET /kiosks returns viewport and overrides without agent-only keys; the migration upgrades and downgrades.
  • Copy: no "‹inherited from global›", "Global default" or "Reset … to global" left in Settings.

docs.title: Settings copy and knobs audit
docs.text:
Status: spec. Mockup: mocks/settings-copy/settings-copy.html, PNGs mocks/settings-copy/png/c1.png, c2.png. Frontend only, except §2 (scope), which needs an owner decision.

Every SettingRow, section and option label in Settings was read against what the code actually does. Category structure (CLV-17) stays. This is about the words and the knobs inside it.

docs.title: 1. Findings, worst first
docs.text:
1. You can't tell which screens a setting changes. Almost every knob is saved on the server and applies to every screen, but several say "this device", "this Pi" or "the Pi's timezone". Touchscreen says "Whether this device is treated as a touchscreen" and then forces touch on every kiosk, phone and laptop. Settings UI size scales Settings on the phone and the wall alike. This is what caused the photos-fullscreen trap (PR #149).
  2. Some descriptions are wrong.
  3. Photo-frame timeout: "Seconds before the photo frame advances." It is actually the idle time before photo-frame mode starts (usePhotoFrameMode.js). The slider also defaults to 60 while the store defaults to 300.
  4. Display name: "shown in the title bar". It's shown in the clock bar.
  5. Auto-hide delay: "the mode indicator". The section is about key-press feedback.
  6. Engineer words. "Origins", "statusbar items", "Config polling interval", "Backend/Frontend version", "Horizontal/Vertical layout" (meaning top/bottom vs side bars), "Apply display rotation … OS display output", "‹inherited from global›".
  7. Redundant or half-knobs.
  8. Screen timeout toggle + Timeout "(0 = never)": two ways to say off.
  9. Theme mode "Auto" vs "Time": you can't tell which one follows the clock.
  10. Dark mode start/end (hour): number inputs taking 0–23.
  11. Things a family member should never meet sit next to things they use daily. Repository, Branch, Log level, Config polling interval and Console logging sit in the open in System.
  12. Similar names for different things. "Keyboard" (on-screen keyboard) vs "Button bindings" (remote) vs "Key-press feedback". "Photo-frame mode" vs photos "Fullscreen". "Power schedule" (Screen & keyboard) vs "Display schedule" (Kiosks).

docs.title: 2. Scope: say where a setting applies (owner decision)
docs.text:
Every row says who it affects, using one rule, not ad-hoc copy:

  • Default (no marker): all screens. That's most settings, so no noise.
  • A row that applies only to the browser you're holding gets a scope chip after the label: This screen (--fs-xs, --ink-2, 1px --line border, --radius-sm, padding 0 6px). Its description never repeats "this device".
  • A row a kiosk can override keeps the Kiosks pattern, with new copy (§3.5).

Decision needed (gate): move the two settings that are obviously per-screen from server config to the browser (localStorage, try/catch, same pattern as calvin-osk-layout):

Setting Today Proposed Why Touchscreen (touchControls) server, all screens This screen (calvin-touch-controls) A mouse PC and a wall panel need opposite answers Settings text size (uiSize) server, all screens This screen (calvin-ui-size) A phone and a 7" panel need opposite answers

On first load after the change, a browser with no local value starts from the old server value, so nothing visibly changes on upgrade. The server key is then only that seed. Everything else stays server-wide.

Recommendation: yes. Without it, the copy in §3 has to keep warning "applies to every screen", which is the problem we're fixing.

docs.title: 4. Advanced disclosure
docs.text: System gets one CollapsibleSection Advanced, closed by default, last in the category. It holds: Repository, Branch, Console logging, Log level, Check for setting changes every. Search (settingsRegistry.js) still finds them and opens the section. No other category gets one: hiding more would make search the only way in.

docs.title: 5. Copy rules (for every future row)
docs.text:
1. Label = what you'd say out loud: a noun ("Font") or a short verb phrase ("Shuffle photos"). No "Enable".
  2. Description only when the label isn't enough. One sentence, ≤ 110 characters, no "this device" (that's the chip). No "Controls whether …".
  3. Units go on the control ("30 s", "5 min"), never in the label "(s)" or the description.
  4. Never describe the code: no "statusbar", "origins", "polling", "backend", "OS output".
  5. Use the same word for the same thing everywhere: screen (not display), clock bar, plugin, web page.
  6. Options are short, parallel words; "Always on" is "Always" when the label already says what's on.

This section is the reference until there is a design README.

docs.title: 6. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• Snapshot-free text checks: each renamed label and description in §3 renders verbatim (one test per category file, table-driven).
  • Photo frame: description says idle; the slider default is 5 min when the config value is missing.
  • Theme mode: "On a schedule" shows the Dark from time pickers; each picker writes a whole hour (0–23) to the existing keys.
  • Turn off when idle: "Never" writes displayTimeoutEnabled: false; any other option writes true plus displayTimeout in seconds. An existing value not in the list shows as its own option ("{n} min").
  • The corner rows show only while Hide controls is on.
  • Advanced: closed by default; a search hit for "branch" opens it and scrolls to the row.
  • Kiosks: inherited rows read "Same as all screens"; Use the shared setting removes the override key.
  • §2, if approved: Touchscreen and Settings text size read/write localStorage, seed once from the server value, survive a storage exception (fall back to the server value), and show the This screen chip.

docs.title: No developer words in the UI (CLV-63)
docs.text:
Status: spec (release prep, epic calvin-354a). Frontend copy only, plus one small helper. Rules from 2026-10-30-settings-copy-audit.md §5: - say screen, page, source, plugin, Calvin (for the server); - never "backend", "frontend", "API", "instance", "config", "branch", "schema", "Healthy"; - no raw error text on the dashboard.

Paths are under frontend/src/. "→ remove" means delete the element. Build after CLV-64 (theme tokens).

docs.title: 1. Raw errors (fix once, everywhere)
docs.text:
Today raw err.message / response.data.detail reaches the screen. On the wall that means "Network Error" or "Request failed with status code 500". Where: stores/images.js, calendar.js, webServices.js, config.js, keyboard.js (error.value = err.message), shown in PhotoSlideshow.vue:23; also WebComponentHost.vue:56, ClockBarItemsTab.vue:110, SecuritySettings.vue:105/145, useConfigForm.js:241.

New helper utils/friendlyError.js: friendlyError(err, action) → one sentence:

Case Text no response (network) Couldn't reach Calvin. Check that it's running and on the same network. 401/403 You need to sign in as admin to {action}. 404 That's no longer there. Reload and try again. 409 That conflicts with an existing one. (callers may pass a specific line) 422/400 with a string detail written for people (backend validation messages) that detail 5xx / anything else Something went wrong on the Calvin server while trying to {action}.
  • Stores keep the raw error for logs (logError) and expose errorText from friendlyError.
  • On the dashboard, no error text at all: offline/stale states use the CLV-20 empty states and the ConnectionStatus pill (#172). Remove PhotoSlideshow.vue:23-24 ({{ imagesStore.error }}).
  • In Settings, a raw detail may appear only behind a Details disclosure (--fs-xs, --font-data, --ink-3) under the friendly line. Same for UpdatesTab.vue:69, 117.

docs.title: Plugin copy, labels and icons (CLV-85)
docs.text: Status: spec for one calvin-plugins lane. Source: calvin-plugins origin/main (209ff2b), the PluginMetadata(...) in each plugin.py, read with ast. Renderer contract: CLV-74 (label = field label; description = the hint under the field; hidden skipped). Copy rules: settings audit §5 and the no-developer-words table (#193). midnight-theme 2.0.0 is in the themes audit §4 and isn't repeated here.

docs.title: 1. Findings
docs.text:
• No field in any of the 14 plugins sets label (54 fields). Every form shows the description as the label, the hint line is empty, and some descriptions are long sentences with URLs and defaults in them.
  • Nothing is required, so a form saves without its address or API key and then fails later.
  • Names and descriptions mix styles: "Mealie Meal Plan", "Email (IMAP)", "Yr.no Weather", URLs inside descriptions, and "Demonstrates event system usage".
  • No plugin sets icon. The contract only allows an emoji or an image file. Emoji render differently per OS and kiosk font (the frontend audit counted 17 emoji-as-icon in the host).
  • test-plugin and test-plugin-frontend are in the catalog. A family would see "Test Plugin" in "Add a web page or app".
  • instance_label (used in "Add {label}" titles) is Title Case or missing.

docs.title: 2. Decisions (owner approved P1 and P2, 2026-10-31)
docs.text:
• P1. Icons are mdi names (recommended): icon: "mdi:<name>". The host resolves it from a curated map in frontend/src/utils/pluginIcon.js (about 30 names, imported individually from @mdi/js, so the bundle grows by a few KB rather than the whole set). An unknown name or an emoji falls back to the first letter, as today. A plugin that needs its own mark may still ship frontend/icon.svg, monochrome and drawn with currentColor. This is a small host change in the same lane as the plugin edits.
  • P2. Test plugins leave the catalog (recommended): plugins.json marks them "catalog": false. They stay installable from the repo for development, and the catalog list filters them out.

docs.title: 3. Names, descriptions, icons, instance labels
docs.text:
Description = one sentence for the picker tile: what you see and what it needs. No URLs, no "Calvin", no brand claims.

Plugin name description icon instance_label chromecast Chromecast What's playing on a Chromecast or Google speaker. mdi:cast speaker image-processor Photo resizer Shrinks large uploaded photos and makes thumbnails. mdi:image-auto-adjust (none; single instance) imap Photos from email Saves photo attachments from an email inbox to Local photos. mdi:email-outline email account immich Immich Albums from your Immich photo server. mdi:image-multiple Immich album lychee Lychee Albums from your Lychee photo server. mdi:folder-image Lychee album mealie Mealie This week's meal plan from your Mealie server. mdi:silverware-fork-knife Mealie server nasa-apod NASA picture of the day NASA's astronomy picture of the day, plus past ones. mdi:telescope (none) picsum Random photos Random photos from Picsum.
