docs.title: 5. Repo rules (calvin-plugins CI)
docs.text:
Extend test_validate_plugins.py so this can't drift: - every instance_config_schema field has a non-empty label in sentence case (first letter upper, no Title Case words except proper nouns from an allowlist: Immich, Lychee, Mealie, NASA, SL, Unsplash, Yr, Gmail, Outlook, Google, Chromecast, ID, API); - description, if present, is ≤ 120 characters, ends with a full stop, and has no http; - name is ≤ 28 characters; description (plugin) is one sentence, ≤ 90 characters, no http; - icon matches ^mdi:[a-z0-9-]+$ and is in the host's curated list (the list is mirrored in the test); - catalog entries with "catalog": false are excluded from the published list.

Bump each touched plugin's patch version (copy-only changes are not breaking). The host map for P1 lands in the same lane as one small calvin PR.

docs.title: Themes audit (CLV-76)
docs.text: Status: audit + decisions. Owner decisions 2026-10-31: D1 yes, D2 yes, D3 yes, D4 yes (four built-ins; plugin themes per §4). The fixes fold into the doctrine migration PRs (frontend doctrine, frontend audit). Owner decisions are marked D1–D4.

docs.title: 1. How theming works today
docs.text:
• Mode (themeMode: Light · Dark · Follow device · On a schedule) toggles .dark on <html>. theme.css holds Calvin's own palette for both.
  • Theme (selectedThemeId; picker shows Calvin default plus the built-ins Light, Dark, Ocean, Forest, Sunset from backend/data/themes/builtin.json). applyCustomTheme() writes the theme's variables, plus its dark_mode block when the mode is dark, onto :root.
  • Every built-in sets the same 22 semantic colours in both modes: bg-0/1/2, ink/-2/-3, line, line-soft, focus, ok, warn, err, their -ink/-text pairs, and shadow/shadow-hover.
  • Everything else is derived from those via color-mix: --focus-glow, --switch-track-off, --tag-* tints.
  • So the role tokens (--text-*, --gap-*, --radius-*) are theme-independent by design. Only colour varies.
  • calvin-0ue problem 1 (themes didn't tint the shell) is resolved: all five set the surface tokens since the semantic migration and CLV-64. The CLV-64 contrast test covers 5 themes × 2 modes for text pairs.

docs.title: 2.1 Light and Dark are not themes (calvin-0ue problem 2, still open)
docs.text:
Theme In light mode In dark mode Problem Light identical to Calvin default identical to Calvin default's dark a duplicate of "Calvin default" Dark dark palette while the mode says Light dark palette contradicts the "Light or dark" setting; On a schedule and Follow device silently stop working

So the picker offers 6 entries where there are really 4 palettes (Calvin, Ocean, Forest, Sunset), and two of the entries fight the mode setting.

docs.title: 2.2 Status colours collide with the accent (all themes)
docs.text:
Hue of focus (the accent) against the status colours:

Theme · mode focus warn ok err Collision Calvin · light 33° 39° 153° 6° warn ≈ focus (6° apart) Calvin · dark #f3b052 #f3b052 155° 5° warn is the accent colour exactly Ocean · light / dark 201° / 199° 38° / 42° 174° / 168° 0° / 4° ok vs focus 27–31° apart (teal vs blue): borderline Forest · light / dark 95° / 88° 39° / 42° 123° / 123° 3° / 5° ok ≈ focus (28–35° apart, both green) Sunset · light / dark 27° / 32° 35° / 42° 113° / 88° 14° / 14° focus, warn and err all orange-red

Effect: a warn Tag ("Update"), an err line and a selected control look alike. That breaks the doctrine rule "orange = act here or selected". Contrast passes, so CLV-64 didn't catch it: this is a hue problem, not a contrast problem.

docs.title: 2.3 Colours outside the theme system
docs.text:
Colour tokens with literal values that no theme sets (theme.css):

Tokens Verdict --region-calendar #4caf50, --region-photos #2196f3, --region-service #ff9800 (page-editor region fills) Fix. Material green/blue/orange, the same in every theme. Blue breaks the palette, orange collides with focus, and colour-coding kinds breaks the doctrine ("a category is never coloured") default calendar colour #2196f3 in the add form Fix. Material blue; ignores the theme --device-* (editor device bezel), --scrim-*, --on-scrim, --qr-surface, --mask-opaque, --on-event-ink* Fine: a device bezel is dark, a QR plate is white and a scrim is black in every theme

docs.title: 2.4 Unfinished-looking
docs.text:
• Sunset light: everything is peach (bg-0 #ffe2d0, bg-1 #fff1e7), so cards barely separate from the page (bg-0 vs bg-1 ΔL small). With §2.2 it reads as one orange wash.
  • Theme picker: a list of names with one swatch. You can't see what a theme does in your current mode, and "Calvin default" vs "Light" looks like a bug.
  • Ocean/Forest/Sunset otherwise look complete in both modes (after #197/#206: toggles, tags and buttons all derive from the 22 tokens).

docs.title: 3. Recommendations
docs.text:
D1. Drop Light and Dark as themes (recommended). A theme is a palette family; light or dark is the mode. - The picker lists Calvin (renamed from "Calvin default"), Ocean, Forest, Sunset. - Migration on load: selectedTheme: "light" → null; selectedTheme: "dark" → null and themeMode: "dark", so nobody's screen changes. - Remove both from builtin.json. Plugin themes follow the same model (§4). - Alternative (not recommended): picking Dark sets the mode to Dark. That keeps two controls for one thing, and the mode would change behind the user's back.

D2. Keep status hues apart from the accent (recommended). Rule for every theme, enforced by extending the CLV-64 contrast test: - hue distance ≥ 25° between focus and each of ok and err; - ≥ 25° between warn and err; - ≥ 12° between focus and warn. Warm accents can't get further from an amber warning without it turning olive, so warn is also never shown without its ⚠ icon and word.

Proposed values (checked: hue Δ and ≥ 3:1 against the surface for the colour itself; the -ink/-text pairs are recomputed for AA by the same script CLV-64 used):

Theme · mode Change Calvin · light warn → #b38f00 (48°, Δ15° from focus) Calvin · dark warn → #ffd84d (47°, Δ12°; it was identical to focus) Forest · both ok → teal-green #1f8a6e / #5fd3b0 (≈ 163°, Δ69–74°) Sunset · both err → crimson #b0203f / #ff6b81 (≈ 349°, Δ40°); warn → #9a7400 / #ffdb4d (Δ16–18°) Ocean · both ok → #2e8b57 / #66d19e (≈ 148°, Δ48–55°)

Plus: status is never colour alone. Tags already carry the word; InlineNote gets the ⚠/✕/✓ icon.

D3. Neutral regions in the page editor (recommended). Region fills use --bg-2 with a 1px --line border, an mdi kind icon and the label. The selected region uses --focus. Delete --region-*. Kinds stay recognisable by icon and label, in every theme.

D4. Theme set: keep four for 0.1.0 (recommended). No new themes now. Later candidates: - Night: very low luminance, warm, for bedrooms and hallways at night. It would be a mode-like schedule target rather than a palette. - High contrast (accessibility).

Both are 0.2+.

Also, with no decision needed: - Calendar colours: an --event-1…8 palette per theme (curated so --on-event-ink is AA on each). New calendars take the next unused one, and the colour field offers these 8 swatches first and a custom colour second. This replaces the #2196f3 default. - Sunset light surfaces: bg-0 a step darker (#f6d6c2), so panels separate from the page (ΔL ≥ the Calvin theme's). - Theme picker: each option shows a mini preview (page, panel, a primary button, a tag) in the current mode, plus "Light and dark" under the name. It lives with Appearance in the Dashboard category migration PR.

docs.title: 4. Plugin themes (e.g. calvin-plugins midnight-theme)
docs.text:
Today: validate_theme_variables accepts any object, and applyCustomTheme() writes every key verbatim as --<key> on :root. So a theme can: - override layout tokens (--gap-*, --z-*, --touch-target); - inject url()/var() values; - ship only half a palette, leaving the other half on Calvin's colours.

midnight-theme 1.1.0 shows all three problems: - it sets 15 of the 22 colours and 17 legacy keys (accent-*, bg-primary, calendar-*, text-*, border-color, indicator-*) that the shell no longer reads; - it sets dark colours in both variables and dark_mode, which is the "Dark ignores the mode" problem from §2.1.

The model (theme contract 2): a theme is a palette family, exactly like a built-in: 1. Colours only. A theme may set only the colour allowlist: the 22 semantic colours plus the optional event-1…event-8. Any other key (role, size, spacing, radius, z-index, font, legacy names) is ignored with a warning at install and never written to the page. 2. Both modes. variables is the light palette and dark_mode the dark one. Both are required, so picking a theme never fights the light/dark setting (D1). 3. Required vs derived. - The 14 base colours are required in both modes: bg-0/1/2, ink/-2/-3, line, line-soft, focus, ok, warn, err, shadow, shadow-hover. - The 8 pairs are derived if missing: focus/ok/warn/err × -ink/-text. - -ink = --ink or --bg-1, whichever passes AA on the tone. - -text = the tone mixed toward --ink until it passes AA on --bg-1. - The same algorithm CLV-64 used, ported to the backend so derived values are stored at install. - event-1…8 fall back to Calvin's palette. 4. Values: #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla() only. No var(), url(), keywords or expressions. 5. Checks at install and at load (every startup, for installed and bundled themes): - missing base colour, bad value, or a text pair below AA (ink/ink-2/ink-3 on bg-1; -text on bg-1; -ink on its tone) → rejected at install, with the missing or failing keys named: "Midnight can't be installed: it's missing bg-2 in dark mode."; - an already-installed theme that fails at load is kept but not selectable. If it was selected, Calvin falls back to the Calvin theme in the current mode, and the picker shows it disabled with "Needs an update to work with this Calvin."; - the hue-distance rule (D2) is a warning, not a rejection, for third-party themes: install succeeds and the picker shows "Status colours may be hard to tell apart in this theme." under its name. - Catalog themes (calvin-plugins) must pass all rules in that repo's CI (test_validate_plugins.py). 6. Versioning: theme.json gains "theme_api": 2. A theme without it is checked by the same rules (most old themes fail on legacy keys only, which are now just ignored).

What midnight-theme needs (calvin-plugins PR, version 2.0.0): - add "theme_api": 2; remove the 17 legacy keys; - keep the dark palette in dark_mode (focus #8b5cf6 263°, ok #3fb950, warn #fbbf24, err #f87171: all pass the D2 distances); - add a real light palette in variables (contrast and hue checked against bg-1):

Token Light value Token Light value bg-0 #eceaf6 focus #6d28d9 (6.6:1) bg-1 #f7f6fc ok #15803d (4.7:1) bg-2 #ffffff warn #a16207 (4.6:1, Δ35° from err) ink #1b1630 (16:1) err #b91c1c (6.0:1) ink-2 #4b4566 (8.3:1) line #d9d5ea ink-3 #6e6889 (4.9:1) line-soft #e7e4f2 shadow / shadow-hover rgba(27,22,48,.10) / rgba(27,22,48,.16)
  • derived pairs: let the host derive them (or ship them; either passes);
  • update its README: "Midnight: violet on night blue in dark mode, violet on pale lavender in light mode."

docs.title: 5. Where the fixes land
docs.text: Fix PR D2 status hues + Sunset surfaces + hue-distance test + --event-* tokens Phase 1 tokens PR (theme.css + builtin.json), one PR D1 drop Light/Dark + migration + picker preview Dashboard category migration PR (useTheme.js, ThemePicker) D3 neutral regions Page editor migration PR Calendar colour palette in the add form Content category migration PR §4 plugin theme contract: backend allowlist + validation + derivation + load check; applyCustomTheme writes allowlisted keys only; picker disabled state Phase 1 tokens PR (backend + useTheme.js), with its own tests midnight-theme 2.0.0 calvin-plugins PR, after the host accepts theme_api: 2

docs.title: 6. Tests
docs.text:
• Hue-distance assertions (§D2 thresholds) in the CLV-64 contrast spec for 4 themes × 2 modes.
  • useTheme migration: light → null with the mode unchanged; dark → null and the mode set to dark; runs once.
  • The picker lists exactly Calvin, Ocean, Forest, Sunset (plus installed plugin themes).
  • No --region-* tokens or #2196f3 left (token lint).
  • --event-*: each passes AA against --on-event-ink in every theme × mode.
  • Theme contract (backend): a non-colour key is ignored and logged; a url()/var() value is rejected; a missing base colour is rejected with the key named; missing pairs are derived and pass AA; a load-time failure marks the theme unselectable and falls back to Calvin; a hue-distance failure warns but installs.
  • applyCustomTheme never writes a non-allowlisted property (unit test with a theme setting --gap-4).

docs.title: Loading light: one engine, swappable indicators
docs.text: Status: spec (owner agreed 2026-11-01). Frontend only. Builds on stores/progress.js and PerimeterProgress.vue (commit 105d4f93). Today the comet only runs for the calendar's background refresh (Dashboard.vue → progressStore.begin("calendar")).

docs.title: 1. Model
docs.text:
Two layers:

  1. Progress engine (stores/progress.js, one implementation): decides what is loading, where and when the light shows. Every indicator style behaves identically because the engine owns timing.
  2. Indicator (swappable): draws the light in a frame. It knows nothing about sources.

docs.title: 2. Engine
docs.text:
API (extends today's begin/end, keyed per source):

begin(sourceId, { regionId = null }) // regionId → region frame; null → app frame
end(sourceId)
  • Scope:
  • a source with a regionId lights that region's frame, on the same path as its focus glow. If the region is focused, the light travels on top of the glow;
  • a source without one lights the app frame (the whole dashboard perimeter);
  • 2 or more regions loading at once → one app-frame light instead of several region lights.
  • Timing (constants in the store, tested):
Rule Value Show only if still loading after 400 ms Once shown, visible at least 800 ms End after the last active source in that frame +300 ms Fade in / out 450 ms (today) Hard stop per source (a stuck fetch never spins forever) 60 s, then end + logError
  • Sources that drive it:
  • first load after a page load, until the dashboard has content (app);
  • Reload UI and a service-worker update, from the tap until the new page is up (app, on any view);
  • calendar, photo-source and plugin data fetches, foreground or background (region when the source belongs to one region, otherwise app);
  • clock-bar and status plugins (app).
  • Never drives it:
  • the /health check and the connection backoff (ConnectionStatus owns those);
  • config polling and clock ticks;
  • photo rotation from cache and prefetching the next photo;
  • SSE keepalives.
  • Failure: a failing source ends its progress. The region's own state or ConnectionStatus then speaks.

docs.title: 3. Indicators
docs.text:
Contract: a component receiving { active: boolean, frame: "app" | HTMLElement, reducedMotion: boolean }. It draws inside that frame's border box only, with aria-hidden="true" and pointer-events: none, at --z-raised above region content.

Style Look Notes Comet (default) today's bead-train orbit (--orbit-duration 3.8s), focus-light tokens Calvin's identity Pulse today's slow frame pulse (2.4s), low opacity forced when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, whatever the setting Off nothing errors, empty states and the connection pill still show, so a stuck load is never hidden

PerimeterProgress.vue splits into LoadingLight.vue (engine-facing: picks the style, mounts one per active frame) plus indicators/Comet.vue and indicators/Pulse.vue. Region frames reuse the region's existing focus-glow geometry (DashboardPanel / FocusPanel), so the light follows the panel radius.

docs.title: 4. Setting
docs.text: Dashboard › Focus & remote › Loading light: SegmentedControl Comet · Pulse · Off. - Description: What Calvin shows while it's fetching something. When the device prefers reduced motion, a second line reads This device prefers less motion, so it pulses. - Per screen ("Same as Default" / "Changed here · Reset to default", default-screen model). Config key loadingLight (comet | pulse | off), default comet.

docs.title: 5. Replaces / keeps
docs.text:
• Replaces: the region loading spinners in CalendarView.vue and WebServiceViewer.vue (background refresh, and first load when cached content is shown), and any remaining refresh spinner in the clock bar.
  • Keeps:
  • empty and "nothing configured" states (the light means working, an empty state means nothing set up);
  • button loading labels ("Saving…") for actions you started;
  • Settings and phone views have no light except the app light for Reload UI / service-worker update.

docs.title: 6. Not now
docs.text:
• Indicators from plugins or themes: the contract allows it later, but third-party animation on a wall display is a performance and accessibility risk.
  • Different styles per region (one style per screen keeps it calm).
  • A determinate bar: background fetches have no real percentage.

docs.title: 7. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• Engine timing with fake timers:
  • < 400 ms: never shown;
  • 450 ms: shown for ≥ 800 ms;
  • back-to-back sources within 300 ms: one continuous light;
  • 60 s cap ends the source and logs.
  • Scope: a regionId source lights that region; a regionless source lights the app; 2 regions promote to one app light.
  • Excluded sources (health, polling, rotation) never call begin (spy on the store from those modules).
  • Style: the setting picks Comet / Pulse / Off; reduced motion forces Pulse; Off renders nothing while the connection pill still appears on failure.
  • Reload UI / service-worker update shows the app light on the Settings view too.
  • Spinners removed: no spinner element in CalendarView / WebServiceViewer during a refresh.

docs.title: Screen on/off schedule: compact editor
docs.text: Status: spec (owner request; after rc.1). Mockup: mocks/schedule/schedule.html, PNG mocks/schedule/png/w1.png. Frontend only. Replaces DisplayScheduleGrid.vue (used on the Default page and on each screen's page).

docs.title: 1. Today
docs.text: Seven day cards, always all open. Each card has a toggle, the day name, and two labelled time fields stacked vertically. They sit in the right-hand control column of a SettingRow (260px wide), so the grid is ≈ 1,680px tall at both 1280 and 390. You scroll past it every time you visit Screens, and almost everyone uses the same times every day.

docs.title: 2.1 Collapsed by default: one row (mock W1, top)
docs.text:
The Screen on/off schedule row keeps its toggle. When it's on, the next row is:

  • Schedule, with a summary in --text-body:
  • On 06:00 · off 22:00, every day;
  • Weekdays 06:00–22:00 · weekends 08:00–23:00;
  • Different each day (+ Off on Sundays when a day is off);
  • a Change button (Button secondary sm) on the right.

That's one 56px row instead of 1,680px. The scope line ("Same as Default" / "Changed here · Reset to default") stays under the summary on screen pages.

docs.title: 2.2 Editing (mock W1, below)
docs.text:
Change expands an editor in place, below the row: a full-width SettingGroup inside the panel, not the narrow control column.

  1. How it repeats: SegmentedControl Every day · Weekdays and weekends · Each day.
  2. Then one compact table. Columns: day label · On · Off. The column headers appear once (--text-meta, --ink-2), never per row.
  3. Every day: 1 row, Every day.
  4. Weekdays and weekends: 2 rows, Mon–Fri and Sat–Sun.
  5. Each day: 7 rows, Mon … Sun (week order follows Week starts on).
  6. A row is --touch-target tall:
  7. the day label (--text-label, 4.5rem wide);
  8. two TextField type="time" (step 900, i.e. 15-minute steps; --control-height; no per-field label; the accessible name is "Monday on" / "Monday off");
  9. a ToggleSwitch on the right, accessible name Screen on, Monday. Off hides the two times and the row reads Off all day in --ink-3.
  10. Done (Button secondary sm) collapses back to the summary. Changes save as you go (existing autosave), so Done only closes.

Doctrine blocks only, with no <style> in the feature: - SettingRow for the summary row (label, summary as description, Button as control); - SettingGroup for the editor; - SegmentedControl, TextField, ToggleSwitch, Button, and InlineNote for the error; - the table is a new block, ui/FieldTable.vue: rows of label + controls, one header row, --gap-inline between cells, --touch-target rows, --text-meta headers, stacking to label-over-controls under 360px. It gets a gallery entry and leaves DisplayScheduleGrid.vue off the settingsNoStyle / controlLint allowlists. Any later "same fields per row" editor reuses it.

Heights: Every day ≈ 150px, Weekdays and weekends ≈ 200px, Each day ≈ 420px. All full width, so the phone shows the same table: day 4.5rem + two 7rem time fields fit 390px.

docs.title: 2.3 Mode from data (no new config)
docs.text:
The stored schedule stays the 7-day array ({ day, enabled, onTime, offTime }). The mode is inferred: - all 7 enabled with the same times → Every day; - Mon–Fri equal and Sat–Sun equal (and both groups enabled or both off) → Weekdays and weekends; - otherwise → Each day.

Switching mode writes the array: - Every day copies the first row to all 7; - Weekdays and weekends copies Mon to Mon–Fri and Sat to Sat–Sun; - Each day keeps the current values.

Editing a grouped row writes all days in its group.

docs.title: 2.4 Where it lives
docs.text: The same component on the Default page (§ Power) and on each screen's page. On a screen page the whole schedule is one override (as today): Changed here · Reset to default under the summary resets all 7 days.

docs.title: 3. Copy
docs.text:
• Row label Schedule; summary as in §2.1, using the user's time format (12h/24h).
  • Segments Every day · Weekdays and weekends · Each day.
  • Column headers On · Off; the row toggle is named Screen on, {day}.
  • An invalid range (off equal to on) gives the row an InlineNote err: On and off can't be the same time.
  • Off earlier than on means overnight. It's allowed and the summary says so: On 22:00 · off 06:00 the next day.

docs.title: 4. Other sections that need the same treatment
docs.text:
Measured with the mocked harness at 1280 (section heights):

Section Height Problem Fix Dashboard › Clock bar layout 1,062px For both bar shapes: 3 sliders each, stacked under Title Case labels ("Time Font Size", "Bar Padding", "Plugin Item Size") and only half-width, plus a preview Per bar: Size SegmentedControl Small · Medium · Large · Custom (presets write the 3 values). Custom opens a SettingGroup with three SettingRows (Time, Padding, Plugin info: label left, RangeSlider right, value in px). One shared live preview under the section. Collapsed ≈ 250px Screens › Touch & keyboard 618px every row stacks its control under the text even at 1280; the label "Show it" lost its context rows go side by side at ≥ 600px (§ below); "Show it" becomes On-screen keyboard; only Also switch to (6 chips) stays stacked. ≈ 380px Dashboard › Focus & remote 884px (1) three per-screen rows (Photo frame, Loading light, Layout) sit in a Dashboard section, while every other per-screen setting lives on the screen pages; (2) their descriptions render in --text-body, larger than every other description move those three to Screens › Default / each screen, in a new section Behaviour (they carry "Same as Default" already); descriptions use --text-meta. Focus & remote keeps Focus light, Dim, Dashboard size and the button rows. ≈ 450px Screens list (875px), Content › Photos (794px) content-driven (cards, sources) fine

SettingRow rule (doctrine §4 row anatomy, clarified): - side by side at ≥ 600px for any control up to 50% of the row width; - stacked only on phone, or for wide controls (chip groups, tables, sliders with a preview), via :stacked; - never stacked just because the description is long: the description wraps in the left column instead; - a height guard e2e (mocked harness) fails if a single SettingRow with a toggle, segmented control or select is taller than 120px at 1280.

docs.title: 5. Tests (vitest)
docs.text:
• Collapsed summary for each of the three shapes, plus "Off on Sundays"; 12h formatting.
  • Mode inference from arrays (equal times, weekday/weekend split, mixed).
  • Mode switching writes the array as in §2.3; editing a grouped row updates its whole group.
  • Change expands the editor; Done collapses; the editor is full width; one header row only.
  • Turning a day's toggle off hides its times and saves enabled: false.
  • FieldTable unit tests + gallery entry; DisplayScheduleGrid removed from the lint allowlists.
  • Same-time error; overnight summary.
  • Screen page: Reset to default clears the schedule override.
  • Height guard (e2e, mocked harness): the collapsed Power section is ≤ 260px tall at 1280 and 390.

docs.title: Pages & regions: swap regions and change what a region shows
docs.text: Status: spec (owner request calvin-7at6; rc.2, builds after rc.1). No mockup yet; sketches below. Frontend only: ScreenRegionEditor.vue, regions/RegionNode.vue, regions/RegionInspector.vue, utils/layout.js. No backend or config-shape change.

docs.title: 1. Today
docs.text:
• In the preview, only the clock bar drags (HTML5 drag, wide editor with a mouse only). Dividers resize.
  • You can't move a region. To put photos on the left and the calendar on the right, you have to remove both regions and add them again. That loses each region's settings: view, week numbers, events per day, photo fit, sources and When tapped.
  • The inspector already has a Shows picker that changes a region in place. But setRegionContentAtPath keeps the old view object. A calendar turned into photos carries mode, weeks and weekNumbers it never reads. The next calendar patch then rebuilds the view from only the calendar's own keys, so what survives depends on the order of edits. §4 fixes this.

docs.title: 2. The model: content swaps, slots stay
docs.text:
A page is made of slots: each slot is a position plus a size, with nested splits. Each slot holds content: id, kind, serviceId, instanceIds and view.

  • Swap exchanges the content of two leaf slots. Each slot keeps its size, and the split tree stays as it was.
  • The id travels with the content, so anything keyed by region id follows it: the screen's activeRegionId (loading light, focus and dim) and the editor selection. Swapping is the same as moving the region, with nothing to re-point.
  • Any two leaves on the same page can swap, at any depth. A sub-region of a split can swap with a top-level region, and it takes that region's slot size.
  • Split regions are not swappable in v1: they have no face to grab, and their sub-regions are the targets. Moving a whole split is a follow-up if anyone asks.
  • New helper swapLeavesAtPaths(layout, pathA, pathB) in utils/layout.js. It is a pure function and returns the layout unchanged when the paths are equal or when either one is a split.

docs.title: 3.1 Drag (every size, mouse and touch)
docs.text:
The clock bar's HTML5 drag doesn't work with touch, which is why it's limited to the wide editor with a mouse. Regions should move on the touch kiosk too, so region drag uses pointer events instead. That gives one code path for mouse, touch and pen, in every size class.

Mouse / pen Touch Start Press on a region face and move 6px or more Long-press 400ms on a region face, then move Before the start A click selects, as today A tap selects, as today. Moving before 400ms does nothing, so a stray swipe never lifts a region Cancel Escape, release over the lifted region, or release outside every region Release over the lifted region or outside every region
  • Dividers (.sre-resizer) keep their own pointerdown with .stop, so resizing never starts a swap.
  • Hit-testing uses document.elementFromPoint → the closest leaf [data-region-id], so nested leaves just work.
  • On release over another leaf: swap (§2), select the moved content, and announce it (§3.3).
  • On a coarse pointer the 400ms press shows its progress: the face's outline fills in --focus, over --dur (none under reduced motion). Then the region lifts (§5). Call navigator.vibrate?.(10) when the region lifts; where vibration isn't available, skip it.
  • On phone with the sheet open (65%), the stage is still visible above the sheet, so dragging works there too. Starting a drag doesn't close the sheet.

docs.title: 3.2 Swap with… (keyboard and tap)
docs.text:
For anyone who can't or won't drag. It goes in the inspector's Arrange group, before Split / Remove:

Arrange
  ⓘ Size 30% — drag the divider in the preview to resize.
  [ Swap with… ▾ ]  [ Split region ]  [ Remove region ]
  • It is a Button size="sm" that opens a Popover + Menu (doctrine §3) listing every other leaf on the page. It's hidden when the page has only one leaf.
  • Each item gives the kind, the source summary when it's filtered, and where the region sits: Photos · right, Calendar · Family · top left.
  • The position comes from the leaf's centre in the preview: left/centre/right × top/middle/bottom. Drop the axis the split doesn't use, so a plain row says only left / centre / right.
  • If two items still read the same, add the size: Service · right · 25%.
  • Each item has the kind icon (ListRow/Menu icon slot), and items are ≥ --touch-target tall.
  • While an item has focus or hover, its region in the preview gets the drop-target highlight (§5). Then a keyboard user sees which region they're about to pick.
  • Choosing an item swaps the regions, keeps the moved content selected, closes the menu, returns focus to Swap with…, and announces the swap (§3.3).

There are no separate Move left / Move right actions. In a two- or three-region page, Swap with… is the same thing in one step, and it also covers nested regions.

docs.title: 3.3 After a swap
docs.text:
• A visually hidden role="status" in the editor announces Swapped Calendar and Photos.
  • Nothing to confirm: a swap only rearranges, and doing it again undoes it. The editor's normal Save / Cancel still applies.

docs.title: 4. Shows: change a region in place
docs.text:
The Shows picker stays where it is. When you pick something, what happens depends on whether the kind changes:

Change Sources Settings (view) Same kind (one service → another service, or calendar → calendar) As the picked option says (today's behaviour) Kept Different kind (calendar → photos) Reset to the new option's (all sources) The new kind's defaults (viewForKind(null, kind))
  • Undo instead of confirm. When the kind changes, the old content (kind, serviceId, instanceIds, view) is parked in editor memory under that region's id. Under the Shows button an InlineNote says: Calendar settings were reset. with an Undo Button size="sm" in the note's action slot.
  • Undo puts the parked content back exactly.
  • The note goes away when another region is selected, or after the next edit to this region.
  • Switching back restores. If you pick the parked kind again for that region during the same editor session, the region gets its parked settings back, not the defaults. Turning calendar → photos → calendar loses nothing.
  • Parked content is editor memory only. It is never saved, and closing the editor drops it, so the saved config only ever holds the active kind's view.
  • Fix the leak from §1: setRegionContentAtPath sets view from viewForKind when the kind changes, and keeps it as-is when the kind stays.

docs.title: 5. Drag and drop-target feedback
docs.text:
The drop targets reuse the clock bar's drop look (.sre-drop: --focus 9% wash, dashed 50% --focus border, --radius-control, --focus-text caption). Swap and the clock bar should read as the same gesture.

State Look Lifted region (source) Stays in place; content at 45% opacity, dashed --line outline, --elev-2; cursor grabbing Drag chip A small pill under the pointer (offset 12px so a finger doesn't hide it): kind icon + Calendar. --bg-2, --elev-2, --radius-round, --text-caption, --z-raised inside the stage. Under reduced motion it still follows the pointer; it just has no fade-in Every other leaf An .sre-drop overlay inset 3px, caption Swap Leaf under the pointer .sre-drop:hover look (28% wash, solid --focus border), caption Swap with Photos Over the source or outside No highlight. Releasing does nothing Clock-bar drop zones Never shown during a region drag, and region overlays never show during a clock drag Hover with a mouse, not dragging Face shows the ⠿ grip (as on the clock bar) and cursor grab. On touch the grip is always hidden; the long-press is the affordance, and the inspector's Swap with… is the visible path

Sizes:

Size class Device Notes Wide (laptop, 1280×800 kiosk) Fitted device, region faces with icon, name, % Captions as above Compact (800×480 kiosk landscape) Smaller faces The caption drops to Swap on the target too when the face is under 120px wide Phone, and 480×800 kiosk portrait Faces may be narrow (name only, < 320px device) Captions are Swap only, and the chip shows only the icon. The sheet stays as it is (§3.1). The subtitle that names gestures is hidden here already

Sketch, wide, landscape, Calendar lifted over Photos:

┌──────────────────────────────┬────────────┐
│ ┊ ⠿ Calendar          70%  ┊ │┏━━━━━━━━━━┓│
│ ┊   (45%, dashed)          ┊ ││ Swap with ││
│ ┊                          ┊ ││  Photos   ││
│ ┊               [▣ Calendar]──▶          ││
│ ┊                          ┊ │┗━━━━━━━━━━┛│
└──────────────────────────────┴────────────┘

Copy changes: the wide header subtitle becomes Design the pages your screens display · drag regions to swap them, dividers to resize, the clock bar to reposition. Region faces keep Enter to select. The inspector's Swap with… is the keyboard path, so the face itself gets no drag ARIA.

docs.title: 6. Tests
docs.text:
• layout.spec.js: swapLeavesAtPaths swaps content and ids, keeps sizes and the split tree, works across depths, and is a no-op for equal paths or a split path.
  • layout.spec.js: setRegionContentAtPath resets view on a kind change and keeps it on the same kind.
  • RegionInspector spec:
  • Swap with… lists the other leaves with position labels, and is hidden with one leaf.
  • Choosing an item emits the swap.
  • A kind change shows the Undo note; Undo restores; switching back restores the parked view.
  • ScreenRegionEditor spec:
  • A pointer drag (6px) over another leaf swaps them and selects the moved content.
  • Escape cancels.
  • Pressing on a divider never starts a swap.
  • Clock and region drop zones never show together.
  • e2e phone (mocked harness): long-press a region, drag it onto another, check that the preview order and selection changed. Then Swap with… does the same from the sheet.

docs.title: 7. Follow-ups (not in this spec)
docs.text:
• Move the clock bar to the same pointer-event drag, so it also drags on touch.
  • Swap a whole split region.

docs.title: Pages are shared: say so, and stop new pages leaking onto every screen
docs.text: Status: spec (owner request calvin-m4rg, "bad UX"; rc.2, builds after rc.1). No mockup yet. Mostly frontend. No config-shape change: it keeps dashboardScreens, the global availableScreens / defaultScreenId, and the per-screen overrides of the same keys. Read together with region swap (#276).

docs.title: 1. Today
docs.text:
• config.dashboardScreens is one catalog for the household. A screen chooses which pages it shows:
  • Default's Pages shown (global availableScreens; null means all) applies to browsers and to every screen that follows Default.
  • A screen's own Pages shown (override availableScreens) replaces that list.
  • Add page in Pages & regions always adds to the catalog. Opened from the Kitchen screen, the new page still shows up on every screen that is on "all", and in every browser. Nothing in the UI says pages are shared, so a page added "on the Kitchen" appearing in the hallway reads as a bug.
  • Bug: the UI ignores Default's list for screens that follow Default. A screen with no availableScreens override really shows Default's list (backend merge_overrides). But three places treat "no override" as all pages:
  • ScreensSettings.effAvailable (the screen page's toggles);
  • ScreenRegionEditor.kioskShowsPage (tab meta, dimming, the mismatch banner);
  • showItOnScreen, which then says "already shown" and saves nothing. If Default hides a page, these screens' toggles show it on, while the screen itself doesn't show it.

docs.title: 2. Decision: one shared catalog, made honest
docs.text:
Keep option 1. Do not move to per-screen pages.

  • Shared is what households want. The family calendar page on the kitchen and the hallway is one page, and a change should land on both. Per-screen copies drift. Then "fix the font on both" turns into two edits, and Default-as-template raises a question with no good answer: does a template edit reach the copies?
  • It matches the Screens/Default model the rest of Settings already uses: one thing, followed live, changed in one place.
  • It's cheap. Option 2 changes the data model, needs a migration, and makes the kiosk agent read per-screen layouts. What's broken today is the UI, not the model.

What changes: where a new page shows, saying which screens a page is on, and two kinds of delete.

docs.title: 3. Scope: the editor works "for" the Preview on target
docs.text:
Pages & regions already has Preview on (a screen, or Any browser). That target is now also the editor's scope: the screen (or Default) that new pages are added to, and that "Hide" acts on.

  • Opened from a screen's page, or on a kiosk: scope = that screen (today's preselection).
  • Opened from Default: scope = Default. Rename the Any browser option to Browsers & new screens so it matches Default's copy ("The pages browsers and new screens show.").

docs.title: 4. Flows
docs.text: Everything below runs in the editor. It saves the same way Show it on… already does: for a screen, GET its overrides, merge, then PUT; for Default, patch the global config.

docs.title: 4.1 Add (and Duplicate)
docs.text:
Scope Catalog Default's list Scope's list Other screens A screen (Kitchen) page added if null (all), it is pinned to the pages that existed before, so the new page does not join it Kitchen gets an override = its current effective list + the new page unchanged: screens on Default don't gain it (Default is pinned); screens with their own list never did Default page added if null, it stays null (gains it); otherwise the new page is appended — screens that follow Default gain it; screens with their own list don't
  • Pinning Default's list doesn't change what anything shows; it only stops "all" from absorbing the newcomer. Default's page then lists the new page switched off, which is the truth.
  • When Kitchen was following Default, it now has its own list. Its page shows Changed here · Reset to default, as for any other override. Reset brings back Default's list and drops the new page from Kitchen. That's correct, and the ScopeLine already explains it.
  • After the add, the Page inspector shows an InlineNote (tone ok) under Shown on (§4.2): Shown on Kitchen only. with an Also show on… action that opens the same popover as Change….

docs.title: 4.2 Shown on (the page's scope, always visible)
docs.text:
There's a new row at the top of the Page inspector, under Page name:

Shown on   Kitchen, Hallway · browsers        [ Change… ]
  • The summary uses the existing screensLine (fixed per §1): screen labels, and browsers when Default shows the page. It reads All screens when every screen and Default show it, and Not shown anywhere (tone warn) when none do.
  • Change… opens a Popover with a ToggleSwitch row per screen, plus one for Browsers & new screens (Default). Each switch writes that target's list, using the same rule as the screen pages' toggles: all on drops the override, and turning off the last page is refused with Pick at least one page.
  • A screen that follows Default and gets toggled becomes Changed here, and its row says so in its meta.
  • This replaces nothing: the mismatch banner (Kitchen doesn't show "X". Show it on Kitchen) stays as the fast path.

docs.title: 4.3 Edit (layout, regions, swap, Shows, clock bar)
docs.text:
• An edit changes the page everywhere it shows. No confirm: the Shown on row already says where.
  • When the page shows on more than the scope, the wide subtitle names it (§5). This covers the #276 actions too: a swap or a Shows change on a page that both kitchen and hallway show changes both. That is intended.

docs.title: 4.4 Rename
docs.text:
• The name is shared. Renaming happens in place, with no confirm.
  • The Page name field gets the description Every screen that shows this page uses this name., but only when Shown on lists more than one target.

docs.title: 4.5 Remove: Hide here vs Delete everywhere
docs.text:
Delete page becomes two actions in the Page inspector:

Action Shown when What it does Hide on Kitchen (secondary) scope is a screen that shows the page, and that screen shows ≥ 2 pages Removes the page from Kitchen's list. Catalog untouched. Copy for Default scope: Hide from browsers & new screens Delete page (danger) always (disabled on the last page in the catalog, as today) Removes the page from the catalog and from every list

Delete page confirms only when someone else is affected: when the page shows anywhere other than the scope. The confirm is a Dialog size="sm":

Delete "Photos" everywhere? Hallway and browsers also show it. To take it off Kitchen only, use Hide on Kitchen. [Cancel] [Hide on Kitchen] [Delete page]

Cleanup on delete: - Strip the id from Default's list and from every screen's override. - If a screen's list would become empty, drop that override, so the screen follows Default again. - A defaultScreenId (start page) that pointed at it is dropped, so that target falls back to its first page. - Screens that are offline get the cleanup on their next override fetch, because the lists live on the server.

docs.title: 5. Copy
docs.text:
Where Today New Editor subtitle (wide) Design the pages your screens display · drag dividers to resize, the clock bar to reposition · changes apply live Pages are shared by your screens · changes apply live everywhere they show Editor stage caption (wide, under the device) — Drag regions to swap them, dividers to resize, the clock bar to reposition (the gesture line moves here; this supersedes #276 §5's subtitle copy) Preview on option Any browser Browsers & new screens Screen page → Pages section description — Pages are shared by all screens. Choose which ones this screen shows. Screen page → each page row meta Not shown here (when off) When on: Also on Hallway / Only here. When off: Not shown here Default page → Pages shown description The pages browsers and new screens show. The pages browsers and screens that follow Default show. Pages are shared by all screens. Page inspector Delete page Shown on row (§4.2), Hide on {scope}, Delete page

Phone: the subtitle and stage caption are hidden, as now. The Shown on row in the sheet carries the scope.

docs.title: 6. Build notes
docs.text:
• One helper effectivePages(target, config, catalog) in utils/screenOverrides.js. It is a pure function: given the override list, else Default's list, else all pages. It replaces the three wrong fallbacks in §1. Add a unit test for each fallback level.
  • addScreen / duplicateScreen take the scope and return the catalog patch plus the list patches (§4.1). Save the catalog first, then the lists. If a list save fails, show the existing Couldn't update {screen}. Try again. note. The page exists either way, and Shown on shows the real state.
  • Tests:
  • add from a screen with Default null pins Default and gives only that screen the page;
  • add from Default with null keeps null;
  • a screen that follows Default and has Default hiding a page shows that page's toggle off (regression for §1);
  • Hide vs Delete, including the empty-list and start-page cleanup;
  • the Delete confirm only when others are affected;
  • e2e (mocked harness): open the editor from a screen, add a page, check that Default's page lists it off.

docs.title: 7. Not doing
docs.text:
• Per-screen page copies or Default-as-template (option 2).
  • A "Make a copy for this screen only" action. Duplicate + Hide already does that in two taps. Revisit if the owner asks.

docs.title: Calvin frontend doctrine
docs.text: Status: doctrine (owner request 2026-10-31). It applies to every frontend PR, and design specs cite it instead of re-deciding basics. Extends 2026-07-04-ui-sizing-tokens.md (sizing mechanism, settings zoom) and the copy rules in 2026-10-30-settings-copy-audit.md §5.

docs.title: 0. Why
docs.text:
Things look different everywhere because: - There is no shared Button. There are 61 hand-rolled button classes in 33 files (security-btn, maint-btn, backup-btn, admin-btn, pc-btn, btn-install, kiosk-software__btn, …). Specs say ".btn", which doesn't exist, so each builder invents one. - The token scales encode the old chaos. They were created 1:1 from existing literals, so we have: - 13 font sizes (--fs-3xs 0.6 … --fs-3xl 1.7, plus --fs-control 0.875 and --fs-control-lg 0.9375); - 9 spacing steps (0.35, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.75 rem…); - 7 radii (6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 16px, pill).

"Uses a token" no longer means "consistent". - Layout has no rules. Settings panels have no padding, so children inset themselves (fixed for three components in #202), and there are 258 raw-rem paddings.

The token lint (CLV-64) stops raw colours. This doctrine stops everything else drifting.

docs.title: 1. Principles
docs.text:
1. Roles, not sizes. Components use semantic role tokens (--text-label, --gap-inline, --radius-control). Raw scales are primitives for theme.css only.
  2. One component per job. If a control exists in components/ui/, use it. Feature components lay things out; they never restyle controls.
  3. Layout comes from primitives: Panel, Row, ListRow, Stack. They own insets, dividers and rhythm, so a feature never sets padding on a child.
  4. Orange means "act here" or "selected". Nothing else is orange.
  5. Every rule is checked by a test, not by memory.

docs.title: 2. Tokens: three layers
docs.text:
All tokens are declared in frontend/src/styles/theme.css. Only theme.css may contain literal values.

Primitives (theme.css only): palettes per theme, and the existing --fs-*, --space-* and --radius-* scales. Components stop referencing these (§7 migration).

Semantic roles (what components use):

Family Token Value Use Type --text-dense --fs-3xs calendar grid chrome only --text-caption --fs-2xs (0.75) tags, counts, timestamps, hints under fields --text-meta --fs-xs (0.8) row descriptions, secondary lines --text-body --fs-md (0.9) body text, control text (buttons, inputs, selects) --text-label --fs-base (1) row labels, list-row names --text-title --fs-lg (1.15) panel and dialog titles, inspector headings --text-display --fs-3xl (1.7) clock, lock-screen title Weight --weight-body / --weight-strong / --weight-title 400 / 500 / 600 nothing else (no 550, 650, 700, bold) Space (4px grid) --gap-1 … --gap-8 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2rem (--gap-1,2,3,4,5,6,8) primitives of the roles below --gap-tight --gap-1 icon ↔ text inside a control --gap-inline --gap-2 between controls in a row --gap-stack --gap-3 between stacked items in a group --gap-group --gap-4 between groups in a panel --gap-section --gap-8 between sections (eyebrow + panel) --panel-pad-x / --panel-pad-y --gap-5 / --gap-3 every panel child's inset (exists since #202) Radius --radius-control 8px buttons, inputs, selects, tags, list-row inner controls --radius-card 12px list rows, inner cards, popovers, sheets --radius-panel 16px settings panels, dialogs, the dashboard card chrome --radius-round 999px toggles, dots, pill indicators (status pill, connection pill) Colour --bg-0/1/2, --line, --line-soft, --ink, --ink-2, --ink-3 existing surfaces, borders, text --focus, --focus-ink, --focus-text, --focus-glow, --focus-edge existing action and selection only (§5) --ok, --warn, --err (+ the --tag-* mix rule) existing status only Elevation --elev-1 (raised: menus, popovers), --elev-2 (dialogs, sheets) 0 6px 18px -8px var(--shadow-hover) / 0 18px 50px -16px var(--shadow-hover) nothing else casts shadows Motion --dur-fast 120ms, --dur 200ms, --ease cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1); --dur-loading-fade 450ms (calc(var(--dur) * 2.25)) all transitions; zero under prefers-reduced-motion. --dur-loading-fade is the loading light's fade only (loading light §2), the one slow transition Layers --z-raised 10, --z-sticky 100, --z-dialog 1000, --z-popover 1050 (popovers teleport to body, so they must clear an open dialog), --z-osk 1100, --z-toast 1200 no other z-index values Breakpoints --bp-phone (max-width: 600px, or max-height: 500px in landscape on anything but a kiosk), --bp-wide (min-width: 1024px) src/styles/breakpoints.js every width @media in app CSS, and the viewport phone checks in JS (isPhone()); nothing else

Breakpoint rules: - Phone is a viewport width <= 600 or a landscape viewport height <= 500 (a phone turned sideways: 667x375, 640x360). A phone gets no automatic on-screen keyboard, no phone hand-off QR, and the compact calendar, panel and lock-screen layouts. - The kiosk is never a landscape phone. The 800x480 wall panel is short and landscape too, so the height clause is skipped on a kiosk. The signal is the kiosk identity (?kiosk=<id>, src/utils/kioskId.js): at boot it puts calvin-kiosk on <html>. isPhone() reads that class, and the customMedia PostCSS plugin emits the height clause of (--bp-phone) as a second block scoped to :where(:root:not(.calvin-kiosk)). A kiosk started without an id gets the phone layout at 800x480. - Width still decides on a kiosk: a portrait Pi 7" (480x800) gets the phone layout, by design. - A screen can force either layout. Settings › Dashboard › Focus & remote › Layout (src/utils/layoutMode.js) sets calvin-layout-desktop or calvin-layout-phone on <html> from the effective choice: a kiosk's screen override, or this browser's own localStorage choice. isPhone()/isPhoneWidth() and the customMedia expansion of (--bp-phone) both read that class; Auto (the default) leaves it off and keeps the viewport rule. - Since CLV-98 the 481-600 px band (and exactly 480) gets the phone variants that used to start at 480 or 768 (calendar extra-small scaling, OSK phone layout, PhoneSetupCard, lock-screen phone layout, AdminAccess stacked rows, SetupWelcomeCard phone card), and 601-767 px landscape screens taller than 500 px lose the compact calendar and panel scaling. - Pane and container sizes are not viewport breakpoints: the pages editor sizes itself from its own modal with isPhoneWidth(). ScreensSettings' two-pane (max-width: 900px) matchMedia is the one JS query still outside the set (tracked as a follow-up). - Plugin and theme CSS is served as-is, without PostCSS, so (--bp-*) never expands there. Plugins and themes keep the literal @media (max-width: 600px); the plugin tokens and .calvin-plugin-* classes are otherwise unchanged.

Component tokens are allowed when a component has geometry of its own. They're prefixed with the component name and built from roles, e.g. --tag-*, --toggle-*, --tab-height, --osk-height, --touch-target, --control-height.

Rules: - The type roles are the whole vocabulary. If a design needs a size that isn't a role, the design changes, not the scale. - --fs-control and --fs-control-lg fold into --text-body; --fs-micro into --text-caption; --fs-sm into --text-body or --text-meta (choose by role); --fs-xl/--fs-2xl into --text-title. - Radii snap: 6→8 (control), 10/11→12 (card). The visual change is deliberate and small.

docs.title: 3. Components: one per job
docs.text:
components/ui/ is the only place controls are styled.

Job Use Never Any button with text Button.vue (new): variant = primary (orange, one per view region), secondary (default: --bg-2, 1px --line), ghost (no border, --ink-2), danger (--err text; filled only inside a destructive confirm); size = md (--control-height) or sm (--touch-target); optional icon a styled <button class="foo-btn"> Icon-only button IconButton.vue an emoji or letter in a styled button Text link that acts Button variant="link" (underline, --ink; --focus-text on hover) link-btn copies On/off ToggleSwitch checkbox styled as a toggle One of 2–4 SegmentedControl tab-like custom groups, filter pills One of many SelectPill native <select> Many of many ChipMultiSelect checkbox rows for chips Number NumberStepper, RangeSlider <input type="number"> Text / secret TextField (new, from PasswordField's shell), PasswordField bare <input> with local styles Label / status Tag badges, chips, pills Settings section SettingsSection (Panel) a bordered div Setting SettingRow label/description markup by hand Item in a list (source, screen, key, plugin) ListRow.vue (new), extracted from SourceList: lead (dot/thumb/icon), body (name --text-label + meta lines), trailing actions group per-feature cards Empty EmptyState an ad-hoc centred paragraph Progress of a long task (uploads) ProgressBar.vue: ARIA progressbar with a label, --progress-h track on --bg-2, --focus fill (progress is action feedback, so it may use orange); the visible "3 of 8" text sits beside it, outside any live region a styled <div> bar, a spinner Confirm / dialog ConfirmModal, DialogScrim; Dialog with size = sm / md (default) / full (edge-to-edge, for the pages editor; same focus trap, Escape and OSK rules) custom overlays, hand-built full-screen shells Navigation between views of the same thing (editor pages, catalog kinds) Tabs.vue (new): ARIA tablist, one line per tab (label + optional --ink-3 meta), 2px --focus underline on the active tab, arrow keys move, scrolls horizontally with edge fades local tablists, filter pills used as tabs. Choosing a value (Light/Dark, Month/Week) stays SegmentedControl Small floating surface anchored to a control (⋯ menus, pickers, the connection explainer) Popover.vue (new): anchored, flips at viewport edges, Escape/outside tap closes, focus returns, --elev-1, --radius-card, --z-popover; Menu.vue on top of it for action lists (items ≥ --touch-target, danger item last) per-feature popovers (SourceList ⋯, ThemePicker, ActionPicker, RegionViewOptions, ConnectionStatus) Colour ColourField.vue (new): the theme's --event-1…8 swatches first (radio group), then Custom… opening the native picker; shows the chosen swatch + name, never a raw hex field by default a bare <input type="color"> + hex text box

docs.title: 3.1 Building blocks for settings (the "new setting looks out of place" fix)
docs.text:
A new setting must look like every other setting, because it's built from the same blocks, with no CSS of its own. The blocks:

Block What it is Props that cover the variations SettingsSection eyebrow + panel; owns inset, dividers, rhythm title, id, #action slot (one secondary Button) SettingRow label · description · control label, description (or #description), stacked, #label-extra (a Tag) SettingGroup (new) a sub-heading inside a panel (--text-label, sentence case) + its rows; replaces uppercase in-card labels title ListRow / SourceList items with lead · body · actions lead, name, meta[], #actions ScopeLine (new, from KioskScope) "Same as Default" / "Changed here · Reset to default" overridden, @reset InlineNote (new) the one-line note/hint/error under a row (--text-meta; tone neutral/warn/err) tone, #action EmptyState, Button, Tag and the ui/ controls see the table above

Rules: 1. A settings category or tab component has no <style> block, or only layout for a genuinely new arrangement, which then becomes a block. controlLint and a new settingsNoStyle check (allowlist, shrinking) enforce it. 2. A new variation becomes a prop on the block, not a local class. If a spec needs something the blocks can't express, the spec says so and the block grows, with a gallery entry (below). 3. Plugin settings already work this way (schema → PluginFieldRenderer). Host settings now follow the same discipline.

Gallery. frontend/ui-gallery.html (dev-only entry, like renderer-gallery.html) renders every block and ui/ control in every state: - default, hover, focus, selected, disabled, error, loading, empty; - at 1280 and 390, in light and Backlit, with the theme switcher on top.

It's the reference a builder copies from and the page a reviewer opens. A Playwright snapshot of the gallery in CI makes any visual change to a block show up as a diff, so drift becomes visible in review instead of on the wall.

docs.title: 4. Layout rules
docs.text:
1. Panel inset: every direct child of a panel insets with --panel-pad-x / --panel-pad-y. A child that needs to bleed to the edge (a full-width list divider) does so explicitly, and only for its border.
  2. Dividers: 1px solid var(--line-soft) between panel children, never before the first or after the last. Panel owns this (.settings-section__panel > * + * { border-top }). Children don't draw their own outer dividers. This replaces ad-hoc rules like .where-shows + .setting-row.
  3. Row anatomy (SettingRow): label (--text-label, --weight-strong) over description (--text-meta, --ink-2), control on the right, --gap-group between them. It stacks under 600px or with :stacked. Descriptions are one sentence (copy rules).
  4. ListRow anatomy: lead · body · actions. The actions group never wraps internally. Under 600px the whole group moves under the body as one right-aligned line. (Today the ⋯ wraps alone; see #202.)
  5. Section rhythm: eyebrow title (--font-data, uppercase, letter-spaced, --ink-3) outside the panel, --gap-2 above the panel, --gap-section between sections. Eyebrows are only for section titles; inside a panel, sub-labels are --text-label sentence case.
  6. One primary per region: at most one primary Button per panel/dialog. "Add …" in a list header is secondary unless the list is empty, where the EmptyState's button is primary.
  7. Touch: every interactive element is ≥ --touch-target in both directions (use padding, not visual size).
  8. Widths: phone (< 600) one column with a 16px page gutter; kiosk/desktop as designed. No horizontal page scroll ever (the e2e phone audit enforces this).

docs.title: 5. Colour and state
docs.text:
State Treatment (all controls, via ui/) Hover surface --bg-2 → color-mix(--ink 4%, --bg-2); text unchanged Focus-visible outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px. Never removed, never colour-only Selected / on color-mix(in srgb, var(--focus) 16%, var(--bg-2)) fill + --focus border, or a filled --focus with --focus-ink text for segmented/toggle Primary action --focus fill, --focus-ink text Disabled opacity: .5, cursor: not-allowed, no hover change Loading label becomes the verb + "…" ("Saving…"), control disabled; no spinners in rows Error --err text line under the control (--text-meta), plus aria-invalid; never a red box Status Tag tones only (ok/warn/err)
  • Orange (--focus) is for primary actions, selection, focus and the ProgressBar fill only. Never use it for decoration, headings, dots that mean nothing, or links (links use --ink + underline).
  • Status colours never decorate. A plugin type, a category or a page is never coloured.
  • No blue. Calvin's palette has none, so a browser-default blue (checkbox, link) is a bug. Use accent-color: var(--focus).
  • Every view is checked in the 5 themes × light/dark (CLV-64 contrast test). Text pairs must hit AA.

docs.title: 6. Writing
docs.text: Follow the copy rules (settings audit §5) and the no-developer-words table (#193): sentence case, one-sentence descriptions, units on controls, plain words (screen, page, source, plugin, Calvin).

docs.title: 7. Enforcement
docs.text:
Tests (vitest, tests/unit/styles/): 1. tokenLint (exists): no literal colours, sizes or radii outside theme.css. 2. roleLint (new): components may not reference --fs-*, --space-* or --radius-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl,2xl} primitives, only roles. Allowlist shrinks per migration phase; it starts with today's files and must only shrink. 3. controlLint (new): in <style> blocks outside components/ui/, a selector that targets a button, input, select or a class containing btn|button may not set background, border, border-radius, font-size, font-weight, color or padding. Layout properties (margin, gap, grid, flex, width) are fine. Same shrinking allowlist. 4. panelInset (exists, #202), generalised: every component rendered as a direct panel child uses the inset tokens. 5. Weights: only --weight-* (no numeric font-weight outside theme.css).

Review: every UI PR attaches screenshots from the mocked e2e harness (tests/e2e/phone/fixtures/api-mock.js, no backend) at 1280 and 390, light and one dark theme. The design lead reviews against this doc.

docs.title: 8. Migration
docs.text:
1. Roles in, no visual change. Add the role tokens as aliases of today's primitives (radius snaps excepted) and add the lints with full allowlists. One PR, mechanical.
  2. The blocks and the gallery. Build Button, TextField, ListRow, SettingGroup, ScopeLine, InlineNote, Popover/Menu, ColourField, Tabs, the Dialog full size and ui-gallery.html first. Then replace the 61 button classes and remove settings <style> blocks file by file. The largest are Security (15 security-btn), Plugins (btn-install, pc-btn), System (maint-btn, backup-btn, update-btn) and Screens (kiosk-software__btn). Each file leaves the controlLint allowlist when done. Panel-owned dividers land here too.
  3. Roles everywhere. Swap primitives for roles per category (Content, Dashboard, Screens, Plugins, System, Security, then the dashboard). Each leaves the roleLint allowlist. Delete the unused primitives at the end.

Open question for the owner: the toggle knob in the "on" state is --focus-ink (near-black in light themes) since CLV-64. That's correct for contrast, but it reads heavy next to every other control. Keep it, or use a white knob with a darker track?

docs.title: Frontend consistency audit (2026-10-31)
docs.text: Owner request: "we need a proper FE audit on things like the .btn issue; it's not scalable." Method: frontend/scripts/ui-audit.py parses every .vue <style> block and template (126 files, dev/ excluded) and counts hand-rolled versions of shared patterns outside components/ui/. "Distinct looks" means distinct combinations of background / border / radius / padding / font-size / weight, i.e. how many visual variants exist. The script is in the repo, so these numbers can be re-run and must only go down. Target components and rules come from the frontend doctrine.

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
Pattern Hand-rolled rules Files Distinct looks Should be Priority Buttons 60 32 39 Button (4 variants × 2 sizes) + IconButton P1 Cards / panels / boxes 117 57 103 SettingsSection panel, ListRow, Card (--radius-card), dialogs P1 Notices / errors / hints / banners 57 33 33 InlineNote (neutral/warn/err/ok) + Banner (page-level) P1 Text inputs / selects 23 16 19 TextField, PasswordField, SelectPill, NumberStepper P1 Overlays / dialogs (position: fixed) 19 18 15 Dialog shell (title, body, actions, scrim, focus trap), Sheet, Popover; toasts stay in NotificationSystem P2 Headings 32 28 19 3 roles: section eyebrow, --text-title, SettingGroup label P2 Empty states 15 14 14 EmptyState (exists, under-used) P2 Tags / badges 9 6 9 Tag (CLV-51 left these) P3

Values that should be a short fixed set:

Thing Found Should be z-index values 28 distinct (0…10000, incl. 9999, 1003, 2100) 5 layers (--z-raised/sticky/dialog/osk/toast) box-shadow 51 distinct 2 (--elev-1, --elev-2) + focus rings font-weight 400, 500, 550, 600, 650, 700 400 / 500 / 600 Transition durations 10 (0.12s … 0.5s, 120ms, 180ms) --dur-fast 120ms, --dur 200ms Breakpoints 479, 480, 600, 720, 768px 600 (phone) and 1024 (wide), via one mixin or container queries Raw spacing (padding/margin/gap without tokens) 627 declarations role tokens (--gap-*, --panel-pad-*) Native controls outside ui/ 62 <input>, 15 checkboxes, 5 number, 3 <select>, 2 colour, 1 textarea wrapped ui/ controls; native only inside them Emoji used as icons in templates 17 in 16 files mdi icons (emoji render differently per OS and kiosk font) Settings files with their own <style> 62 layout-only, then none (doctrine §3.1)

Re-implemented components: 5 files build their own switch, 2 their own tabs, 4 their own modal and 3 their own popover or menu. 9 files implement role="dialog" separately: ConnectionStatus popover, ThemePicker, AdminSignInDialog, EmbedOverlay, HandoffOverlay, ActionPicker, ScreenRegionEditor, ProviderPicker, Settings.

docs.title: 2. What this means
docs.text:
• Every new feature re-solves "what does a button / box / error look like". With 39 button looks and 103 box looks, any new setting is guaranteed to differ from its neighbours. Specs can't prevent it, because there is nothing to point at.
  • Tokens didn't fix it. Most of these rules already use tokens. The variation is in which token and which combination. Shared components fix that; more tokens don't.
  • Overlays are a correctness risk, not just looks. 28 z-index values and 9 dialog implementations are how the OSK/dialog stacking bugs (CLV-9 review) happened. Each dialog also re-implements its own focus trap and Escape handling.

docs.title: 3. Plan (maps onto the doctrine's migration)
docs.text:
P1: the shared blocks, then the worst files. 1. Build in components/ui/, each with a gallery entry (ui-gallery.html) and unit tests: - Button (primary / secondary / ghost / danger / link; md / sm; icon; loading); - TextField; - InlineNote (tones); - Card; - ListRow; - Dialog (title, body, actions, scrim, focus trap, Escape, --z-dialog, OSK-aware via dialog-above-osk). 2. Add the lints with today's offenders as a shrinking allowlist: controlLint (buttons and inputs), roleLint (z-index, shadow, weight, duration literals and primitives), settingsNoStyle. 3. Migrate one category per PR, worst first (matrix below): Plugins (installer, InstanceModal, picker), the page editor and its inspectors, Screens, the sign-in dialog and lock screen, Security, System, Content, then the dashboard surfaces. Each PR deletes the file's local control styles and removes it from the allowlists, with before/after shots from the mocked e2e harness at 1280 and 390.

P2: Dialog adoption for the 9 dialog implementations; EmptyState everywhere; headings to 3 roles; z-index, shadow, weight and duration to the fixed sets; one breakpoint set.

P3: remaining badges to Tag; emoji → mdi; native controls wrapped.

Done when ui-audit.py reports, outside components/ui/: - 0 hand-rolled buttons, inputs, notices and dialogs; - ≤ 3 distinct card looks (panel, list row, card); - ≤ 5 z-index values and ≤ 2 shadows; - 0 settings <style> blocks beyond layout.

The script output goes into each migration PR description.

docs.title: Cycle A — Design Foundation Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Build the reusable visual/interaction foundation (tokens, themeable fonts, the focus-light primitive, and the touch-control component kit) that the dashboard (cycle B) and Settings (cycle C) rebuilds will both consume.

Architecture: Pure frontend, no surface rewired and no backend changes. Extend the existing CSS-variable theming (theme.css + useTheme.js) with semantic color tokens and font-role tokens; self-host the type-theme fonts; ship four new reusable Vue components and one composable. Existing components keep working because new color tokens alias the old ones.

Tech Stack: Vue 3 (Composition API, <script setup>), Vite, Pinia, Vitest + @vue/test-utils (jsdom), CSS custom properties.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Do not change keyboard behavior — no edits to useKeyboardActions.js or the action vocabulary. (Cycle A touches no input handling at all.)
  • Themeable identity — color and type are both theme-controlled via CSS custom properties on document.documentElement; never hardcode a hex or a font family in a component.
  • Nordic coverage — every shipped font face must cover Latin Extended-A (å ä ö æ ø).
  • Tabular data — the --font-data face must have tabular figures.
  • Offline-first — fonts are self-hosted woff2; no runtime CDN dependency.
  • Touch targets — interactive controls are ≥ 44px (default 46–48px).
  • Quality floor — preserve :focus-visible outlines (the 24" unit is keyboard-driven) and respect prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Test runner — npx vitest run <file> for a single spec; tests live in tests/unit/components/.
  • Commit trailer — end every commit message with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs.title: Task 1: Semantic color + focus + font-role tokens
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: frontend/src/styles/theme.css

Interfaces: - Produces: CSS custom properties available app-wide — --bg-0 --bg-1 --bg-2 --line --line-soft --ink --ink-2 --ink-3 --focus --focus-ink --focus-glow --focus-edge --ok --warn --err and --font-display --font-ui --font-data. Components in later tasks consume these.

docs.title: Task 2: Self-host type-theme fonts (via @fontsource, OFL-1.1)
docs.text:
Files: - Modify: frontend/package.json (+ package-lock.json) — add @fontsource/* deps - Create: frontend/src/styles/fonts.js — imports the needed weight CSS - Create: frontend/src/assets/fonts/LICENSES/*.LICENSE — vendored OFL texts - Modify: frontend/src/main.js

docs.title: Task 3: Type-theme registry + useTypeTheme composable
docs.text:
Files: - Create: frontend/src/styles/typeThemes.js - Create: frontend/src/composables/useTypeTheme.js - Test: frontend/tests/unit/composables/useTypeTheme.spec.js

Interfaces: - Consumes: nothing from earlier tasks (font stacks are self-contained strings). - Produces: - typeThemes.js: TYPE_THEMES (object keyed by 'instrument'|'marquee'|'station', each { display, ui, data } CSS font-family strings), DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME = 'instrument', isTypeTheme(id) → boolean. - useTypeTheme() → { current (Ref<string>), applyTypeTheme(id) → void, loadTypeTheme() → void }. applyTypeTheme sets --font-display/--font-ui/--font-data on document.documentElement, updates current, and persists to localStorage['calvin-type-theme']; an unknown id falls back to DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME.

  • [ ] Step 1: Write the registry

Create frontend/src/styles/typeThemes.js:

export const TYPE_THEMES = {
  instrument: {
    display: '"IBM Plex Sans Condensed", system-ui, sans-serif',
    ui: '"IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, sans-serif',
    data: '"IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace',
  },
  marquee: {
    display: '"Space Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif',
    ui: '"Inter", system-ui, sans-serif',
    data: '"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace',
  },
  station: {
    display: '"Schibsted Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif',
    ui: '"Schibsted Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif',
    data: '"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace',
  },
};

export const DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME = "instrument";

export const isTypeTheme = id => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(TYPE_THEMES, id);
  • [ ] Step 2: Write the failing test

Create frontend/tests/unit/composables/useTypeTheme.spec.js:

import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import { useTypeTheme } from "@/composables/useTypeTheme";

describe("useTypeTheme", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    document.documentElement.removeAttribute("style");
    localStorage.clear();
  });

  it("applies the requested theme's font roles to :root", () => {
    const { applyTypeTheme, current } = useTypeTheme();
    applyTypeTheme("marquee");
    const root = document.documentElement;
    expect(root.style.getPropertyValue("--font-display")).toContain("Space Grotesk");
    expect(root.style.getPropertyValue("--font-ui")).toContain("Inter");
    expect(root.style.getPropertyValue("--font-data")).toContain("JetBrains Mono");
    expect(current.value).toBe("marquee");
    expect(localStorage.getItem("calvin-type-theme")).toBe("marquee");
  });

  it("falls back to instrument for an unknown id", () => {
    const { applyTypeTheme, current } = useTypeTheme();
    applyTypeTheme("nonsense");
    expect(current.value).toBe("instrument");
    expect(document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue("--font-display")).toContain("Plex Sans Condensed");
  });

  it("loadTypeTheme restores the persisted choice", () => {
    localStorage.setItem("calvin-type-theme", "station");
    const { loadTypeTheme, current } = useTypeTheme();
    loadTypeTheme();
    expect(current.value).toBe("station");
  });
});
  • [ ] Step 3: Run test to verify it fails

Run: cd frontend && npx vitest run tests/unit/composables/useTypeTheme.spec.js Expected: FAIL — cannot resolve @/composables/useTypeTheme.

  • [ ] Step 4: Write the composable

Create frontend/src/composables/useTypeTheme.js:

import { ref } from "vue";
import { TYPE_THEMES, DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME, isTypeTheme } from "@/styles/typeThemes";

const STORAGE_KEY = "calvin-type-theme";

export function useTypeTheme() {
  const current = ref(DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME);

  const applyTypeTheme = id => {
    const themeId = isTypeTheme(id) ? id : DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME;
    const { display, ui, data } = TYPE_THEMES[themeId];
    const root = document.documentElement;
    root.style.setProperty("--font-display", display);
    root.style.setProperty("--font-ui", ui);
    root.style.setProperty("--font-data", data);
    current.value = themeId;
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, themeId);
    } catch {
      /* storage unavailable — non-fatal */
    }
  };

  const loadTypeTheme = () => {
    let id = DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME;
    try {
      id = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) || DEFAULT_TYPE_THEME;
    } catch {
      /* storage unavailable */
    }
    applyTypeTheme(id);
  };

  return { current, applyTypeTheme, loadTypeTheme };
}

docs.title: Task 5: SegmentedControl
docs.text:
Files: - Create: frontend/src/components/ui/SegmentedControl.vue - Test: frontend/tests/unit/components/ui/SegmentedControl.spec.js

Interfaces: - Consumes: color/focus tokens (Task 1). - Produces: <SegmentedControl v-model="value" :options="[{value,label,icon?}]" :aria-label="str" />. Renders role="radiogroup"; each option is a role="radio" button with aria-checked, the selected one also carrying class on. Clicking an option emits update:modelValue. Left/Up and Right/Down arrows move and emit. Only the selected button is in the tab order (roving tabindex).

  • [ ] Step 1: Write the failing test

Create frontend/tests/unit/components/ui/SegmentedControl.spec.js:

import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { mount } from "@vue/test-utils";
import SegmentedControl from "@/components/ui/SegmentedControl.vue";

const OPTS = [
  { value: "landscape", label: "Landscape" },
  { value: "portrait", label: "Portrait" },
];

describe("SegmentedControl", () => {
  it("marks the selected option with aria-checked and class", () => {
    const w = mount(SegmentedControl, { props: { modelValue: "landscape", options: OPTS } });
    const btns = w.findAll('[role="radio"]');
    expect(btns).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(btns[0].attributes("aria-checked")).toBe("true");
    expect(btns[0].classes()).toContain("on");
    expect(btns[1].attributes("aria-checked")).toBe("false");
  });

  it("emits update:modelValue on click", async () => {
    const w = mount(SegmentedControl, { props: { modelValue: "landscape", options: OPTS } });
    await w.findAll('[role="radio"]')[1].trigger("click");
    expect(w.emitted("update:modelValue")[0]).toEqual(["portrait"]);
  });

  it("moves selection with ArrowRight", async () => {
    const w = mount(SegmentedControl, { props: { modelValue: "landscape", options: OPTS } });
    await w.find('[role="radiogroup"]').trigger("keydown", { key: "ArrowRight" });
    expect(w.emitted("update:modelValue")[0]).toEqual(["portrait"]);
  });
});

  • [ ] Step 3: Write the component

Create frontend/src/components/ui/SegmentedControl.vue:

<template>
  <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" :aria-label="ariaLabel" @keydown="onKey">
    <button
      v-for="(o, i) in options"
      :key="o.value"
      :ref="el => setRef(el, i)"
      type="button"
      role="radio"
      class="seg__btn"
      :class="{ on: o.value === modelValue }"
      :aria-checked="o.value === modelValue ? 'true' : 'false'"
      :tabindex="o.value === modelValue ? 0 : -1"
      @click="select(o.value)"
    >
      <span v-if="o.icon" class="seg__ic" aria-hidden="true">{{ o.icon }}</span>
      {{ o.label }}
    </button>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";

const props = defineProps({
  modelValue: { type: [String, Number], default: null },
  options: { type: Array, required: true },
  ariaLabel: { type: String, default: null },
});
const emit = defineEmits(["update:modelValue"]);

const refs = ref([]);
const setRef = (el, i) => {
  if (el) refs.value[i] = el;
};

const select = v => {
  if (v !== props.modelValue) emit("update:modelValue", v);
};

const onKey = e => {
  const idx = props.options.findIndex(o => o.value === props.modelValue);
  if (idx < 0) return;
  let n = idx;
  if (e.key === "ArrowRight" || e.key === "ArrowDown") n = (idx + 1) % props.options.length;
  else if (e.key === "ArrowLeft" || e.key === "ArrowUp")
    n = (idx - 1 + props.options.length) % props.options.length;
  else return;
  e.preventDefault();
  emit("update:modelValue", props.options[n].value);
  refs.value[n]?.focus();
};
</script>

<style scoped>

  background: var(--bg-0);
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 11px;
  padding: 4px;
}

  font-size: 14px;
  font-weight: 500;
  color: var(--ink-2);
  background: transparent;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 10px 18px;
  min-height: 44px;
  cursor: pointer;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 7px;
}

  color: var(--focus-ink);
}

  outline: 2px solid var(--focus);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

<template>
  <div class="pill-wrap">
    <button
      type="button"
      class="pill"
      :aria-expanded="open ? 'true' : 'false'"
      aria-haspopup="listbox"

      <span class="pill__cv" aria-hidden="true">▾</span>
    </button>
    <ul v-if="open" class="pill__menu" role="listbox">
      <li
        v-for="o in options"
        :key="o.value"
        role="option"
        class="pill__opt"
        :aria-selected="o.value === modelValue ? 'true' : 'false'"
        @click="choose(o.value)"
      >
        {{ o.label }}
      </li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref, computed } from "vue";

const props = defineProps({
  modelValue: { type: [String, Number], default: null },
  options: { type: Array, required: true },
  swatch: { type: String, default: null },
});
const emit = defineEmits(["update:modelValue"]);

const open = ref(false);
const currentLabel = computed(
  () => props.options.find(o => o.value === props.modelValue)?.label ?? ""
);
const choose = v => {
  emit("update:modelValue", v);
  open.value = false;
};
</script>
