  • ✅ Version control separately but coordinate releases

This setup gives you the flexibility to develop plugins independently while maintaining a clean separation between core and plugins.

docs.title: Theme package format (theme_api 2)
docs.text:
A Calvin theme is a palette family, not a skin. It changes colours and nothing else: layout, spacing, radii, typography and z-index stay the host's, and light/dark remains the mode setting. A theme therefore ships one light palette and one dark palette, and never fights "Follow device" or "On a schedule".

The installer validates a package at install; the host validates every bundled and installed theme again on every startup. Both use the same rules in app/services/theme_contract.py.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
{theme_id}/
  theme.json       # required: manifest + both palettes
  preview.(png|jpg|webp)   # optional: picker image

theme.json:

{
  "id": "midnight",
  "name": "Midnight",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "theme_api": 2,
  "description": "Violet on night blue.",
  "variables": { "...light palette..." },
  "dark_mode": { "...dark palette..." }
}

id must be a lowercase slug (it names the directory under themes/). theme_api is optional but recommended: a package without it is checked by the same rules. A package declaring a newer theme_api than this Calvin supports is rejected.

docs.title: Colours only
docs.text:
A theme may set only these keys. Any other key (gap-4, radius-lg, z-modal, font-ui, or the retired bg-primary / accent-primary / calendar-* / text-* names) is ignored and logged; it is never written to the page.

Group Keys Surfaces / ink bg-0, bg-1, bg-2, ink, ink-2, ink-3, line, line-soft Accent focus Status ok, warn, err Text on a tone focus-ink, focus-text, ok-ink, ok-text, warn-ink, warn-text, err-ink, err-text Elevation shadow, shadow-hover Calendar (optional) event-1 … event-8

Required in both modes (14 base colours): bg-0, bg-1, bg-2, ink, ink-2, ink-3, line, line-soft, focus, ok, warn, err, shadow, shadow-hover.

Derived if missing (8 pairs): focus/ok/warn/err × -ink / -text. The host derives them at install and stores them:

  • -ink is --ink or --bg-1, whichever clears WCAG AA on the tone;
  • -text is the tone mixed toward --ink until it clears AA on --bg-1.

Ship the pairs yourself if you prefer; they are checked the same way.

event-1…8 fall back to Calvin's palette when omitted.

docs.title: Value syntax
docs.text: #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb(), rgba(), hsl() and hsla() only. var(), url(), calc(), expression(), named keywords and any other value shape are rejected — a theme cannot reach layout tokens or inject a resource.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
At install a package is rejected when:

  • a base colour is missing (the error names the key and mode);
  • a value does not parse as one of the allowed shapes;
  • ink / ink-2 / ink-3 is below AA on bg-1;
  • a -text pair is below AA on bg-1, or a -ink pair is below AA on its tone.

The message is user-facing, for example: Midnight can't be installed: it's missing bg-2 in dark mode.

At load (every startup, bundled and installed themes) the same checks run. A theme that now fails is kept but marked unselectable; if it was selected, Calvin falls back to its own palette in the current mode and the picker shows the theme disabled with "Needs an update to work with this Calvin."

The status hue rule is a warning for third-party themes, not a rejection: focus ↔ ok / err ≥ 25°, warn ↔ err ≥ 25°, focus ↔ warn ≥ 12° (the accent must never look like a warning). When a theme fails it still installs and the picker adds "Status colours may be hard to tell apart in this theme." Themes in the official catalog must pass every rule in that repository's CI.

docs.title: Applying
docs.text: useTheme writes the allowlisted keys of the palette for the current mode onto :root, and removes them when Calvin is selected. It also re-checks the value syntax as a last line of defence, so a hand-edited theme.json cannot inject a var() or url().

docs.title: Overnight Audit Prompt
docs.text:
A ready-to-paste prompt for an unattended, hours-long audit of Calvin by a powerful orchestrator model (Fable). It delegates almost all reading/reproduction to cheaper subagent models, adversarially verifies every finding, and files beads only — no product-code changes. Hand it to the agent as-is; fill in <date>.

Design choices: - File beads only — pure audit, safe to leave running unattended. - Adversarial verification — each finding must survive a refuter subagent before it becomes a bead, to avoid a morning pile of hallucinated issues. - Model-tiered delegation — Fable (orchestrator) spends its scarce tokens on judgment and writing beads; haiku scans, sonnet analyzes/refutes, opus is the escalation for genuinely hard reasoning only. - Focus — correctness bugs → UX/visual polish → new features (priority order). - Triage — every bead is labelled overnight-audit for a single morning triage view (bd list --label overnight-audit).

You are the orchestrator for an unattended overnight audit of Calvin, a self-hosted
Raspberry Pi dashboard (Vue 3 frontend + FastAPI backend + plugin system). You will run
alone for hours. Your job is to produce a high-signal backlog of beads (issues) for bugs,
UX/visual problems, and genuinely useful new features. You do NOT change product code.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
GROUND RULES (read fully before doing anything)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. OUTPUT IS BEADS ONLY. Do not edit, fix, or refactor product code. The only things you
   may write are: beads (via `bd`), and throwaway files under the scratchpad dir for your
   own notes / repro harnesses. No commits to product source.

2. WORK IN AN ISOLATED BRANCH. Create and stay on `audit/overnight-<date>` off `main`.
   Anything you scribble (notes, repro scripts) lives there or in scratchpad. Never push,
   never open a PR, never touch other branches.

3. TOKEN BUDGET IS THE HARD CONSTRAINT. You (Fable, the powerful orchestrator) cannot run
   long. Treat your own context as scarce. Your tokens are for JUDGMENT, DEDUP, and WRITING
   BEADS — not for reading files. DELEGATE all scanning, reading, reproduction, and
   first-pass analysis to subagents, matching the model to the difficulty of the task:
     • Broad file scanning / mapping            → Agent(subagent_type: "Explore",  model: "haiku")
     • Deeper single-area analysis / repro      → Agent(subagent_type: "general-purpose", model: "sonnet")
     • Adversarial verification (see below)     → Agent(subagent_type: "general-purpose", model: "sonnet")
     • Genuinely hard reasoning (subtle races,  → Agent(subagent_type: "general-purpose", model: "opus")
       tricky contract logic, high-stakes refute)
   Use opus only when a task is too hard for sonnet — it's your "smarter subagent" escalation,
   not the default. Reserve yourself (Fable) for: planning the sweep, triaging returned
   findings, killing duplicates/false-positives, and composing final bead text. Prefer many
   small, well-scoped subagent tasks that return STRUCTURED findings (not file dumps) over
   reading yourself. Launch independent subagents in parallel (multiple Agent calls in one
   message).

4. EVERY FINDING MUST SURVIVE ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION BEFORE IT BECOMES A BEAD.
   After a finding is discovered, dispatch a SEPARATE subagent whose explicit job is to
   REFUTE it: reproduce it, find the code path that already handles it, or prove it's
   intended behavior. Default to "not real" when uncertain. A finding becomes a bead only if
   the refuter fails to kill it. Bugs must be reproduced (in-app via Playwright, or by citing
   the exact failing code path + inputs). This is how we avoid a morning pile of hallucinated
   issues — quality over quantity.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ENVIRONMENT & COMMANDS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• Read CLAUDE.md (root) first — it's the developer guide. Run `bd prime` for issue-tracker
  workflow, existing memories, and session rules. Skim existing beads (`bd ready`,
  `bd list`) so you don't file duplicates of known work.
• Run the app for live/UX testing: `make dev` (frontend Vite + FastAPI backend; check
  `make help` for ports/logs, `make dev-logs-read` for logs, `make dev-down` to stop).
  Use the Playwright MCP tools to drive the UI, take snapshots/screenshots, and reproduce
  UX and visual issues. Also exercise the RPi kiosk / touch context, not just desktop.
• Tests/quality signals you may RUN (read-only, to surface gaps or reproduce): `make test`,
  `make test-backend`, `make test-frontend`, `make lint`, `make type-check`. Failing or
  missing tests are themselves findings.
• Plugins live in ../calvin-plugins/. The plugin contract (1.0) is central — bugs in the
  loader, instance manager, renderers, or contract enforcement are high value.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHERE TO SPEND EFFORT (in priority order)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A. CORRECTNESS BUGS — backend/frontend logic errors, race conditions (note the SQLite
   "database is locked" / retry_on_db_locked pattern), error handling, edge cases, the
   plugin contract, config normalization, cache/TTL fallback paths, API/store mismatches.
B. UX & VISUAL POLISH — use Playwright. Interaction rough edges, accessibility, responsive
   behavior, the RPi kiosk/touch experience, theme correctness (note: in light theme
   --bg-2 == --bg-1 == #fff and --focus is orange, not blue — verify against real tokens),
   settings flows, empty/error/loading states.
C. NEW FEATURES — be genuinely creative but grounded. Propose features that fit Calvin's
   vision as a self-hosted, glanceable, kiosk dashboard for calendars/photos/web services.
   Each feature bead must include: the user problem, why it fits Calvin, a rough shape of
   the implementation, and which existing pattern/extension point it builds on (prefer
   schema-driven plugin extensions over new one-offs). No generic "add AI" filler — real,
   usable ideas someone would actually want on their wall display.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SUGGESTED FLOW
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Orient: read CLAUDE.md, `bd prime`, list existing beads. Decide a sweep plan carving the
   codebase into ~8–15 independent zones (backend routes, plugin loader/instance manager,
   renderers, each Pinia store, calendar view, settings, keyboard, image pipeline, main.css
   vocabulary, plugin contract tests, etc.).
2. Fan out haiku Explore agents over the zones → each returns a STRUCTURED list of candidate
   findings (type, location file:line, one-line claim, severity guess). No prose dumps.
3. Triage returned candidates yourself: drop obvious noise and duplicates, cluster related
   ones.
4. For surviving candidates, dispatch sonnet subagents to (a) deep-analyze / reproduce and
   (b) adversarially refute (escalate to opus if the refutation is genuinely hard). Run a
   parallel Playwright-driven UX pass for category B.
5. Only confirmed survivors become beads. Write them yourself.
6. Loop until zones are covered and 2 consecutive discovery rounds yield nothing new, or
   your budget runs low — whichever first. If you must stop early, prioritize A > B > C.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BEAD FORMAT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• File with `bd create` (run `bd create --help` for exact flags). Set a sensible type
  (bug/feature/task/chore) and priority.
• Label every bead from this run `overnight-audit` so the maintainer can triage them as a
  batch in the morning.
• Each bead must contain: a crisp title; the affected file:line or UI location; for bugs —
  concrete repro steps or the failing input/path and expected vs actual; for features — the
  problem/fit/shape as described above; and a one-line note on HOW it was verified (repro,
  code-path, or refuter-survived). Link related beads.
• Do NOT file: things already covered by existing open beads, pure style nits without user
  impact, or anything you couldn't get past the refuter — instead just drop those.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
HOUSE RULES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• No Claude attribution anywhere (this repo strips it) — but you aren't committing anyway.
• Stay self-contained; respect the plugin architecture (no cross-plugin imports, schema-
  driven UI first). Check the CLAUDE.md "Gotchas" list before calling weird behavior a bug.
• Leave the repo clean: on `audit/overnight-<date>`, no product-code diffs, dev server
  stopped (`make dev-down`).

When done, print a summary: beads filed (by category), zones covered, anything skipped for
budget, and the 3 findings you're most confident matter.

docs.title: WPE WebKit + cog as the Pi 3 kiosk browser
docs.text:
Research date: 2026-10-29 Bead: calvin-8by7 (test matrix; not closed by this document) Scope: desk research plus an on-host WebKit compatibility run. No product code, scripts, units or services were changed. Nothing was installed on, or measured against, a real Raspberry Pi.

Status (2026-10-31): implemented as the kiosk default on EVERY board. auto in the kiosk installer now resolves to cog everywhere; only an explicit --display-stack x11 selects Chromium and only an explicit wayland selects labwc. An explicit --display-stack x11|wayland|cog always wins over auto, and a re-run keeps an existing kiosk's recorded stack (existing X11 kiosks are not migrated silently). Owner decision after on-hardware verification on a Pi 3B+ and a Pi 400: install, boot/reboot, rotation via the display agent, screen off/on, real sites in WPE and a 60 min soak (cog ~67 MB + WPE ~273 MB, CPU ~94 % idle). The A/B numbers in §5 are still unmeasured, and the caveats below (native <select>, WPE security horizon, no runtime rotation API) still apply.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Superseded 2026-10-31 by the status above. This section records the original 2026-10-29 conclusion and the evidence it rested on; the decision to make cog the default on every board was taken later after hardware verification. Do not replace Chromium on the Pi 3B+ yet. Run the A/B in §5 first, and keep Chromium as the default until it produces numbers.

The case for cog is real and better than for any compositor swap: one apt install on Trixie Lite gives a DRM/KMS browser with no X, no Wayland compositor, and no Chromium GPU stack — exactly the three layers that are either heavy or broken on the Pi 3 today (calvin-scuh: Chromium 156 must run with --disable-gpu because its GPU path crashes the VC4 renderer). WPE's own hardware table lists Raspberry Pi 3 / VideoCore IV / Mesa vc4 / cog drm and wl as a validated configuration, Debian trixie ships everything you need, and Calvin's frontend boots, renders, opens Settings, registers its service worker and types through the on-screen keyboard in a WebKit engine with zero console errors (§4).

What holds it back is not compatibility, it is evidence:

  1. No memory win is proven, and there is a warning sign. Nobody has published a Pi 3-class cog memory figure. The only number this research produced (§4.5) is from x86_64 and shows WebKit above Chromium for the same page (981 MB vs 536 MB summed RSS). Different engine build, different architecture — but it is enough to say "cog is lighter" is an assumption, not a fact.
  2. Calvin loses two runtime controls. Under cog-DRM there is no xrandr/wlr-randr and no wlopm: rotation is fixed at cog start (renderer=gles,rotation=N, needs a restart to change) and panel power has no supported path (test vcgencmd display_power; otherwise CEC or the monitor's own schedule). Today's display agent assumes one of those tools.
  3. A real UI gap upstream: native <select> dropdowns do not open under cog's DRM backend (upstream issues #793 and #503, both open). Calvin uses <select> in plugin config, the calendar-source form and the update tab (§4.3). The kiosk can still be configured from a phone ("Use your phone"), but Settings-on-the-panel is degraded.
  4. Maintenance: Debian trixie's wpewebkit is 2.48.3, and Debian's security tracker currently lists many WebKit CVEs for trixie as vulnerable (no DSA, ignored), while Raspberry Pi ships a current Chromium. Upstream calls cog a legacy launcher (pre-2.54 API) that new projects should replace with a small WPEPlatform launcher.

The decision rule: adopt cog for Pi 3B+ SPLIT only if the §5 A/B shows ≥150 MB lower steady-state memory after one hour, first paint no worse than Chromium's baseline, and 24 h without an unplanned restart — and if we accept that orientation/panel-power become a restart/vcgencmd/CEC story or we move that kiosk to the labwc variant (cog -P wl under labwc keeps wlopm). Otherwise stay on Chromium and revisit when Debian 14 ships WPE 2.54 with the built-in DRM platform.

For Pi 4/5 this question is much less interesting: they can afford Chromium and a compositor, and the Wayland research (2026-10-29-kiosk-wayland.md) already covers them.

docs.title: 1.1 What is in Debian 13 (trixie) arm64
docs.text:
Package trixie arm64 What it is cog 0.18.4-1+b1 (source 0.18.4-1) launcher; ships cog, cogctl and the platform modules libwpewebkit-2.0-1 2.48.3-1 the WPE WebKit engine (shared library + web/network processes) libwpe-1.0-1 1.16.2-1 legacy embedding library libwpebackend-fdo-1.0-1 1.16.0-1 legacy FreeDesktop backend (EGL/GBM buffer export) wpewebkit-driver 2.48.3-1 (arch all) WebDriver, for automated testing

Versions from Debian madison and packages.debian.org/trixie/cog (checked 2026-10-29).

The DRM/KMS platform plugin is included. The arm64 file list is:

/usr/bin/cog
/usr/bin/cogctl
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/cog/modules/libcogplatform-drm.so
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/cog/modules/libcogplatform-headless.so
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/cog/modules/libcogplatform-wl.so
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libcogcore.so.9.2.7

(file list). That is cog's default build set (drm, headless, wayland). There is no X11 platform module, so "cog inside the current X11/openbox kiosk" is not an option with Debian's package — cog would need to run on DRM or under Wayland.

Debian's build of the engine is -DPORT=WPE with the Bubblewrap sandbox on (ENABLE_BUBBLEWRAP_SANDBOX=ON) and Skia left at its default per wpewebkit 2.48.3-1 debian/rules. cog itself has only Depends: (no Recommends), so nothing pulls GStreamer plugins or fonts for you.

docs.title: 1.2 What is in the Raspberry Pi archive
docs.text:
Nothing. http://archive.raspberrypi.com/debian/dists/trixie/main/binary-arm64/Packages.gz (1,477 binary packages, fetched 2026-10-29) contains no cog, wpewebkit, libwpe or libwpewebkit package. The only WPE-named packages are gstreamer1.0-wpe and its -dbgsym, which are GStreamer's WPE sink/source plugin, not a browser engine — do not confuse the two.

So on Raspberry Pi OS Trixie the packages come from Debian's trixie/arm64 archive (Debian 13 is what Pi OS Trixie is built on), and Raspberry Pi does not test or patch them. Practical consequence: the Pi gets Debian's 2.48.3, not the Raspberry Pi-patched Chromium it gets today, including Debian's security posture (§1.3) and Debian's feature set.

docs.title: 1.3 Version and security horizon
docs.text:
• cog 0.18.4 is upstream's May 2024 release; trixie's cog saw one binary rebuild (+b1) and nothing else. Debian 14 (forky) and sid carry 0.18.5 with WPE 2.54 — i.e. cog stays at 0.18.x for trixie's whole life.
  • WPE 2.48's last upstream point release is 2.48.6; trixie has 2.48.3, so any later security fixes have to come from Debian.
  • Debian's security tracker for wpewebkit shows, for trixie, a large number of WebKit CVEs marked vulnerable (no DSA, ignored) at the time of checking (forky/sid show fixed). That is not a bug in our plan, it is a property of the package; it is the strongest non-technical argument for keeping Chromium, which Raspberry Pi rebuilds regularly.
  • Upstream WPE FAQ calls cog the legacy launcher: "kept for existing deployments, but new projects do not need it". Since 2.54 the DRM/Wayland/headless platforms live inside WPE WebKit itself (WPE_PLATFORM=drm) and a launcher is ~30 lines of C. A future Pi OS (Debian 14) migration will be a small custom launcher, not cog.

docs.title: 2.1 DRM/KMS, no compositor (the interesting variant)
docs.text:
Yes, and it is a supported configuration. WPE's supported-hardware table lists exactly our target:

Raspberry Pi 3 · VideoCore IV · Mesa vc4 · backend fdo · Cog platforms wl, drm, headless

The DRM platform docs add the requirements (WPEBackend-fdo, Wayland client libs, GLESv2, libdrm, libgbm, libinput, libudev — all pulled in by the package) and the knobs:

Need How Select the platform cog --platform=drm (or COG_PLATFORM_NAME=drm) Resolution / refresh COG_PLATFORM_DRM_VIDEO_MODE=1920x1080, COG_PLATFORM_DRM_MODE_MAX=1920x1080@60; default = preferred mode of the first connected output Fullscreen inherent — there is no window, just a CRTC Rotation only with --platform-params=renderer=gles,rotation=1 (1 = 90° CCW, 3 = 270°). The default renderer=modeset attaches frames directly and cannot rotate Cursor hidden by default; COG_PLATFORM_DRM_CURSOR=1 draws a hardware cursor sprite (and implies pointer events) Pointer off by default; COG_PLATFORM_DRM_POINTER=1 forwards motion/buttons/scroll Touch + keyboard always forwarded (libinput), independent of the pointer options

Operational requirements that are easy to miss:

  • DRM master + input access. cog opens the KMS device and calls drmModeSetCrtc (platform/drm/cog-drm-modeset-renderer.c), so it needs to be DRM master; and libinput needs to read /dev/input/event*. On Pi OS Lite the reliable recipe is running the unit as root; the alternative (user in video + input groups) depends on no other master existing and on udev /dev/input permissions — UNVERIFIED on this image, check with ls -l /dev/dri/card0 /dev/input/event* and id.
  • The seat is hard-coded to seat0 in 0.18.4 (libinput_udev_assign_seat(..., "seat0"), platform/drm/cog-platform-drm.c:1259). Fine on a Pi; would break on a multi-seat setup.
  • The kernel console is on the same CRTC. Stop getty@tty1 in the unit (Conflicts=getty@tty1.service) so boot messages and the getty do not flash over/under the page.
  • Rotation and touch. 0.18.1 fixed touch-region dimensions for 90°/270° (NEWS) and 0.18.4 tries to set libinput's per-device rotation to match (libinput_device_config_rotation_set_angle, cog-platform-drm.c:1019). Many touch drivers do not support device rotation, in which case the call is skipped; finger positions then have to be checked on the actual panel. On the Pi 3 that means: test all four orientations with a tap target, not just the picture.
  • Rotation is a startup property. It can be changed at runtime through the CogDrmPlatform:rotation GObject property, but cog exposes no D-Bus action for it, so in practice changing orientation = rewrite the unit's platform-params and systemctl restart. (Calvin's display agent currently rotates with xrandr/wlr-randr at runtime.)
  • Known upstream DRM bugs in this release line: #748 (0.18.4 + DRM + GLES: "Cannot create framebuffer (Bad file descriptor)", fd exhaustion after a few seconds), #794 (open PR: DRM cold start / SHM robustness / cursor fixes for compositor-less boots, i.e. released 0.18 is known to be fragile exactly on "boot straight into cog"). Neither is confirmed on VC4, but both are the same shape of failure we must watch for in the first ten boots.

docs.title: 2.2 Wayland (labwc)
docs.text:
Also supported (-P wl, module present). Requirements from the wl platform docs:

  • compositor running first, with WAYLAND_DISPLAY and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR in the service environment, and access to /dev/dri (render node is enough here);
  • COG_PLATFORM_WL_VIEW_FULLSCREEN=1 for a real fullscreen surface (it is a request; labwc honours it);
  • F11 toggles fullscreen — with a USB keyboard attached that can un-fullscreen the kiosk. On a touch-only wall there is no way to press it.
  • input, touch and cursor belong to labwc. Cursor hiding is the same problem as Chromium today (one-shot HideCursor + WarpCursor, reappears on touch), i.e. worse than cog-DRM, which never draws one.
  • rotation is the compositor's job (wlr-randr --transform), so the existing agent code path and wlopm panel power keep working. That is the main reason to prefer this variant if the panel-power schedule matters.
  • cog's own D-Bus control is on the session bus by default (cog_dbus_control=user, upstream default; Debian does not flip it, and the package ships no system-bus policy), so cogctl only works when cog runs inside a user session with a session bus — under labwc, if dbus-user-session is installed. UNVERIFIED on Pi OS Lite; do not build a watchdog on it.

docs.title: 2.3 Which needs what — summary
docs.text: DRM/KMS (-P drm) Wayland (-P wl, labwc) Compositor none labwc (existing calvin-wayland.service) Extra packages cog only cog + labwc stack (already used by the opt-in Wayland install) Permissions DRM master + /dev/input (root on Lite) /dev/dri render node; input via compositor Seat libinput seat0, hard-coded compositor's Fullscreen inherent COG_PLATFORM_WL_VIEW_FULLSCREEN=1 Cursor never drawn (unless enabled) compositor cursor; needs the labwc hide hack Touch libinput → page; rotation via libinput device rotation (driver-dependent) wlroots maps touch to output and follows the transform Rotation start-up only, renderer=gles only runtime, wlr-randr, follows compositor Panel power no supported path (test vcgencmd, CEC) wlopm (existing agent path) Escape hatch used by today's agent none none (agent is xrandr/wlopm-based, still works)

docs.title: 3. Kiosk needs
docs.text:
Need cog behaviour Verdict for Calvin Fullscreen DRM: yes by construction. Wayland: COG_PLATFORM_WL_VIEW_FULLSCREEN=1. Good. F11 un-fullscreens on Wayland with a keyboard. Fixed URL URL argument or COG_URL; no address bar, tabs, or navigation UI. The URL can only be changed at runtime through the session-bus cogctl open (or by restarting). Good; also simpler than Chromium's kiosk flags. Auto-restart on a crashed page --webprocess-failure=restart: retries the web process up to 5 times inside a 1 s window, then renders cog's built-in "Crash!" / "Out of memory!" page (launcher/cog-launcher.c:350, core/cog-webkit-utils.c). Default is error-page; exit/exit-ok also exist. Good with a watchdog: the fallback error page has no reload path, so a hung/crashed renderer can sit there forever. Run the unit with Restart=always and add an HTTP health watchdog. Cursor hiding DRM: no cursor at all unless COG_PLATFORM_DRM_CURSOR is set. Wayland: compositor cursor. DRM is better than anything we have today. Autoplay video WPE 2.48's WebKitSettings:media-playback-requires-user-gesture default is off ("media playback could start automatically", WebKitSettings.cpp, 2.48 branch). It can be pinned with [websettings] in a --config file. Audible-audio policy is a separate WebKit preference; UNVERIFIED whether unmuted video autoplays. Probably fine for muted loops; test the actual plugin. Install GStreamer plugins (gstreamer1.0-plugins-good/bad/libav) — Pi OS Lite has none, and cog's package does not recommend them. VC4 gives no hardware H.264 to GStreamer anyway, so expect software decode. Crash reporting Everything goes to stderr → journal: platform init, web-process termination reason (CRASHED / EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT), retry attempts, then the error page. No metrics, no HTTP status. WEBKIT_INSPECTOR_SERVER=0.0.0.0:2999 exposes the remote Web Inspector for live console/network checks. Adequate if we add a systemd watchdog (cogctl is not reachable from a system unit; use the backend's /api/health). Memory on Pi 3-class hardware No published measurement found. What exists: cog issue #65 (2018, Snapdragon 410) shows the three-process model — cog + WPEWebProcess + WPENetworkProcess — and a ~25 MB/hour leak in a canvas page; that issue is still open and is not evidence about 2.48. WPE marketing says "small footprint" but gives no number. §4.5 has this host's measurement and the reason it is not a Pi answer. Unknown — this is the go/no-go gate. Measure in §5.

Chromium today uses ~600 MB of the Pi's 905 MB (given). If cog lands under ~450 MB steady-state, the A/B is a win worth taking; if it lands at 600 MB too, cog buys nothing but risk.

docs.title: 4.1 Method
docs.text:
Built the real frontend and drove it in a WebKit engine on this machine:

cd frontend
npm ci
npm run build                     # dist/, 2.06 s, no errors

Engine: Playwright 1.59.1's WebKit, which on Linux is the WPE MiniBrowser (webkit-2272, navigator.userAgent … Version/26.4 Safari/605.1.15) — i.e. the same engine family as cog, one architecture away and many versions newer than Debian trixie's 2.48.3. It was launched from NixOS' Playwright browser bundle (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/nix/store/…-playwright-browsers, via playwright-core 1.59.1), so no playwright install/FHS download was needed.

Serving: a local static server on 127.0.0.1:8731 for frontend/dist (not 8000/5173). No backend was started. Every /api/** answer is a stub: pass A used page.route with service workers blocked; pass B enabled the service worker and served the same stub JSON from the local server (a service worker's own fetches bypass page.route). Stubs included /api/config (onScreenKeyboard: "on"), /api/auth/status (authenticated), empty /api/plugins, /api/calendar/*, /api/images/list, /api/kiosks, /api/keyboard/mappings.

A Chromium run through the identical harness was used as the control.

docs.title: 4.2 Results
docs.text:
Check WebKit (WPE MiniBrowser 26.4) Chromium control App boots, dashboard renders (calendar, photo pane, QR cards) ✅ 882 ms (local, stub API) ✅ 719 ms Settings opens, all 8 categories, authenticated ✅ ✅ On-screen keyboard opens on field focus ✅ ✅ OSK keys type into the field ("" → "abc", focus retained) ✅ ✅ Service worker registers, activates, scopes /, caches created ✅ calvin-shell-*, calvin-assets-*, calvin-api-*; page reloads controlled and boots again ✅ Console errors none none Failed requests none one aborted /api/health on reload (harness) Uncaught page errors one: ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications. none

Screenshots (committed with this document):

  • webkit-dashboard.png
  • webkit-settings.png
  • webkit-osk-typed.png — Display name field showing abc typed on the on-screen keyboard

CSS/JS feature probe (all true unless noted): color-mix(), :has(), container queries, dvh, unprefixed backdrop-filter, aspect-ratio, subgrid, CSS nesting, oklch(), text-wrap: balance, scrollbar-gutter, View Transitions, Popover API, <dialog>, navigator.mediaSession, navigator.clipboard, structuredClone, crypto.randomUUID, Array.findLast, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, PointerEvent, touch events. navigator.share is false (WPE has no Web Share); the frontend does not use it. All of these except Web Share shipped in Safari/WebKit 15.4–18.x, i.e. before 2.48 — so 2.48.3 should have them, but that is an inference, not a measurement (UNVERIFIED on 2.48).

docs.title: 4.3 WebKit-specific issues found
docs.text:
A. Native <select> dropdowns do not open under cog's DRM backend. Upstream, open: cog #793 ("cog with DRM backend doesn't support dropdowns", 0.18.5/2.50, reported on a Pi-class board) and cog #503 ("Popup menu not opened when selecting HTML select element"). Calvin uses native selects in:

  • frontend/src/components/PluginFieldRenderer.vue:50 and :64 — plugin select config fields (any plugin with a choice field),
  • frontend/src/components/settings/tabs/content/CalendarSourcesTab.vue:15 — calendar source type,
  • frontend/src/components/settings/tabs/system/UpdatesTab.vue:30 — update branch.

Not visible in the Playwright run (that engine renders popups); it is a known cog-DRM limitation. On a cog kiosk, those three settings would have to be changed from a phone/desktop (Calvin already offers "Use your phone" with a QR code) unless we replace native selects with an in-DOM picker.

B. Touch auto-detection may not fire under cog. The on-screen keyboard's auto mode depends on (any-pointer: coarse) or navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0 (frontend/src/composables/useTouchCapability.js:32-45, and the same signals gate useOnScreenKeyboard). In this headless WPE run maxTouchPoints was 0 and any-pointer: coarse did not match even with hasTouch: true; the OSK only appeared because the stub config sets onScreenKeyboard: "on". cog's DRM platform forwards libinput touch events but what WPE reports to the page is UNVERIFIED. Mitigation: set touchControls: "on" and onScreenKeyboard: "on" (per-kiosk overrides exist) for any cog kiosk before trusting touch chrome.

C. ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications. is raised as a page error in WebKit (Chromium suppresses it). It appeared on both passes and only on Settings. Candidates: frontend/src/components/settings/shell/CategoryRail.vue:51-52 (measure on observe; the rail's contents change when a category is selected), frontend/src/components/ui/OnScreenKeyboard.vue:135-136 (height measurement), and frontend/src/composables/useFitClamp.js:90. It is benign — layout settles and the screenshots are correct — but it is the one non-clean console signal, and on a Pi it would also fire. No action needed unless it ever loops.

D. Service worker + page.route interaction (harness, not product). An early run produced SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern on /api/keyboard/mappings and /api/auth/status. Cause: the page registered its service worker, and Playwright routing does not intercept fetches made by a service worker, so the worker's network-first fallback got index.html from the static server and WebKit's JSON.parse produced that message. Not a WebKit bug and not a cog issue; but it is a useful reminder for anyone testing Calvin with Playwright WebKit: block service workers, or serve API stubs from the server, not only from page.route.

E. No other engine-specific problems. Dialogs, the QR code (canvas), the clock bar, the calendar grid, the photo pane, backdrop-filter surfaces, the settings search, the keyboard's inert/aria-hidden handling and Teleport to body all rendered correctly.

F. Not exercised (no backend, by design): SSE (only used for the update log stream, frontend/src/composables/useSystem.js:210), plugin iframes, full-size photo decoding, video playback, admin sign-in round-trip, and anything that touches /api/system/* (stubbed out and never called on a live backend).

docs.title: 4.4 What this run does and does not prove
docs.text:
• Proves: the built frontend is engine-portable to WebKit's layout/JS stack; the OSK, router, Pinia stores, service worker and CSS feature set all work without a Chromium-only API.
  • Does not prove: behaviour on WPE 2.48.3 (⅓ of the version gap in the other direction), VC4 GLES paths, cog's popup handling, libinput touch semantics, JIT/heap behaviour on Cortex-A53, or memory on 1 GB.

docs.title: 4.5 Memory, measured — and why it is not a Pi number
docs.text:
Same built page, same 1280×800 viewport, same stubs, this host (x86_64, NixOS), 12 s after load, summing all browser processes:

Engine Sum RSS Sum PSS Notes WPE MiniBrowser (WebKit 26.4, Skia, headless) 981 MB 696 MB 4 processes; one web/content process at 679 MB RSS / 585 MB PSS Chromium (headless shell, same page) 536 MB 281 MB 11 processes

Blank-page control: WPE 489 MB RSS, Chromium 378 MB. So the engine baseline is already heavier here, and the dashboard adds more.

Do not read this as "cog will use 1 GB on a Pi". It is a different build of a newer engine on a different architecture with different raster settings, and PSS on x86 shares a lot of mapped library pages. What it does establish is the absence of any evidence that WPE is automatically the leaner engine — which is why the Pi measurement in §5 is the actual decision, not this table.

docs.title: 5. On-Pi test plan (coordinator, over SSH)
docs.text: Preconditions: Pi 3B+ on Raspberry Pi OS Trixie Lite 64-bit, SPLIT topology, working Chromium kiosk, SSH access, panel attached, and a way to see the screen (photo is fine). Run as the kiosk user with sudo. Nothing here calls /api/system/*; the horizontal checks use curl /api/health only.

docs.title: 5.1 Baseline first (Chromium, current stack)
docs.text:
# what is running now
systemctl list-units 'calvin-*' --no-pager
free -m; vcgencmd measure_temp; vcgencmd get_throttled
# memory of the current stack, 10 samples over 5 min
for i in $(seq 10); do
  printf '%s ' "$(date -Is)"
  free -m | awk 'NR==2{printf "used=%sMB avail=%sMB ", $3, $7}'
  ps -eo rss=,comm= | awk '/chromium/{s+=$1} END{printf "chromium_rss=%dMB\n", s/1024}'
  sleep 30
done | tee ~/baseline-chromium.log

Also note "cold boot to dashboard" three times (systemd-analyze plus a stopwatch on the panel) and curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' https://calvin.example.com/api/health for the network baseline.

docs.title: 5.2 Install cog (Chromium untouched)
docs.text:
sudo apt update
apt-cache policy cog libwpewebkit-2.0-1
sudo apt-get -s install --no-install-recommends cog | tail -5   # size preview
sudo apt install --no-install-recommends cog
# only if a plugin plays video; Pi OS Lite ships no GStreamer plugins
sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-libav
cog --version                       # expect: cog 0.18.4 (WPE WebKit 2.48.3)
ls /usr/lib/*/cog/modules/          # expect: libcogplatform-{drm,headless,wl}.so

docs.title: 5.3 First run by hand (DRM, no unit yet)
docs.text:
sudo systemctl stop calvin-x.service calvin-kiosk-remote.service calvin-display-agent.service
sudo systemctl stop getty@tty1.service
sudo cog --platform=drm \
     --platform-params=renderer=modeset \
     --webprocess-failure=restart \
     'https://calvin.example.com/'

Watch the console for the first 2 minutes. Success = dashboard in <15 s, no Cannot create framebuffer, no repeated Renderer process terminated. Then Ctrl+C and repeat from a cold boot once you have the unit.

docs.title: 5.4 Variant A — DRM/KMS unit
docs.text:
/etc/systemd/system/calvin-cog.service:

[Unit]
Description=Calvin kiosk (cog + WPE WebKit, DRM/KMS)
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target systemd-udev-settle.service
Conflicts=getty@tty1.service

[Service]
Type=simple
# Root gives DRM master and /dev/input access on a Lite image.
# Alternative: User=calvin, SupplementaryGroups=video input, with no other DRM master.
Environment=COG_PLATFORM_DRM_VIDEO_MODE=1920x1080
Environment=COG_PLATFORM_DRM_MODE_MAX=1920x1080@60
ExecStart=/usr/bin/cog --platform=drm --platform-params=renderer=modeset \
          --webprocess-failure=restart https://calvin.example.com/
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

[Install]
WantedBy=graphical.target

Portrait/180°: replace renderer=modeset with renderer=gles,rotation=1 (90° CCW) or rotation=3 (270°), or rotation=2 for 180°. Changing orientation needs a unit edit + restart; note that in the result.

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl disable --now calvin-kiosk-remote.service calvin-x.service
sudo systemctl enable --now calvin-cog.service
journalctl -u calvin-cog -f

docs.title: 5.5 Variant B — cog on labwc (keeps wlopm)
docs.text:
Use the existing Wayland install (--display-stack wayland, KIOSK_INSTALL.md), then replace the Chromium line in ~/.config/labwc/autostart with:

COG_PLATFORM_WL_VIEW_FULLSCREEN=1 cog 'https://calvin.example.com/'

(or a user unit with Environment=WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000, COG_PLATFORM_WL_VIEW_FULLSCREEN=1). Rotation stays wlr-randr, panel power stays wlopm — the existing agent keeps working.

docs.title: 5.6 Measurements
docs.text:
# memory: PSS of each cog process + system available, every minute for an hour
for i in $(seq 60); do
  printf '%s ' "$(date -Is)"
  for p in $(pgrep -x cog) $(pgrep -f WebKitWebProcess) $(pgrep -f WebKitNetworkProcess); do
    printf '%s=%sMB ' "$(cat /proc/$p/comm)" \
      "$(( $(awk '/^Pss:/{print $2}' /proc/$p/smaps_rollup 2>/dev/null || echo 0) / 1024 ))"
  done
  free -m | awk 'NR==2{printf "used=%sMB avail=%sMB\n", $3, $7}'
  sleep 60
done | tee ~/cog-mem.log

# CPU / temperature / throttling
sudo apt install -y sysstat
pidstat -h -p "$(pgrep -x cog)" 5 12
vmstat 5 12
vcgencmd measure_temp; vcgencmd get_throttled
journalctl -u calvin-cog -p warning --since '-1h' --no-pager

# load time: unit start → first backend request (the server side is the honest clock)
systemd-analyze blame | head
systemd-analyze critical-chain calvin-cog.service
journalctl -u calvin-cog -o short-precise | head -20
# on the Calvin server, at the same moment:
#   docker logs --since 5m calvin 2>&1 | grep -E "GET /api/(config|health)"

# crash drill: kill the renderer and watch recovery
sudo kill -9 "$(pgrep -f WebKitWebProcess | head -1)"
sleep 5; journalctl -u calvin-cog -n 20 --no-pager

docs.title: 5.7 Panel checks (someone at the screen)
docs.text:
1. Dashboard renders; photos rotate; clock bar is right.
  2. Touch: every region, the hot corner, and a swipe/drag.
  3. Settings → Display → "Display name": tap the field, type with the on-screen keyboard, confirm the field updates and stays focused.
  4. Settings → Content Sources → Calendars → "type" dropdown: expected to fail under cog DRM (issue #793) — record what happens.
  5. Rotation: all four orientations, and re-tap the same target after each.
  6. Cursor: no arrow at rest, none after a tap.
  7. Panel power: sudo vcgencmd display_power 0 then 1. If that does nothing under KMS, record it — it means the schedule needs CEC or the monitor's own timer, or this kiosk should use variant B.
  8. Cold boot 10×: no boot text left on screen, no blank frame that stays.

docs.title: 5.8 Soak and acceptance
docs.text:
24 h at the dashboard with a 5-minute memory sample (sleep 300), plus journalctl -u calvin-cog -p warning and dmesg | grep -iE 'vc4|drm' at the end.

Adopt cog if all of these hold:

  • steady-state PSS (cog + web + network) < 450 MB after 1 h, and at least 150 MB below the Chromium baseline;
  • first dashboard paint no worse than Chromium +10 %;
  • 24 h with no unplanned restart, no Renderer process terminated storm;
  • touch, OSK and rotation verified physically;
  • the <select> workaround is acceptable (configure from a phone) or a fix is scheduled;
  • panel power has a working path, or that kiosk's schedule is disabled;
  • rollback (§5.9) tested once.

Reject / keep Chromium on any failed gate, or if memory comes out within noise of Chromium — in that case cog costs a second engine, a stale CVE set and a lost display-control path for nothing.

docs.title: 5.9 Rollback
docs.text:
sudo systemctl disable --now calvin-cog.service
sudo systemctl enable --now getty@tty1.service
# X11 stack
sudo systemctl enable --now calvin-x.service calvin-kiosk-remote.service calvin-display-agent.service
# or the Wayland stack, if that is what the kiosk had
# sudo systemctl enable --now calvin-wayland.service

Chromium and the X11/labwc packages were never removed, so this is a service switch, not a reflash. sudo apt remove cog is optional and only frees space.

docs.title: 6. Risks
docs.text: Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation cog uses as much RAM as Chromium (or more) Medium No reason to switch Measure first (§5); accept/reject on the number DRM+GLES hits a VC4 bug similar to Chromium's Low–medium Black screen / framebuffer errors Variant B (Wayland) as fallback; journal the first boot; issue #748 is the signature to watch for Touch unreliable (upstream #737/#456) Medium Kiosk unusable by finger Variant A/B test on the real panel; fall back to Chromium Rotation needs restart; touch mapping wrong after rotation Medium Portrait kiosk wrong renderer=gles,rotation=N; physical tap test in all four orientations No panel-power path under DRM High Night schedule stops working vcgencmd test; CEC; monitor timer; or variant B with wlopm <select> dropdowns dead on the kiosk High (DRM) Settings degraded Configure from phone; or replace native selects Trixie's wpewebkit gets no security updates (tracker: "vulnerable, ignored") High Long-lived unpatched browser cog is the default since 2026-10-31; restrict kiosk network reach, re-check the tracker each Pi OS point release, and switch a kiosk to --display-stack x11 if that risk is unacceptable cog 0.18 is legacy; Debian 14 moves to WPE 2.54 Certain eventually Launcher rewrite Treat cog as a stop-gap; plan a ~30-line WPEPlatform launcher at the next OS cycle Second browser engine on the image (+deps) Certain Disk/SD wear, update surface --no-install-recommends, remove cog if rejected

docs.title: 7. Open questions / explicitly UNVERIFIED
docs.text:
• UNVERIFIED: cog's memory on a Pi 3B+ (the whole point of §5).

docs.title: Kiosk display stack: X11 or Wayland?
docs.text: Research date: 2026-10-29 Bead: calvin-98dq

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Move the Pi 4/5 kiosks (SPLIT and FULL) to Raspberry Pi OS Trixie with Wayland + labwc, and keep X11 + openbox as the supported fallback for Pi 3B/3B+ SPLIT until real hardware proves that Chromium-in-a-compositor is acceptable there. Pi OS has made Wayland/labwc the default desktop on every model, Trixie still ships an X11 meta-package, and labwc gives us the three things Calvin's agent needs (wlr-output-management for wlr-randr rotation, wlr-output-power-management for wlopm, and FreeDesktop/labwc autostart) with the least distance from the platform Raspberry Pi itself supports. Cage is the cleaner single-app compositor, but its Pi OS build has no cursor control and no configuration, and its headless/hotplug behaviour is a known operational hazard. Do not do a flag-day switch: add a model-based dual-stack setup, make the display agent compositor-aware, and only then flip the default for Pi 4/5. Pi 3B/3B+ stay on X11 for now: they can run Wayland (Pi OS defaults to it), but the 1 GB RAM and VideoCore IV GPU leave too little margin for a browser kiosk, and no credible benchmark shows a win.

Scope: Calvin's kiosk browser stack (Pi OS Lite + Chromium), both SPLIT (remote backend) and FULL (backend on the same Pi). This is a research document only; no scripts, services, or application code were changed.

Evidence note. Facts are linked inline. Package versions were checked against the Raspberry Pi Trixie archive and Debian on 2026-10-29. Forum posts and user reports are labelled as such; anything I could not verify is marked UNVERIFIED.

docs.title: 1. What current Raspberry Pi OS ships and defaults to
docs.text:
Trixie is current; Bookworm is oldstable but still relevant.

  • Debian 13 "trixie" is the current stable release (13.7, 2026-09-12). Debian 12 "bookworm" is oldstable, with LTS through 2028-06-30. Trixie's own end-of-life is 2028-08-09, with LTS through 2030-06-30 (Debian releases).
  • Raspberry Pi OS Trixie was announced on 2025-10-02. Raspberry Pi staff said Bookworm would get Debian support for another two years and new kernels for critical vulnerabilities, but no further Raspberry Pi-specific package updates (Trixie announcement + staff comments). Bookworm remains downloadable as "Legacy" and still receives Chromium builds; the Pi archive currently carries Chromium 156 for both Bookworm and Trixie.
  • Desktop default: since the October 2024 Bookworm release, Raspberry Pi Desktop runs Wayland with labwc by default on all models, including Pi 3; X11 remains selectable, and Wayfire is no longer supported with updates (labwc announcement). Trixie continues the labwc default. On Bookworm before that update, Pi 4/5 used Wayfire/Wayland and Pi 3 used X11.
  • Lite: Raspberry Pi OS Lite is command-line only; it ships no display server and no compositor. Trixie splits the desktop into meta-packages: rpd-wayland-core for a bare Wayland desktop, rpd-x-core for a bare X11 desktop, plus rpd-theme, rpd-preferences, etc. (Trixie announcement). Both meta-packages are present in the Trixie archive at version 1.35.
  • Is X11 still supported on Lite? Yes. Installing rpd-x-core (or just xserver-xorg/xinit/openbox) gives a supported X11 kiosk, and raspi-config still exposes an X11 session. UNVERIFIED: Raspberry Pi has not published a date on which X11 will be removed. The practical horizon is the Trixie support window (Debian security to 2028, LTS to 2030); do not assume X11 survives beyond that, but there is no announced near-term cutoff.

Per model, in practice:

Model Pi OS Trixie Desktop default Lite: what you install Notes for Calvin Pi 5 / Pi 500 / CM5 Wayland + labwc rpd-wayland-core + Chromium Best Wayland target; Pi 5 has no H.264 decoder (see §5) Pi 4B / Pi 400 / CM4 Wayland + labwc same Recommended Wayland target; 2 GB+ Pi 3B / 3B+ / 3A+ Wayland + labwc same 1 GB (3A+ 512 MB); Chromium is the bottleneck, not the compositor Pi Zero 2 W / older Wayland + labwc on Desktop same 512 MB; not recommended for Chromium (Calvin already says this)

The X11 option is still present on Trixie; Raspberry Pi's own current kiosk tutorial uses the Desktop image and labwc's ~/.config/labwc/autostart (Raspberry Pi kiosk tutorial). That is a strong signal that Wayland/labwc is now the supported path, while X11 is compatibility, not the future.

docs.title: 2. Candidate compositors for a single-app kiosk
labwc
docs.text:
• Packaged: yes, default. Pi archive Trixie: 0.20.2-1~bpo13+1; Bookworm: 0.8.4-1+rpt1. Debian stable has 0.8.3, so Pi OS deliberately ships a newer backport.
  • Maintenance: active; 0.20.2 released 2026-08-21, developed closely with Raspberry Pi and wlroots.
  • Autostart without a desktop: yes. ~/.config/labwc/autostart (shell script) or a FreeDesktop .desktop file in /etc/xdg/autostart; Raspberry Pi's kiosk tutorial uses the former. labwc can be started directly as the session process; it does not require LXDE or a login manager.
  • Cursor: HideCursor and WarpCursor actions exist, but there is no persistent "hide after idle" setting. piSignage documents the workaround: bind HideCursor + WarpCursor x=-1 y=-1, then fire it at startup with wtype (labwc actions, piSignage cursor guide). The cursor reappears on pointer/touch input.
  • Rotation: wlr-randr or kanshi; labwc implements wlr-output-management v4. labwc's own integration guide recommends wlr-randr for one-shot output changes and kanshi for profiles (labwc integration).
  • Touch mapping: wlroots maps touch to the output under the touch point and applies the output transform. labwc additionally exposes <touch><mapToOutput>HDMI-A-1</mapToOutput> and per-device <libinput> settings in rc.xml (rc.xml reference). There is a known stylus-specific rotation bug, while finger touch rotates correctly (labwc #1990); test the actual panel.

docs.title: cage
docs.text:
• Packaged: yes. Pi archive Trixie: 0.3.1-1~bpo13+1+rpt2; Bookworm: 0.2.0-2+rpt1.
  • Maintenance: active but small; 0.3.1 released 2026-06-30. Cage is purpose built for one maximized application, with no configuration file: everything is command-line or environment (cage configuration wiki, cage(1)).
  • Autostart without a desktop: yes, but it needs a proper logind/PAM session (wlroots must be built with systemd-logind support). The upstream wiki has a cage@.service template with PAMName, TTYPath, and pam_systemd (cage systemd guide). This is very close to Calvin's existing calvin-x.service shape.
  • Cursor: no supported option in 0.3.1. If any input device has pointer capability, cage shows a cursor. On a Pi, vc4-hdmi itself can register as a keyboard+pointer device, which is why a cursor appears in the middle of the screen even with no mouse. Workarounds are a transparent cursor theme, udev rules to ignore the device, or patching. Cage master gained a cursor-shape fix and "drop set_cursor when pointer capability is absent" in 2026, after 0.3.1 (cage #299). For a product kiosk this is a real drawback.
  • Rotation: wlr-randr/kanshi; cage supports wlr-output-management v4 (cage configuration wiki).
  • Touch mapping: wlroots default mapping follows the output layout/transform; cage exposes no mapping configuration. Verify with the target panel.

docs.title: sway
docs.text:
• Packaged: yes; Pi archive 1.10.1-2+rpt1, Debian stable 1.10.1, upstream 1.12 (2026-05-25).
  • Maintenance: very active.
  • Autostart without a desktop: exec lines in ~/.config/sway/config; can be launched from a TTY or systemd session.
  • Cursor: seat seat0 hide_cursor <timeout-ms> is a first-class setting (sway-input(5)).
  • Rotation: output <name> transform 90|180|270|flipped… or wlr-randr (sway-output(5)).
  • Touch: input <identifier> map_to_output <output> plus the output transform.
  • Fit: capable, but it brings tiling-window-manager concepts (workspaces, borders, config language) that a one-app kiosk does not need. More to get wrong than labwc.

docs.title: wayfire
docs.text:
• Packaged: yes, but legacy on Pi OS: Pi archive 0.9.0-5+rpt1; upstream 0.11. Raspberry Pi's October 2024 announcement says Wayfire will no longer be supported with updates on Pi OS (announcement).
  • Autostart: [autostart] in wayfire.ini.
  • Rotation/touch: supports wlr-output-management, so wlr-randr works, but the stack is frozen on Pi OS. Do not start a new deployment on it.

docs.title: weston
docs.text:
• Packaged: Debian (14.0.2 stable, 16.0.0 testing); not part of Pi OS's desktop stack.
  • Kiosk shell: exists and is designed for single-app use (Weston kiosk-shell).
  • Missing pieces: Weston does not implement wlr-output-management or wlr-output-power-management (both marked x in the Wayland Explorer tables), so no wlr-randr, kanshi, or wlopm. Rotation is weston.ini plus restart. It is a reference compositor, not a good fit for Calvin's runtime display controls.

docs.title: 3. Pi 3B/3B+: is Wayland + Chromium usable?
docs.text:
Technically yes; practically, not yet a safe default.

What is verified:

  • Raspberry Pi says labwc was optimised until it "runs just as fast as X on older Raspberry Pi models", and Trixie was tested back to Pi 1; a staff comment calls the Pi 3 desktop "perfectly usable" (labwc announcement, Trixie comments). That is a desktop claim, not a Chromium-kiosk benchmark.
  • The Pi 3 GPU is VideoCore IV: Mesa's VC4 driver supports Pi 0–3 with OpenGL ES 2.0 (Mesa VC4). A wlroots compositor can run on it, but every frame is composited by that GPU, and Chromium's raster/compositing competes for the same 1 GB of RAM.
  • Pi 3B/3B+ have 1 GB RAM. Calvin's own install guide already says "Pi 3B / 3B+ works, but Chromium is slow" and treats Pi 4/5 as recommended (KIOSK_INSTALL.md). Raspberry Pi's kiosk tutorial sets the floor at "Pi 3 or newer with at least 1 GB RAM", and Chromium/Firefox refuse to run below that (tutorial).
  • Real reports are mixed, and none show a performance win:
  • A Pi 3B+ user running Bookworm + labwc + Chromium kiosk reports Chromium starting to a white screen from the labwc autostart (forum report). Anecdotal, but exactly the kind of failure a kiosk cannot have.
  • A Pi 3 user reports Chromium 149 failing to start on a fresh Trixie 32-bit Desktop image, on both X11 and Wayland (forum report, June 2026). Current Chromium is 156, so this may be fixed; UNVERIFIED.
  • Chromium has a low-RAM warning popup on Pi 3-class devices that is hard to suppress in kiosk mode (Chromium issue 373891800).
  • The most experienced comparable project, Anthias, deliberately does not put a compositor on Pi 3 or Pi 4: it uses linuxfb on Pi 1/2/3-32, eglfs on Pi 3-64/Pi 4, and cage/Wayland only on Pi 5/x86/Rock Pi 4 (Anthias hardware notes). That is a strong practitioner signal about where compositor overhead is affordable.
  • A small hobby project, KioskPi, does claim cage + Chromium on "Pi 3+ / Trixie 64-bit" (KioskPi), but it is a one-maintainer project with no published benchmark. Treat it as existence proof, not evidence of acceptable performance.

Conclusion: Wayland + Chromium will boot on a Pi 3, and Pi OS defaults to it, but there is no evidence it is faster than X11 for this workload, and the failure reports cluster around exactly the Pi 3. Keeping X11 for Pi 3B/3B+ SPLIT is reasonable and low-risk: X11 is still supported in Trixie, and the only thing we give up is being on the default path. Re-evaluate after a measured Chromium 156 A/B test on a 3B+ (cold boot, first paint, tab switch, 24 h memory).

docs.title: 4. Replacing what the backend does today
docs.text:
Calvin currently uses xrandr (display_orientation_service.py, calvin_display_agent.py) and xset dpms / xset s (display_power_service.py, calvin_display_agent.py). Under Wayland those tools either do not see the DRM output or do not own it: Xwayland is a client, not the display server, so xset dpms cannot power the panel. The labwc maintainers explicitly recommend wlopm for this instead of wlr-randr --off (labwc integration).

Need X11 today Wayland replacement Compositor support Caveats Rotation / mode xrandr --output … --rotate left --mode 1920x1080 wlr-randr --output HDMI-A-1 --transform 90 --mode 1920x1080@60Hz cage, labwc, sway, wayfire (wlr-output-management v4); not weston Output names change (HDMI-1 → HDMI-A-1); transform direction differs from xrandr (see migration table); CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT=HDMI-1 will be wrong Output profile xrandr script kanshi profile, or wlr-randr at compositor start cage, labwc, sway, wayfire kanshi needs the compositor's output-management protocol; start it inside the session Panel on/off xset dpms force off/on, vcgencmd display_power wlopm --off <output> / --on <output> cage ≥0.3.0, labwc, sway, wayfire (wlr-output-power-management); not weston Some monitors fake a hotplug when signal drops; labwc re-enables outputs by default → panel wakes. Set <autoEnableOutputs>no</autoEnableOutputs> and use wlr-randr/kanshi to enable at boot. wlopm --on can fail after a hotplug; wlr-randr --output … --on is the fallback Legacy panel power vcgencmd display_power 0/1 Not a Wayland API; keep only as a legacy Pi 3/4 fallback n/a Pi 5 vcgencmd may not register display_power at all; under vc4-kms-v3d on Pi 4 it can be a no-op or the panel can wake after ~12 s. Do not make it the primary path Screen-blank timeout xset s N, xset +dpms, xset dpms N N N swayidle -w timeout N 'wlopm --off *' resume 'wlopm --on *', or the backend schedule calling wlopm directly labwc and sway support ext-idle-notify; swayidle works with both Calvin's authoritative feature is a schedule, not an idle timeout. Keep the schedule logic and call wlopm; add idle blanking only if the product wants it TV on/off (optional) — cec-ctl -d /dev/cec0 --to 0 --standby / --image-view-on Display-server independent Only works through HDMI-CEC on a TV; most monitors have no CEC. cec-ctl comes from v4l-utils (cec-ctl(1))

Which compositor gets which protocol: cage, labwc, sway, and wayfire support both wlr-output-management and wlr-output-power-management. Weston supports neither. That alone eliminates Weston for Calvin's runtime rotation/power.

wlopm is in Debian Trixie as 0.1.0-1 (arm64 0.1.0-1+b1), so it is one apt install on Pi OS Lite; wlr-randr is 0.4.1-1, kanshi 1.5.1-2, swayidle 1.8.0-1 (Debian madison, 2026-10-29).

docs.title: 5. Chromium on Wayland on a Pi
Ozone flags and environment
docs.text:
• Chromium ≥140 auto-detects the display server and prefers Wayland when available; --ozone-platform-hint default changed to auto (Chrome 140 change). On current Pi OS Chromium (156) you normally do not need Ozone flags when Chromium is started inside a Wayland session.
  • To force it, or if auto-detection fails, use --ozone-platform=wayland (documented in the Ozone overview). --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform is the legacy form; do not add it blindly.
  • A systemd-launched Chromium needs the session environment, not just the binary: XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland, WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0, and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/<uid>. Without those it may fall back to X11/ XWayland or fail to connect. This is the single most important unit-file change.
  • Keep kiosk flags minimal. Real Pi 5 cage kiosks run chromium --kiosk --ozone-platform=wayland <url> successfully (rpi/linux #7721).

docs.title: GPU raster and hardware video decode
docs.text:
• Raster/compositing: Pi 4/5 use V3D for rendering with VC4/KMS for display (Mesa V3D); Pi 3 uses VC4 (GLES2 only). Chromium does use the GPU for compositing/raster when Mesa/EGL works, but you must verify on the device with chrome://gpu. Do not cargo-cult --use-gl=egl, --use-angle=gles-egl, or --ignore-gpu-blocklist: a current Pi 5 cage kiosk report shows --use-angle=gles-egl triggering repeated V3D resets, while stock flags ran for hours (rpi/linux #7721).
  • Hardware video decode is model- and codec-specific, and not a reason to choose Wayland:
  • Pi 4: the Raspberry Pi Chromium build can hardware-decode H.264 through the V4L2 stateful decoder; users report working 1080p playback with the RPi build (forum report).
  • Pi 5: the legacy H.264 decoder was removed; the Pi 5 decoder is HEVC-only (rpivid/V4L2 stateless). Stock Chromium reports software decode and does not accept HEVC, so hardware decode is effectively unavailable without a patched build (Pi 5 decode investigation; a patched Chromium exists at chromium-rpi-hevc).
  • Calvin's dashboard is calendars, photos, and web services; do not make video decode a migration gate. If a plugin embeds video, test that plugin separately.

docs.title: Known kiosk bugs / sharp edges
docs.text:
1. Cursor on cage (no option, vc4-hdmi counts as a pointer) and labwc (one-shot HideCursor only). See §2.
  2. Pi 3B+ labwc autostart → white Chromium window, one forum report; test cold boot, not just systemctl restart.
  3. Pi 5 V3D GPU hang in a cage + Chromium kiosk while zooming a map (Oct 2026, open). Stock flags are safer; add a GPU-hang watchdog/restart.
  4. Low-RAM warning on Pi 3-class devices; the popup can cover a kiosk page.
  5. Cage headless boot binds zero outputs and never recovers without udev in the container; Anthias added a watchdog that exits/restarts the viewer when there is no bindable output (Anthias notes).
  6. Monitor hotplug wake after wlopm --off; see §4.
  7. Panel over fullscreen if you run the full Raspberry Pi Desktop; use the bare rpd-wayland-core stack (no panel) or configure the panel away.

docs.title: 6. What comparable projects do
docs.text:
Project Current stack Why / lesson FullPageOS Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm (2024-11-19 base), 32-bit, Chromium 130, X11 (uses xdotool, x11vnc); last release 0.14.0, 2025-07-14 (release) The best-known "browser on boot" distro has not moved to Trixie/Wayland yet. Inertia and X11 tooling still dominate the kiosk-distro niche. Anthias (Screenly OSE) Per-board: linuxfb on Pi 1/2/3-32, eglfs/KMS on Pi 3-64/Pi 4, cage/Wayland on Pi 5/x86/Rock Pi 4; QtWebEngine viewer, not Chromium (hardware notes, wayland launcher) They only pay for a compositor where the SoC can afford it. On Wayland they rotate with wlr-randr transforms and blank with wlr-randr --off; they hit cage's headless/hotplug bugs and added a watchdog. This is the closest match to Calvin's problem. piSignage Current Pi player is labwc/Wayland; docs include a labwc cursor-hiding procedure and a Trixie post-install guide (cursor guide) Commercial signage moved with Pi OS to labwc. It also confirms that cursor hiding is a manual hack (HideCursor + wtype), not a supported compositor feature. MagicMirror² Electron; v2.38 (2026-10-01) starts with --ozone-platform=wayland when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is set, otherwise X11 (clientonly/index.js, changelog) Electron/Chromium upstream now handles Wayland; the remaining work is session environment, not browser patches. Many installed mirrors still run X11.

The pattern: new/high-end boards go Wayland; low-end boards stay on a framebuffer/EGL stack; X11 remains common where tooling or inertia wins. No comparable project reports Wayland making a Pi 3 browser kiosk faster.

docs.title: 7.1 Target matrix
docs.text:
Hardware / topology Default stack Notes Pi 5 / Pi 500 / CM5, SPLIT or FULL Wayland + labwc Primary target; test V3D hang and HEVC Pi 4B / Pi 400 / CM4 (2 GB+), SPLIT or FULL Wayland + labwc Recommended minimum for FULL Pi 3B / 3B+, SPLIT X11 + openbox (unchanged) Keep supported; optional Wayland pilot behind an env flag Pi 3B / 3B+, FULL X11 + openbox (best effort) FULL officially needs Pi 4/5; do not block the migration on Pi 3 FULL Pi Zero 2 W / older Unsupported 512 MB is below Chromium's practical floor

Use an explicit CALVIN_DISPLAY_STACK=x11|wayland (default auto) in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk, plus a model check from /proc/device-tree/model (Calvin already reads this in is_raspberry_pi()). auto chooses X11 on Pi 3, Wayland on Pi 4/5. Do not infer only from WAYLAND_DISPLAY: an X11 session can have XWayland, and a broken Wayland session can leave a stale variable.

docs.title: 7.2 Dual support, not a flag day
docs.text:
1. Phase 1 (SPLIT, opt-in): add the Wayland unit/config and agent branch; install it only with --display-stack wayland or on Pi 4/5 test devices. Keep the X11 packages and units installed so rollback is a service switch, not a reimage.
  2. Phase 2 (SPLIT, default Pi 4/5): make setup-kiosk.sh choose Wayland on Pi 4/5, X11 on Pi 3. Keep an env override.
  3. Phase 3 (FULL, Pi 4/5): same selection in setup.sh; FULL on Pi 3 stays X11 and is documented as legacy.
  4. Phase 4 (Pi 3 reassessment): only after an A/B test on 3B+ with the current Chromium, and only if it wins on cold boot and 24 h memory.

docs.title: 7.3 Backend / agent changes (proposed, not implemented here)
docs.text: File / service Today Wayland change backend/app/services/display_orientation_service.py Parses xrandr --query, applies xrandr --rotate normal|left|right|inverted Add a Wayland branch: list/apply with wlr-randr (--json if available, else text); --transform normal|90|180|270; --mode WxH@Hz. Keep X11 branch for Pi 3. The current allowlist will reject an unknown unit by design Docs X11/openbox wording in KIOSK_INSTALL.md, DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md Document the model matrix and the CALVIN_DISPLAY_STACK override

docs.title: 7.4 Rotation mapping (must be verified on hardware)
docs.text:
xrandr and wlr-randr use different names and directions. A reasonable first mapping, to be confirmed by looking at the panel:

Calvin config xrandr today wlr transform (proposed) landscape, not flipped normal normal portrait, not flipped left (90° CCW) 90 (wlroots transform 90 is CCW) landscape, flipped inverted 180 portrait, flipped right (90° CW) 270

Anthias documents the same trap from the other direction: wlr transforms turn counter-clockwise, so a user-facing "rotate 90° clockwise" maps to 270 (Anthias notes). Treat this table as a starting point and assert the result physically; a wrong direction is easy to miss on a symmetric dashboard.

docs.title: 7.5 Environment keys (proposed)
docs.text:
CALVIN_DISPLAY_STACK=auto        # auto | x11 | wayland
CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION=normal   # normal | left | right | inverted (existing)
CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT=HDMI-A-1   # Wayland names differ from xrandr's HDMI-1
CALVIN_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION=1920x1080@60
CALVIN_WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0

CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT deserves a compatibility pass: existing installs have HDMI-1; Wayland uses HDMI-A-1. Accept both, or leave it unset and auto-detect the first connected output, before changing any defaults.

docs.title: 9. What must be tested on real hardware
docs.text:
Minimum matrix (do not sign off from a single Pi 5):

Dimension Cases Board Pi 3B, Pi 3B+, Pi 4B (2 GB and 4/8 GB), Pi 5 (4/8 GB), Pi 400/500 if available OS Trixie Lite 64-bit (primary), Trixie Lite 32-bit (spot check), Bookworm Lite 64-bit legacy (upgrade path) Topology SPLIT (remote backend) and FULL (local backend) Display HDMI 1080p; 4K on Pi 4/5; DSI Touch Display 2; portrait and 180°; cold boot with display attached; boot headless then hot-plug; monitor power-cycle Boot Cold boot 20×; boot with backend down; boot with network down; boot after unclean shutdown Chromium First paint; kiosk URL/query string; backend restart/reconnect; tab/screen switching; chrome://gpu and chrome://media-internals; 72 h soak; memory on Pi 3; GPU-reset logs (dmesg | grep v3d) Rotation All four orientations; output/mode change at runtime; touch coordinates after each; 180° + touch Power Schedule on/off across midnight and DST; wlopm off/on; wake after hotplug; fake-hotplug monitor; vcgencmd fallback on Pi 3/4 only Cursor No mouse; touch-only panel; USB mouse plugged/unplugged; after idle; after touch Update Kiosk bundle self-update; rollback; unit restart; signature/manifest checks; unknown-unit rejection Regression X11 Pi 3 still boots and the agent still rotates/powers the panel after the shared code changes

Acceptance criteria for flipping Pi 4/5 to Wayland: 20/20 clean cold boots with a display attached; no cursor at rest; rotation and touch correct in all four orientations on the target panel; schedule off/on works for 7 consecutive days including a monitor power-cycle; Chromium survives a 72 h soak without a GPU-reset black screen; rollback to X11 is one service switch and re-tested.

docs.title: 10. Open questions / explicitly unverified
docs.text:
• UNVERIFIED: a formal Raspberry Pi end-of-support date for X11. Debian's Trixie LTS (2030-06-30) is the outer bound I can defend; Raspberry Pi has made no such promise for its own packages.
  • UNVERIFIED: whether Bookworm's labwc 0.8.4 supports autoEnableOutputs, HideCursor/WarpCursor, and <touch><mapToOutput>. Trixie's 0.20.2 does. Test before promising feature parity on legacy installs.
  • UNVERIFIED: current (Chromium 156) status of the Pi 3 Trixie "Chromium won't start" report; the report is from June 2026 and Chromium has moved on.
  • UNVERIFIED: whether wlopm --on works reliably on the specific monitors Calvin users have; the labwc discussion shows at least one monitor family where it does not, and wlr-randr --on is required.
  • UNVERIFIED: touch rotation behaviour on the DSI Touch Display 2 under cage specifically; labwc's wlroots path and explicit mapToOutput are better documented.
  • UNVERIFIED: whether Calvin's dashboard (no heavy WebGL) can trigger the Pi 5 V3D hang; the public report is a map/OpenLayers page, so test the real screens.
