  • Motion/keyboard wake. Scheduled windows only, matching backend behaviour.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
A small long-running local agent on the kiosk Pi. It does not poll every minute. The scheduled on/off boundaries are computed locally, so the agent sleeps until the exact next boundary and flips the panel precisely then. The only reason to contact the server is to notice UI edits to the schedule, which it does on a slow safety refresh (default 15 min, tunable).

┌────────── central server ──────────┐        ┌──────────── kiosk Pi ────────────────┐
│ Calvin backend                     │  HTTPS │ calvin-display-agent.service          │
│  - schedule authored in UI         │ <──────│   calvin_display_agent.py (Type=simple)│
│  - GET /api/config exposes it      │  every │     loop:                             │
│  (display_power_service inert here;│  ~15m  │       fetch /api/config               │
│   no local display)                │  +edits│       apply desired state (on change) │
└────────────────────────────────────┘        │       sleep → min(next boundary, 15m) │
                                               │       vcgencmd / xset local           │
                                               └───────────────────────────────────────┘

Traffic: ~1 config fetch per refresh interval (≈96/day at 15 min) plus one at each boundary — versus 1440/day for naive 60s polling. Panel flips happen at the boundary, not up to a minute late.

Control loop: 1. Agent reads CALVIN_BACKEND_URL (and optional CALVIN_DISPLAY_REFRESH_SECONDS, default 900) from /etc/default/calvin-kiosk — the same env file the kiosk browser uses. 2. GET ${CALVIN_BACKEND_URL}/api/config (no auth; already public, consumed by the kiosk browser). On failure: keep the last applied state, sleep a short backoff (60s), retry — never blank on a network blip. 3. Compute desired state for "now", mirroring display_power_service: - display_schedule_enabled false → on (schedule disabled ⇒ keep display on). - Else find today's entry by now.weekday() (0=Mon … 6=Sun — same as backend). - Entry missing or enabled false → on. - Else on/off from onTime/offTime, midnight-spanning via the backend's exact rule: off < on ⇒ (now ≥ on or now < off), else on ≤ now < off. - Timezone from config timezone (via zoneinfo); null → system local time. 4. Apply only when the desired state differs from the last applied state (plus once at startup), to avoid needless HDMI toggling: vcgencmd display_power 0|1 first; if ineffective, fall back to xset dpms force off|on (DISPLAY=:0). 5. Compute seconds to the next boundary: enumerate each enabled day's on/off datetimes across the next ~8 days, take the earliest strictly after "now". Sleep min(that, refresh_interval) so boundaries are exact and edits are still picked up within the refresh window. Loop.

docs.title: Components (all new)
docs.text:
Path Purpose deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py The agent (pure Python 3 stdlib), long-running control loop. deploy/kiosk-agent/test_display_agent.py pytest unit tests for decision + next-boundary logic. deploy/systemd/calvin-display-agent.service Type=simple, Restart=always, RestartSec=10; runs the agent as calvin with EnvironmentFile=/etc/default/calvin-kiosk and DISPLAY=:0; After=calvin-frontend.service. No timer — the agent sleeps internally.

Modified: - scripts/setup-kiosk.sh — install the script to /usr/local/bin/, install+enable the service/timer, and write the anti-blank openbox autostart (below). - scripts/setup-common.sh — configure_openbox_autostart emits the corrected xset block. - docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md — document Mode-B screen scheduling.

docs.title: Screen-blanking / DPMS configuration (the subtle part)
docs.text:
The kiosk runs X11/Xorg. Two independent concerns must not conflict:

  • Prevent automatic blanking (the original black-screen bug): screensaver + DPMS idle timers must be off.
  • Preserve on-demand power-off: the agent's xset dpms force off fallback requires DPMS to be enabled (capability present), just with no idle timers.

Correct openbox autostart block (replaces any xset -dpms, which would disable the capability and break scheduled off):

xset s off        # no screensaver
xset s noblank
xset +dpms        # DPMS capability ON …
xset dpms 0 0 0   # … but no automatic standby/suspend/off timers

vcgencmd display_power is independent of X DPMS state and is tried first; xset is the fallback for hosts where vcgencmd is a no-op under the KMS driver.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• Config fetch fails / times out → log, keep the last applied state, short backoff (60s), retry. Never blank a working display on a blip.
  • vcgencmd absent or ineffective → fall through to xset.
  • Malformed schedule/time values → treat as "keep on" (matches backend's defensive fallbacks).
  • Agent crash → Restart=always brings it back; it re-reads config and re-establishes state on startup (startup always applies once, regardless of last-state tracking).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Pure-logic unit tests (no hardware, no network) over the decision core, pinned from validation already run against the live server: - Standard window 06:00–22:00: off before 06:00, on 06:00–21:59, off from 22:00, off overnight. - Midnight-spanning 20:00–07:00: on 20:00→06:59 across midnight, off 07:00–19:59. - display_schedule_enabled false ⇒ always on. - Day not in schedule / entry disabled ⇒ on. - Malformed onTime ⇒ on (defensive). - Config-fetch failure path ⇒ no state change (mock the fetch to raise; assert apply not called).

vcgencmd/xset invocation is covered by asserting the correct command is chosen for on vs off (subprocess mocked); no real hardware in CI.

Next-boundary logic (drives the sleep): with a 06:00–22:00 schedule and injected "now", seconds_to_next_boundary returns the correct next transition — e.g. at 09:00 → next is 22:00 today; at 23:00 → next is 06:00 tomorrow; midnight-spanning 20:00–07:00 at 23:00 → next is 07:00. Result is always capped by the refresh interval by the caller. "Apply only on change" is verified by asserting no command is issued when desired state equals last-applied (except the forced startup apply).

docs.title: Integration into setup-kiosk.sh
docs.text: New Mode-B installs get the agent automatically: install the script, install+enable calvin-display-agent.timer, and the corrected autostart block. CALVIN_BACKEND_URL already exists in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk, so the agent needs no extra config.

docs.title: Deploying to the existing (old-dev) Pi
docs.text: This session's Pi is an older native install (units calvin-backend/calvin-frontend, no /etc/default/calvin-kiosk). Manual deploy of the same artifact: 1. Create /etc/default/calvin-kiosk with CALVIN_BACKEND_URL=https://calvin.example.com. 2. Install calvin_display_agent.py to /usr/local/bin/, install+enable the timer. 3. Update the openbox autostart to the corrected xset block. 4. Files transferred via base64 -d | sudo tee one-liners (the Pi's terminal truncates multi-line pastes).

docs.title: Verification (live)
docs.text:
1. Deploy; confirm systemctl list-timers calvin-display-agent.timer shows it scheduled.
  2. Manually confirm which power method works on this panel (vcgencmd display_power 0 vs xset dpms force off) and record it.
  3. In Calvin's UI, enable the schedule with an off-window covering "now"; within ~60s the panel powers down. journalctl -u calvin-display-agent.service shows display -> OFF via <method>.
  4. Move the window so "now" is inside on-hours; panel powers back up.
  5. Restore the desired real schedule. ```

docs.title: Zero-touch kiosk provisioning — design
docs.text: Date: 2026-07-11 Status: Draft (awaiting review) Related: dd9 epic (per-kiosk settings model), dd9.2 (kiosk identity), scripts/setup-kiosk.sh, Deployment Topologies Mode B

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Bringing a new Mode-B kiosk online today means: flash Raspberry Pi OS, sort out headless wifi + SSH + hostname, SSH in, and hand-type sudo bash scripts/setup-kiosk.sh --backend-url http://…. Three distinct frictions, confirmed with the requester:

  1. Flashing / first boot — headless wifi, SSH, hostname, all manual.
  2. Typing config per-Pi — SSH in and hand-type the backend URL.
  3. Non-technical setup — the person bringing a kiosk online may not be comfortable with SSH/CLI at all.

Explicitly not a goal: reproducibility at large scale (this is a handful of kiosks, not dozens), and runtime backend discovery (mDNS). The backend URL is known when the card is prepared, and should be baked in so first boot is zero-touch.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: After a technical person prepares a card, a non-technical person should be able to plug in power and nothing else and end up at a running kiosk pointed at the right backend, with a stable CALVIN_KIOSK_ID. No SSH, no per-Pi typing on the device.

docs.title: Relationship to the client-handling / dd9 work
docs.text: The feature/client-arch settings rearchitecture (now in develop) and the dd9 epic (server-side per-kiosk config store, merged /api/config, per-kiosk content assignment) are complementary, not conflicting. Provisioning's job is to get a Pi onto wifi and pointed at a backend with a stable CALVIN_KIOSK_ID in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk. That identity + backend URL is exactly the foundation the dd9 config model consumes via /api/config?kiosk=<id>. This design deliberately establishes only that foundation and reuses the existing setup-kiosk.sh for everything else.

docs.title: Approaches considered
docs.text:
1. firstrun.sh generator + Raspberry Pi Imager (chosen). A small generator produces a first-boot bundle that stages wifi/hostname/SSH and then runs the existing setup-kiosk.sh unattended. No image to build or host; uses the OS's official first-boot mechanism; composes with setup-kiosk.sh.
  2. Local image-bake script. Download RPi OS Lite, inject the firstrun hook, emit a ready-to-flash calvin-kiosk.img. Most non-technical final step (flash one img, boot), but the most machinery to build and maintain (loopback mounts, a Linux host to run it, large artifacts). Deferred — a natural later upgrade if the boot-partition file copy proves too much.
  3. Document Imager + the existing one-liner. Zero new code, but still requires SSH + typing the URL — under-delivers on all three named frictions.

docs.title: Correction on mechanism
docs.text:
An earlier framing assumed Raspberry Pi OS's custom.toml could run setup-kiosk.sh. It cannot — custom.toml only covers wifi/hostname/SSH/locale and runs no arbitrary scripts. The mechanism that runs commands on first boot is firstrun.sh triggered from cmdline.txt (systemd.run=…). This design uses a single first-boot mechanism (firstrun.sh) and does not mix in custom.toml, to avoid two first-boot flows racing to reboot.

There is a real ordering subtlety: firstrun.sh runs before networking is up, but setup-kiosk.sh needs the network (apt, git, curl). So firstrun.sh only stages offline config and enables a one-shot service that runs setup-kiosk.sh after network-online.target.

docs.title: 1. scripts/bake-kiosk-firstrun.sh (new)
docs.text:
The generator. A technical person runs it once per site against a freshly flashed card's boot partition:

sudo bash scripts/bake-kiosk-firstrun.sh \
  --backend-url http://homeserver.local:8000 \
  --wifi-ssid HomeNet --wifi-psk secret --wifi-country SE \
  --hostname kitchen \
  --ssh-pubkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub \
  --boot-dir /media/$USER/bootfs

It writes onto the boot partition:

  • a generated firstrun.sh, and
  • a one-line append to cmdline.txt (systemd.run=… systemd.run_success_action=reboot systemd.unit=kernel-command-line.target).

Reuses setup-common.sh helpers (upsert_env_value, logging) so there is one source of truth for how /etc/default/calvin-kiosk is shaped.

docs.title: 2. Generated firstrun.sh (offline staging only)
docs.text:
Runs on boot 1, before networking:

  • Sets hostname.
  • Writes a NetworkManager keyfile for wifi (Bookworm-native, /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/…nmconnection, chmod 600).
  • Enables SSH; installs the provided --ssh-pubkey (key-only; no password).
  • Seeds /etc/default/calvin-kiosk with CALVIN_BACKEND_URL using the same env-file shape as setup-kiosk.sh's install_kiosk_config.
  • Installs and enables calvin-kiosk-firstboot.service.
  • Removes its own cmdline.txt hook so it never re-runs, then reboots.

docs.title: 3. calvin-kiosk-firstboot.service + wrapper (new, under deploy/)
docs.text:
A oneshot unit, After=network-online.target / Wants=network-online.target. Runs on boot 2, once the network is up:

  • Invokes the existing setup-kiosk.sh --backend-url <seeded url>.
  • On success: writes a sentinel, systemctl disables itself, reboots into the kiosk.
  • On failure: leaves logs in journalctl -u calvin-kiosk-firstboot; SSH is already enabled for recovery; the sentinel is not written so a manual re-run is possible.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
bake script  →  writes firstrun.sh + cmdline.txt hook onto boot partition
   │
boot 1 (firstrun.sh, no network): hostname + wifi + ssh + seed env
         + enable firstboot service, remove cmdline hook  →  reboot
   │
boot 2 (network up): firstboot service runs setup-kiosk.sh
         → installs X/openbox/chromium + calvin-* units → reboot
   │
boot 3: kiosk is live, registered at /api/config?kiosk=<CALVIN_KIOSK_ID>

The non-technical person only ever plugs in power.

docs.title: Reuse / boundaries
docs.text:
• The bake script and firstboot wrapper are thin: they get the card to the point where the existing, tested setup-kiosk.sh runs unattended. No provisioning logic is duplicated.
  • Kiosk identity (dd9.2), the display-power agent, and rotation all come along for free because they already live in setup-kiosk.sh.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Bake script validates:

  • --backend-url matches ^https?:// (same check as setup-kiosk.sh).
  • --boot-dir exists and looks like a boot partition (contains cmdline.txt).
  • --wifi-country is present when wifi is requested (regulatory domain — otherwise wifi silently fails to associate).
  • Refuses to append the cmdline.txt hook twice (idempotent re-runs).

Firstboot service: idempotent via sentinel; failures are recoverable over the already-enabled SSH.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
bats tests for bake-kiosk-firstrun.sh, mirroring the existing scripts/tests/ pattern — all at the filesystem level, no real Pi needed:

  • Arg validation (missing/invalid --backend-url, missing --boot-dir, missing wifi country).
  • Correct files written into a temp "boot-dir".
  • cmdline.txt hook appended exactly once across repeated runs.
  • Generated firstrun.sh seeds the env file with the right URL/hostname and installs the SSH key.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
• New docs/setup/KIOSK_PROVISIONING.md — flash → bake → boot walkthrough.
  • Link it from DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md (Mode B) and SETUP_SCRIPTS.md.

docs.title: Resolved decisions
docs.text:
• Wifi optional. If the operator uses Imager's own wifi UI, --wifi-* may be omitted; the bake script then only stages the setup trigger.
  • SSH key-only. Default is --ssh-pubkey (no password), since these are headless devices.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Full prebaked/hosted .img (Approach 2) — deferred.
  • Runtime backend discovery via mDNS — the URL is known at flash time.
  • Large-scale fleet imaging.
  • Any change to the dd9 per-kiosk config store; this only establishes the identity + backend URL it builds on.

docs.title: Per-device (per-kiosk) settings model — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-11
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Epic: calvin-dd9
  • Children: dd9.1 (Tier-1 display settings), dd9.2 (kiosk identity — keystone), dd9.3 (per-kiosk config store + merged /api/config), dd9.4 (content assignment), dd9.5 (multi-screen), dd9.6 (orientation home), dd9.7 (SSE upgrade — deferred)
  • Base branch: develop (this design lives on feature/dd9-kiosk-model)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Calvin is shifting from all-in-one Pis (Mode A) to a central server + multiple dumb kiosk Pis (Mode B, see DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md). In Mode B the backend and its data live on a server; each Pi runs only Chromium against the server URL.

The server config is a single flat global JSON blob served at GET /api/config (stored as key-value rows in ConfigDB via config_service, merged on PUT). It mixes three concerns that no longer share a home once one server drives many kiosks:

  1. Device-physical — orientation, orientationFlipped, applyDisplayRotation (and, in scope for this epic, brightness / resolution / which HDMI output). These are physical to a specific Pi. The backend used to apply them locally via xrandr/vcgencmd in the main.py lifespan (display_orientation_service, display_power_service); a remote backend cannot reach a kiosk's display.
  2. Content/layout — dashboardLayout, dashboardScreens (already a version: 2 model with a screens[] catalog + activeScreenId). Different kiosks may want to show different screens.
  3. UI prefs — theme, time format, keyboard combos, etc. Genuinely global.

Two regressions triggered this epic (screen power schedule and rotation on a converted Pi); both are instances of the same gap. Screen scheduling was already solved with a device-local display-agent (deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py) that reads the schedule from /api/config and applies it locally. This epic defines the broader model.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• A stable per-kiosk identity so the server can distinguish kiosks (the keystone).
  • A single config resolution model (layered merge) that yields a per-kiosk view of config.
  • UI-authored device-physical settings (rotation/brightness/output) with no SSH — the display-agent applies them device-side from values the server hands it.
  • Per-kiosk content assignment without re-authoring dashboards.
  • Full backward compatibility: a request with no kiosk id behaves exactly as today.

docs.title: Non-goals (this epic / deferred)
docs.text:
• SSE push for instant apply — deferred to dd9.7 (version-poll is the core mechanism).
  • Multi-output-per-Pi content mapping — dd9.5, an optional extension of the content override.
  • Reworking the global UI-prefs set. Those stay global.

docs.title: The model — layered resolution (decision: option A)
docs.text:
The server holds global config (unchanged, in ConfigDB) plus an optional sparse per-kiosk overrides map. A kiosk's effective config is:

device-local env (/etc/default/calvin-kiosk, optional escape hatch)
        ▲ wins over
per-kiosk override (server, authored in UI)   ← primary authoring surface
        ▲ wins over
global config (server default)
  • GET /api/config?kiosk=<id> → deepmerge(global, overrides[id]).
  • No kiosk param ⇒ no override lookup ⇒ exactly today's global response.
  • Sparse: a kiosk inherits global for every field it doesn't override. A global change reaches every kiosk that hasn't overridden that field.

This one mental model subsumes dd9.3 (per-kiosk store + merged config), dd9.4 (content), and dd9.6 (orientation): each is just a field resolved through the layers.

docs.title: Device-physical settings: authored in server config, applied by the agent
docs.text:
Key design pivot from the original two-tier sketch: device-physical settings (rotation/brightness/output) are authored per-kiosk in the server config / UI, not in a device-local env file. The backend still can't run xrandr on a remote Pi — so the display-agent is the device-side applicator:

  1. Agent knows its own CALVIN_KIOSK_ID (see identity below).
  2. Agent reads GET ${CALVIN_BACKEND_URL}/api/config?kiosk=<id> (already polls this URL for the schedule).
  3. If rotation/brightness/output changed since last apply, it runs xrandr (rotation/mode/ output) or backlight sysfs/ddcutil (brightness). xrandr --output X --rotate left applies live while Chromium runs — no reboot.

The device-local /etc/default/calvin-kiosk shrinks to bootstrap only (CALVIN_BACKEND_URL, CALVIN_KIOSK_ID), plus an optional escape hatch: CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION (and future CALVIN_DISPLAY_*) remain honored and win over the UI value, per the precedence order, for break-glass on a misbehaving Pi without touching the server. This env already ships on develop; keeping it is backward-compatible.

docs.title: Kiosk identity (dd9.2 — the keystone)
docs.text:
• Storage: CALVIN_KIOSK_ID in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk, written once by setup-kiosk.sh. Operator-editable to a friendly name (kitchen, hallway).
  • Default recipe: <hostname>-<suffix>, where <suffix> is a short (~6-char) slice of a stable per-device source, in preference order:
  • /etc/machine-id (present on all systemd Pis; changes on re-image — correct, a re-imaged card is a new kiosk)
  • primary NIC MAC (fallback)
  • Pi CPU serial from /proc/cpuinfo (last resort)

Rationale: a stock Pi OS image defaults the hostname to raspberrypi, so hostname alone collides across multiple Pis. Two stock Pis become raspberrypi-3f9a2c / raspberrypi-b71e04 — unique, stable, readable. - Transport: query param ?kiosk=<id> on /api/config and data requests, baked into the Chromium kiosk URL. Chosen because it's the only option that survives the Mode-B constraints (dumb Pi, no proxy, top-level Chromium navigation can't set request headers) without extra machinery, and the display-agent reuses the same param verbatim. The frontend reads the id from its own URL and threads it onto its API/XHR calls. - Registration: on any request carrying a kiosk id, the server upserts a Kiosk row (id, hostname, last-seen). The UI can then list/manage known kiosks.

docs.title: Server storage — Kiosk table (decision: dedicated table)
docs.text:
Introduce one Ormar/SQLite model, matching the existing ORM idiom. The kiosk registry (dd9.2) and the overrides store (dd9.3) are the same table:

column purpose id (PK) CALVIN_KIOSK_ID hostname reported by the kiosk (shown next to id to spot duplicates) last_seen updated on each request carrying the id last_applied_version device-config version the agent last confirmed applied overrides (JSON) sparse per-kiosk config (device-physical + content fields)

Global config stays in ConfigDB / config_service, untouched. No id on a request ⇒ no table lookup ⇒ today's exact behavior. DB writes wrap with retry_on_db_locked per house rules.

docs.title: The nudge — version-poll / conditional GET (dd9.x, core; SSE = dd9.7)
docs.text:
So a UI change applies without SSH and feels near-instant:

  • Server computes a cheap deviceConfigVersion per kiosk = hash of that kiosk's resolved device-physical settings (rotation/brightness/output/schedule). Exposed as an ETag on GET /api/config?kiosk=<id> (or a tiny GET /api/kiosk/<id>/device-version → {version}).
  • Agent runs two cadences: a cheap fast-poll every ~10–15s (If-None-Match → usually 304), plus its existing slow full-refresh. On version change → fetch → diff → apply.
  • "Apply now" in the UI is not a special endpoint — a normal save bumps the version; the agent catches it within one fast-poll (~15s).
  • Confirmation loop: on apply, the agent POSTs back its last_applied_version + result, so the UI can show Applied ✓ / applying… / kiosk offline instead of firing blind.

Rationale: near-instant feel with no persistent connections; survives network drops/proxies; matches the codebase's existing polling idiom (configPollInterval, the agent's schedule poll). StreamingResponse(text/event-stream) is already proven in system.py, but the only existing SSE is a bespoke update-log tailer, so a real push channel is genuinely new infra → deferred to dd9.7.

docs.title: Content assignment (dd9.4; multi-screen dd9.5 deferred)
docs.text:
Keep the screens[] catalog global (authored once in the UI). The per-kiosk override adds two small fields only:

  • availableScreens: [ids] — optional allowlist of which global screens this Pi may show (default: all). The kiosk's existing screen-switching UI/keyboard is unchanged, just filtered to this set.
  • defaultScreenId — which screen this Pi boots into. Runtime activeScreenId stays local + user-switchable; the per-kiosk default just seeds it.

No per-kiosk screen authoring. Multi-output (dd9.5) later adds an optional outputScreenMap (e.g. {"HDMI-1":"screen-home","HDMI-2":"screen-agenda"}) on the same override — a future extension, not built in the core.

docs.title: Orientation decision (dd9.6)
docs.text:
• Canonical home: per-kiosk server config, authored in the UI, applied device-side by the display-agent. (This resolves dd9.6 toward option (b)/(c) with device-local winning as the escape hatch — consistent with the shipped rotation work.) Orientation/rotation is stripped from / not authoritative in the un-scoped global response for a kiosk that has a per-kiosk value; global remains a default.
  • display_orientation_service (main.py lifespan, backend-local xrandr): make it Mode-A-only — no-op / skip when it can't reach a local display — so single-Pi setups keep working and Mode B doesn't error. (Not deleted; least-disruptive.)
  • Settings UI orientation control: keep it, but it now writes the per-kiosk override (when a kiosk is selected) or the global default (unscoped). Relabel accordingly.

docs.title: UI surface
docs.text:
• A Kiosks view (extends the settings area; DeviceSettings.vue / DisplaySettings.vue are the neighbors) lists known kiosks from the Kiosk table: id, hostname, last-seen, apply status.
  • Selecting a kiosk scopes the device-physical + content controls to that kiosk's override; unscoped edits write the global default. Prefer schema-driven rendering where the existing settings components already cover the field type (house rule: schema-driven UI first).

docs.title: Backward compatibility
docs.text:
• No kiosk param anywhere ⇒ no Kiosk lookup ⇒ GET /api/config returns today's global blob.
  • Mode-A all-in-one Pi keeps working: display_orientation_service still applies locally (Mode-A-only guard is a no-op there), and a Mode-A install can run without a kiosk id.
  • The device-local CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION escape hatch keeps its current semantics.

docs.title: Affected code (anchors)
docs.text: Area Path Config route (GET/PUT /api/config) backend/app/api/routes/config.py Config storage backend/app/services/config_service.py, backend/app/models/db_models.py (ConfigDB; new Kiosk model) Backend-local display services backend/app/services/display_orientation_service.py, display_power_service.py, backend/app/main.py lifespan Display-agent (device-side applicator) deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py (+ tests) Kiosk provisioning scripts/setup-kiosk.sh, deploy/calvin.env.example, /etc/default/calvin-kiosk Frontend config polling + kiosk id threading frontend/src/stores/config.js (+ related stores), kiosk URL Settings UI frontend/src/components/settings/categories/DeviceSettings.vue, DisplaySettings.vue, new Kiosks view Docs docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md

docs.title: Incremental delivery (maps to children)
docs.text:
1. dd9.2 (keystone): Kiosk model + upsert-on-request; CALVIN_KIOSK_ID in setup-kiosk.sh (default recipe); query-param transport; frontend threads the id; server records/lists kiosks. No behavior change without an id.
  2. dd9.3: overrides column + merged GET /api/config?kiosk=<id>; deviceConfigVersion /ETag; agent fast-poll + apply + confirmation POST-back.
  3. dd9.6: move orientation authoring to per-kiosk/global-default; Mode-A-only guard on display_orientation_service; relabel the UI control.
  4. dd9.1 follow-ups: extend the agent's device-physical application to brightness / resolution / primary-output, driven by the same override fields.
  5. dd9.4: availableScreens + defaultScreenId override + Kiosks UI scoping.
  6. dd9.5: optional outputScreenMap for multi-output Pis.
  7. dd9.7: SSE push channel replacing the version-poll for instant apply (also evaluate pushing config to the browser + live kiosk status).

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text:
• Backend: unit tests for layered deepmerge(global, overrides) incl. sparse + empty cases; Kiosk upsert/registry; deviceConfigVersion stability (same inputs → same hash) and change detection; GET /api/config unchanged when no id (regression guard for backward compat).
  • Agent: extend deploy/kiosk-agent/test_display_agent.py — version-poll 304 fast path, apply-on-change, escape-hatch env precedence, confirmation POST-back.
  • Frontend: config store threads kiosk id onto requests; Kiosks list renders registry.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. Deferred by design: SSE (dd9.7), multi-output mapping (dd9.5), and the exact brightness backend (backlight sysfs vs ddcutil) which is a dd9.1 follow-up detail.

docs.title: dd9.3 — Server-side per-kiosk config store + per-kiosk config endpoints — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-12
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issue: calvin-dd9.3 (epic calvin-dd9)
  • Base branch: develop (this design lives on feature/dd9.3-per-kiosk-config)
  • Builds on: dd9.2 (kiosk identity). The whole-epic model is in 2026-07-11-per-kiosk-settings-model-design.md; this doc pins the dd9.3-specific decisions.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: dd9.2 gave each kiosk a stable identity and a registry (kiosks table with an unused overrides JSON column + last_applied_version, and GET /api/kiosks). Today the kiosk carries its id as ?kiosk=<id> on GET /api/config, which only records the kiosk and returns global config unchanged. This slice adds the per-kiosk config layer: a place to store sparse overrides per kiosk, a way for each kiosk to read its effective (merged) config, and a cheap version signal the (future) display-agent will poll to know when to re-apply device-physical settings.

docs.title: API shape (decision: consolidate under /api/kiosks/{id})
docs.text:
The per-kiosk surface lives entirely under /api/kiosks/{id}; /api/config goes back to meaning only "global". Exactly one endpoint per persona:

Endpoint Persona Returns / does GET /api/config Mode-A Pi / no identity Global config (also the template kiosks inherit). Unchanged. GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config client (browser + display-agent) That kiosk's effective (merged) config. Records the kiosk. ETag + 304. GET/PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides admin (future UI / curl) The raw sparse override layer.

"Effective config" (the computed result a client runs) and "the override layer" (the sparse thing an admin edits) are genuinely different resources — not a query-param toggle on /api/config. This retires the ?kiosk=/?khost= params on /api/config: a kiosk now registers itself by fetching its own config endpoint.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Store a sparse per-kiosk override layer; read/write it via GET/PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides.
  • GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config returns shallow-merge(global, overrides[id]) and records the kiosk (last-seen, ?khost= hostname).
  • Expose a deviceConfigVersion (ETag + body field) on the effective-config read so the future agent can detect device-physical changes cheaply.
  • Backward compatible for Mode A: GET /api/config (no id) is byte-identical to today.
  • A kiosk with no overrides ⇒ its effective config == defaulted global (plus the version field).

docs.title: Non-goals (deferred)
docs.text:
• The display-agent apply loop (read device-physical, xrandr/backlight, If-None-Match fast-poll, POST back last_applied_version) — its own later slice, merges with dd9.1. This slice is testable with API + unit tests, no Pi.
  • Content-assignment keys (availableScreens, defaultScreenId) — dd9.4; just more override keys, no new mechanism.
  • The admin write UI — a later slice once the backend is complete.

docs.title: 1. Storage — reuse KioskDB.overrides
docs.text: The overrides JSON column already exists (dd9.2). It holds a sparse dict of config fields, e.g. {"orientation": "portrait", "displayScheduleEnabled": true}. No migration. null/absent ⇒ no overrides.

docs.title: 2. DRY refactor — extract the global-config builder
docs.text:
get_config in backend/app/api/routes/config.py builds the global dict then applies ~150 lines of inline defaults. The effective-config endpoint needs the same defaulted global as its merge base, so extract that into a reusable helper rather than duplicating it:

  • async build_global_config() -> dict (in config_service or a config route helper) — returns the fully-defaulted global config (including frontendVersion, devMode).
  • GET /api/config becomes a thin wrapper: return await build_global_config(). Its kiosk/ khost params are removed (retired).

docs.title: 3. Effective-config read — GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config
docs.text:
The single endpoint a client (browser + agent) reads in Mode B.

  1. Validate {id} against _KIOSK_ID_RE (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$, reuse from kiosk_registry); 400 on bad shape.
  2. Record the kiosk best-effort: record_kiosk(id, hostname=khost) (from ?khost=<host>), wrapped in try/except + logger.warning (same hardening as dd9.2's config recording).
  3. base = await build_global_config(); overrides = await get_overrides(id); merged = merge_overrides(base, overrides) (shallow top-level: each override key replaces that global key; no recursion, no array merge).
  4. version = device_config_version(merged); attach as body field deviceConfigVersion and as an ETag header. If the request's If-None-Match equals version, return 304 Not Modified (no body).
  5. Merged config includes device-physical values (served, not stripped) — the agent reads them; the browser ignores what it can't act on in Mode B.

An unknown kiosk id here is not an error: it records the kiosk and returns defaulted global + version (a kiosk's first-ever fetch registers it). Invalid shape is a 400.

docs.title: 4. Override layer CRUD — GET/PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides
docs.text:
• GET → {"id": <id>, "overrides": {...}} — the raw stored layer (NOT merged). 404 if the kiosk id is unknown (you can't read overrides of a kiosk that doesn't exist). 400 on bad id shape.
  • PUT body {"overrides": {...}} → replaces the whole layer (idempotent; the editor does read-modify-write). PUT {"overrides": {}} clears. Upserts the kiosk row if new (pre-provisioning). 400 on bad id shape or malformed body. Wrap the write with retry_on_db_locked.
  • Validation: the overrides object is validated by the existing ConfigUpdate model (extra="allow" — unknown keys pass, declared keys type-checked). Reject a non-object body; cap serialized size (reject > 64 KB). No hand-maintained per-kiosk allowlist — the UI controls which fields it exposes.

docs.title: 5. deviceConfigVersion — ETag + body field
docs.text:
• DEVICE_PHYSICAL_KEYS — a module constant naming the keys a device-agent applies: orientation, orientationFlipped, applyDisplayRotation, displayScheduleEnabled, displaySchedule (current), plus reserved displayBrightness, displayOutput, displayResolution (harmless if absent). One place to extend as dd9.1 follow-ups land.
  • Version = short hex of sha256(json.dumps({k: merged.get(k) for k in DEVICE_PHYSICAL_KEYS}, sort_keys=True, default=str)). Stable (sorted keys); any device-physical change ⇒ new version; theme/time-format changes do not bump it.

docs.title: 6. Service layer (app/services/kiosk_registry.py)
docs.text: Pure functions (DB-free, unit-testable) + thin DB accessors: - def merge_overrides(base: dict, overrides: dict | None) -> dict — shallow top-level merge. - def device_config_version(merged: dict) -> str — the hash helper. - async get_overrides(kiosk_id) -> dict | None — raw layer, None if kiosk unknown. - async set_overrides(kiosk_id, overrides: dict) -> None — upsert row + replace overrides (retry_on_db_locked). - record_kiosk / list_kiosks — reuse from dd9.2.

docs.title: 7. Frontend — withKiosk becomes a URL selector
docs.text:
dd9.2's withKiosk() appended ?kiosk=&khost= to /api/config. Change it to a URL selector so a scoped client fetches its own endpoint: - frontend/src/utils/kioskId.js: replace withKiosk(url) with configUrl() — when getKioskId() is set, return /api/kiosks/{id}/config?khost=<encoded host>; else /api/config. - frontend/src/stores/config.js: the GET uses configUrl(). The POST stays axios.post("/api/config", ...) = global (per-kiosk override writes are the future admin UI via PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides, not the config store's normal save).

This keeps the frontend change small and contained (it's our own unreleased dd9.2 code).

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Browser / display-agent  (Mode B, has id)
  └─ GET /api/kiosks/hallway-3f9a2c/config?khost=pi-hallway   [If-None-Match: <etag>?]
        └─ validate id shape
        └─ record_kiosk(id, hostname=khost)          (best-effort)
        └─ base    = build_global_config()           (shared with /api/config)
        └─ overrides = get_overrides(id)
        └─ merged  = merge_overrides(base, overrides)   (shallow)
        └─ version = device_config_version(merged)
        └─ If-None-Match == version ? 304 : 200 + ETag + body{..., deviceConfigVersion}

Mode-A Pi / no identity
  └─ GET /api/config → build_global_config()          (global, unchanged)

Admin UI (future) / curl
  └─ GET /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides  → { id, overrides }
  └─ PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides  { overrides:{...} } → upsert + replace

docs.title: Backward compatibility
docs.text:
• Mode A: GET /api/config (no id) is byte-identical to today (regression test).
  • dd9.2 recording relocates: the ?kiosk=/?khost= params + recording move off /api/config onto GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config. dd9.2's recording integration tests are updated/relocated to the new endpoint; test_get_config_no_kiosk_unchanged becomes the Mode-A regression guard.
  • New kiosk / no overrides ⇒ effective config == defaulted global (plus deviceConfigVersion).
  • POST /api/config stays global-only (unchanged).

docs.title: Affected code
docs.text:
Area Path Extract build_global_config; GET /api/config → global-only (drop kiosk params) backend/app/api/routes/config.py Effective-config + override CRUD routes backend/app/api/routes/kiosks.py Service: overrides + merge + version helpers backend/app/services/kiosk_registry.py Reuse id-shape regex / ConfigUpdate validation kiosk_registry.py / config.py Frontend URL selector frontend/src/utils/kioskId.js, frontend/src/stores/config.js Tests backend/tests/unit/test_kiosk_registry.py, backend/tests/integration/test_api_config.py, test_api_kiosks.py, frontend/tests/unit/kioskId.spec.js Docs docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md (kiosk-identity section → per-kiosk config + endpoints)

No migration (column exists). No new dependency. OpenAPI snapshot + generated types.ts regenerate (additive: new kiosk endpoints, /api/config loses its query params).

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text:
• Unit (pure, no DB): merge_overrides — override wins, sparse fall-through, empty/None == base, top-level-only (nested key replaces wholesale). device_config_version — stable for same inputs; bumps on a device-physical key change; unchanged on a non-device-physical change.
  • Service: get_overrides (unknown → None), set_overrides (upsert new kiosk; replace; clear via {}).
  • Integration: PUT then GET /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides round-trip; GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config reflects overrides and records the kiosk; GET /api/config unchanged (Mode-A regression); unknown-kiosk effective == global; ETag present + If-None-Match → 304; invalid id → 400; oversized override body → rejected; POST /api/config still writes global.
  • Frontend: configUrl() returns /api/kiosks/{id}/config?khost=… when an id is present, /api/config when not; config store GET uses it; POST stays /api/config.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. Deferred by design: the display-agent apply loop (own slice), content-assignment override keys (dd9.4), the write UI (later). The deviceConfigVersion surface (ETag + body field) is deliberately enough for the agent slice without a dedicated version endpoint now.

docs.title: dd9.4 — Per-kiosk content assignment (available screens + default screen) — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-12
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issue: calvin-dd9.4 (epic calvin-dd9)
  • Base branch: develop (this design lives on feature/dd9.4-per-kiosk-content)
  • Builds on: dd9.2 (kiosk identity), dd9.3 (per-kiosk override store + effective-config endpoint). Whole-epic model: 2026-07-11-per-kiosk-settings-model-design.md.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A kiosk shows one of several screens from a global catalog (dashboardScreens = {version, activeScreenId, screens[]}). Two gaps block multi-kiosk use:

  1. No per-kiosk assignment: every kiosk shows the same screens; you can't say "the kitchen Pi shows only the calendar screen, the hallway Pi boots into the agenda screen."
  2. The active screen is global and persisted. Switching screens — keyboard screen_jump (useKeyboardActions.js saveDashboardScreens) or the ScreenDots switcher (config.js activateDashboardScreen/cycleDashboardScreenBy) — calls updateConfig({ dashboardScreens }), writing activeScreenId into global config. In Mode B, switching on one kiosk changes the active screen for all kiosks.

dd9.4 delivers per-kiosk content assignment and fixes (2), which is a prerequisite: without it, any screen switch clobbers the per-kiosk assignment.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Runtime active screen is client-local in Mode B (kiosk id present): seeded on load, updated on switch, never written to the server. Mode A (no id) keeps today's global-persist behavior exactly. (Decision A.)
  • Two override keys carry the assignment; they flow through dd9.3's effective-config merge with no new endpoints:
  • availableScreens: list[str] | None — allowlist of screen ids this kiosk may show (absent/null ⇒ all).
  • defaultScreenId: str | None — the screen this kiosk boots into.
  • The screen catalog stays global (authored once in DashboardRegionsEditor). dd9.4 only selects/filters, never forks the catalog.
  • Setting the keys is via the API (PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides, dd9.3). The friendly admin UI is the deferred management-UI slice, not dd9.4.

docs.title: 1. Backend — type the two keys (2-line change)
docs.text:
Add to ConfigUpdate in backend/app/api/routes/config.py: 

availableScreens: list[str] | None = None
defaultScreenId: str | None = None
This lets PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides type-check them (dd9.3 validates the override body via ConfigUpdate). They already merge into the effective config via dd9.3's shallow merge and are served on GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config. No new endpoint, no migration.

docs.title: 2. Frontend — local active screen that survives polling (the meat)
docs.text:
The config store polls the effective config every configPollInterval (~30s) and re-applies it. A naive "switch mutates dashboardScreens locally" would be clobbered on the next poll. So the active screen becomes a dedicated local ref, seeded once, preserved across polls, in Mode B.

In frontend/src/stores/config.js: - Add a local kioskActiveScreenId ref (null in Mode A). - Kiosk mode = getKioskId() != null (reuse dd9.2's kioskId.js). - Seeding (once, on first successful config load in kiosk mode): kioskActiveScreenId = firstValid(defaultScreenId, dashboardScreens.activeScreenId, firstAvailableScreenId) — see fallbacks below. - applyConfigPayload must NOT overwrite kioskActiveScreenId on subsequent polls (only seeds when still null). This is the key guard: server dashboardScreens.activeScreenId seeds but never re-steers a kiosk that has since switched. - An effectiveActiveScreenId getter: kiosk mode ⇒ kioskActiveScreenId; Mode A ⇒ dashboardScreens.value.activeScreenId (today's source of truth). - Switch actions branch on kiosk mode: - activateDashboardScreen(id) / cycleDashboardScreenBy(dir): kiosk mode ⇒ update kioskActiveScreenId locally, no updateConfig; Mode A ⇒ unchanged (mutate dashboardScreens + updateConfig). The keyboard path (useKeyboardActions.js saveDashboardScreens / activateFirstScreenContainingKind) routes through the same store actions so it inherits the branch. - Components that read the active screen (ClockBarHorizontal/Vertical via getActiveDashboardScreen, Dashboard.vue, ScreenDots) consume effectiveActiveScreenId (the store getter) instead of reading dashboardScreens.activeScreenId directly.

docs.title: 3. availableScreens filtering + seeding + fallbacks
docs.text:
• Filtering (kiosk mode): the switcher's visible screens = dashboardScreens.screens filtered to availableScreens (absent ⇒ all). ScreenDots renders only the allowed set; keyboard screen_jump/cycle actions skip disallowed screens. A kiosk cannot switch to a screen it isn't assigned.
  • Seed precedence for kioskActiveScreenId: defaultScreenId → else global dashboardScreens.activeScreenId → else first available screen.
  • Fallbacks (never render an empty/invalid screen):
  • defaultScreenId not in availableScreens, or not in the catalog ⇒ fall back to the first available screen.
  • availableScreens lists ids absent from the catalog ⇒ ignore those ids (intersect with the catalog).
  • availableScreens empty or resolves to nothing valid ⇒ treat as "all" (fail open — a blank kiosk is worse than an over-broad one).
  • If the current kioskActiveScreenId is no longer available (catalog edited server-side, picked up on poll) ⇒ re-seed to the first available.
  • Pure helpers (in frontend/src/utils/layout.js, next to the existing screen helpers) so this logic is unit-testable without a store: e.g. filterAvailableScreens(screens, availableIds) and resolveKioskActiveScreen({screens, availableScreens, defaultScreenId, current}).

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
GET /api/kiosks/hallway-1/config  (dd9.3)
  → effective config incl. { dashboardScreens (global catalog),
                             availableScreens?: [...], defaultScreenId?: "screen-agenda" }
  → config store: kiosk mode → seed kioskActiveScreenId once (default→global→first-available),
                  filter switcher to availableScreens
  → user presses screen_jump / taps ScreenDot:
       kiosk mode → kioskActiveScreenId = next allowed id  (LOCAL, no server write)
  → next 30s poll re-applies config → kioskActiveScreenId preserved (guard), catalog refreshed
Mode A (no kiosk id): unchanged — switch persists to global dashboardScreens.

docs.title: Backward compatibility
docs.text:
• Mode A (no kiosk id): every path unchanged — active screen still lives in global dashboardScreens.activeScreenId, switches still updateConfig. Regression-guarded.
  • A kiosk with no availableScreens/defaultScreenId overrides ⇒ all screens available, boots to the global active screen — i.e. current behavior, just now local (a switch no longer leaks to other kiosks).
  • The global catalog + DashboardRegionsEditor are untouched.

docs.title: Affected code
docs.text:
Area Path Type the 2 override keys backend/app/api/routes/config.py (ConfigUpdate) Local active-screen state + getter + seeded/guarded polling frontend/src/stores/config.js Switch actions branch on kiosk mode frontend/src/stores/config.js, frontend/src/composables/useKeyboardActions.js Pure filter/resolve helpers frontend/src/utils/layout.js Consume effectiveActiveScreenId + filtered screens ClockBarHorizontal.vue, ClockBarVertical.vue, views/Dashboard.vue, ui/ScreenDots.vue Kiosk-mode detection reuse frontend/src/utils/kioskId.js (getKioskId) Tests backend/tests/integration/test_api_kiosks.py, frontend/tests/unit/ (layout helpers + config store)

No new endpoint, no migration, no dependency.

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text:
• Backend: PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides accepts availableScreens/defaultScreenId (typed) and they appear in the effective config; a wrong type → 400 (dd9.3 handler).
  • Frontend (pure helpers): filterAvailableScreens (absent ⇒ all; intersect with catalog; empty ⇒ all). resolveKioskActiveScreen seed precedence + every fallback (invalid default, stale current, ids not in catalog).
  • Frontend (config store): Mode-A switch still calls updateConfig (regression); kiosk-mode switch updates kioskActiveScreenId with no network write; a config poll does not clobber a switched kioskActiveScreenId; seeding runs once; switcher/keyboard filtered to availableScreens.

docs.title: Non-goals / deferred
docs.text:
• Admin UI to set availableScreens/defaultScreenId per kiosk — the management-UI slice.
  • Per-kiosk region-view state (calendar rolling/counts via updateRegionView, cycleActiveDashboardRegionBy) — these still persist to global in Mode B; localizing them is a separate concern (note as a known limitation, not fixed here).
  • Multi-output (one Pi → multiple screens) — dd9.5.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. The region-view-state limitation is called out above as deliberately out of scope; if it proves annoying in practice, it's a small follow-up using the same kiosk-mode-local pattern.

docs.title: dd9.6 — Where 'orientation' lives (decision) + Mode-A guard — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-12
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issue: calvin-dd9.6 (epic calvin-dd9, type: decision)
  • Base branch: develop (this doc lives on feature/dd9.6-orientation-home)
  • Relates to: the whole-epic model 2026-07-11-per-kiosk-settings-model-design.md; builds on dd9.3 (per-kiosk override store).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The global server config holds orientation / orientationFlipped / applyDisplayRotation, applied at backend startup by display_orientation_service via xrandr. In server+kiosk (Mode B) this is wrong: orientation is physical to each Pi, but the setting is global and the backend can't reach a remote kiosk's display. This issue decides orientation's canonical home and precedence, and cleans up the one piece of live code that misbehaves in Mode B.

docs.title: Decision (ratified)
docs.text:
• Canonical home = per-kiosk server config (an override key), applied device-side by the display-agent. This is already true at the data layer: orientation / orientationFlipped / applyDisplayRotation are fields on ConfigUpdate (so dd9.3's PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides already accepts them) and are in DEVICE_PHYSICAL_KEYS (so the deviceConfigVersion bumps on an orientation change → the display-agent detects it). No new storage/serving work.
  • Precedence: device-local env (CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION, the break-glass escape hatch) > per-kiosk override (server) > global default.
  • Global config keeps orientation as a default — Mode-A single-Pi installs and the template new kiosks inherit it. It is not removed.

docs.title: The one code change — Mode-A guard on the startup sync
docs.text:
backend/app/main.py's _sync_display_orientation() calls display_orientation_service.sync_with_config() at startup, which runs xrandr on the backend's host. Today it guards on is_raspberry_pi() (so a non-Pi Docker server is already quiet) and catches exceptions, but a Pi acting as a remote backend with no local X display still hits xrandr, fails, and logs a warning every boot — and the intent ("orient the machine the backend runs on") is wrong in Mode B.

Change: gate the startup sync on a local display actually being present, reusing the existing has_x11() helper (app.utils.platform). If no local X display, skip at debug level and return early — do not call the service, do not run xrandr. When a local display is present, behavior is unchanged (Mode-A auto-orient-on-boot still works; genuine errors still warn).

Sketch (in _sync_display_orientation): 

from app.utils.platform import has_x11
if not has_x11():
    logger.debug("No local X display; skipping backend orientation sync (device-side agent owns it in Mode B)")
    return
# ... existing apply_rotation / sync_with_config logic unchanged ...

  • display_orientation_service itself (get_current_orientation / apply_orientation / sync_with_config) is kept — it's still the Mode-A path; it's just no longer invoked pointlessly on a display-less backend.
  • No new config or env flag: the guard auto-adapts (local display ⇒ Mode-A behavior; none ⇒ skip).

docs.title: Settings UI orientation control
docs.text: Keep as-is. It writes the global default orientation (a Mode-A convenience and the template new kiosks inherit). Per-kiosk orientation is set via the API (PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides) today; a friendly per-kiosk control is part of the deferred management-UI slice, not dd9.6.

docs.title: Affected code
docs.text:
Area Path Mode-A guard on startup sync backend/app/main.py (_sync_display_orientation) Reuse local-display check app.utils.platform.has_x11 (existing) Test backend/tests/ (unit test for the guard)

No migration, no new dependency, no API change. Orientation override storage/serving already shipped in dd9.3.

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text: • Unit: _sync_display_orientation (or an extracted testable unit) — when has_x11() is False, it returns early without calling display_orientation_service.sync_with_config (assert the service is not invoked; assert a debug-level, not warning-level, log). When has_x11() is True, it proceeds to the existing sync path (service called). Patch has_x11 and the service to assert the branch.

docs.title: Follow-ups (file, don't build here)
docs.text:
1. Display-agent applies orientation from the merged per-kiosk config (read orientation/ orientationFlipped from GET /api/kiosks/{id}/config, apply via xrandr, honor the CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env escape hatch as the winning layer). This is part of the deferred display-agent-apply slice (kin to dd9.1 follow-ups) — verify it's captured, file if not.
  2. Per-kiosk orientation control in the eventual management UI (set a kiosk's orientation override without curl) — part of the deferred management-UI slice.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None. The decision is ratified and the storage/serving already exists; dd9.6's only build is the Mode-A guard + tests + the two follow-up issues.

docs.title: Display-agent apply architecture (dd9.9 + dd9.5) — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-12
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issues: calvin-dd9.9 (agent applies per-kiosk device-physical — first slice, detailed here), calvin-dd9.5 (multi-output content routing — outlined; own detailed spec later)
  • Base branch: develop (this doc lives on feature/dd9.9-agent-apply)
  • Builds on: dd9.3 (per-kiosk effective config + deviceConfigVersion), dd9.6 (orientation is a per-kiosk override). Whole-epic model: 2026-07-11-per-kiosk-settings-model-design.md.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The per-kiosk override store serves device-physical settings (orientation, and future brightness/output) in each kiosk's effective config, but nothing on the Pi applies them: the backend can't reach a remote kiosk's display. The device-side display-agent (deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py) already polls config for the screen schedule and applies rotation once from an env var, but it does not read or apply per-kiosk device-physical config from the server. This design defines the agent's apply architecture and implements its first consumer (orientation, dd9.9); dd9.5 (multi-output) reuses the same foundation.

docs.title: Constraints (the agent's world)
docs.text:
• Pure Python 3 stdlib — the kiosk Pi has no venv. urllib/subprocess only; no requests.
  • Idempotent, no-reboot — apply via xrandr (works live). Re-apply only on change.
  • Fail-safe — a fetch/apply failure must never crash the agent; log and continue the loop.
  • Testable — run(...) already takes injectable fetch/sleep; add an injectable applier so the apply path is unit-testable without a real display.

docs.title: 1. Effective-config fetch (unify on the per-kiosk endpoint)
docs.text:
fetch_config(backend_url) currently GETs ${backend}/api/config (global). Change it to fetch the kiosk's effective config when a kiosk id is present:

  • Read CALVIN_KIOSK_ID from env (dd9.2 writes it to /etc/default/calvin-kiosk).
  • If set: GET ${backend}/api/kiosks/{id}/config?khost=<hostname> — the merged config incl. per-kiosk overrides and deviceConfigVersion.
  • If unset: GET ${backend}/api/config (today's global behavior — backward compatible).

One fetch now feeds both the schedule and device-physical, so the schedule becomes per-kiosk too (a feature: different kiosks can have different on/off times).

docs.title: 2. Version-gated device-physical apply
docs.text:
The agent tracks the last-applied deviceConfigVersion (from dd9.3, present in the config body). On each poll: - read cfg["deviceConfigVersion"]; - if it differs from the last one the agent applied → run the device-physical apply step, then store the new version; - if unchanged → skip (no xrandr churn).

This reuses the server-computed hash — no extra request, no local diffing of individual keys. (The ETag/If-None-Match → 304 optimization is deliberately skipped: the agent already fetches the full config for the schedule, so the version rides along in the body.)

State: a small in-memory last_applied_version in the loop (reset on agent restart, so a restart re-applies once — correct and cheap). POST-back of last_applied_version to the server is deferred (management-UI/confirmation slice) — dd9.9 tracks locally only.

docs.title: 3. Escape-hatch precedence
docs.text:
CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env (device-local break-glass) wins over the server orientation: - if the env is set (non-empty) → apply that xrandr value, ignore the server's orientation; - else → apply the orientation derived from the effective config.

This preserves dd9.1's device-local override as the top precedence layer: device-local env > per-kiosk override > global default (the last two are already resolved server-side by dd9.3's merge; the agent only adds the env layer on top).

docs.title: dd9.9 — orientation apply (first slice, detailed)
docs.text:
Add device-physical apply to the loop, with orientation as the one consumer.

  • Trigger: on a deviceConfigVersion change (per §2), and once at startup.
  • Precedence: if CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env set → use it (existing startup behavior, now also the winning layer in the loop). Else derive from config.
  • Gate: only apply if applyDisplayRotation (config, default True) is truthy.
  • Mapping (server config → xrandr rotate value) — match display_orientation_service exactly: 
    if orientationFlipped:      rotation = "inverted"
elif orientation == "portrait": rotation = "left"
else:                       rotation = "normal"   # landscape / unknown
    (config keys read tolerantly for both camelCase and snake_case, like the existing cfg_get.)
  • Apply: reuse apply_rotation(rotation, output) + detect_primary_output() (or CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT env). These already exist.
  • Structure: extract an apply_device_physical(cfg, *, applier=apply_rotation, env=os.environ) function (pure-ish, injectable applier) called from run() when the version changed. Keep it small and separate from the schedule reconcile.

docs.title: Data flow (dd9.9)
docs.text:
loop (run):
  cfg = fetch_config(backend)            # /api/kiosks/{id}/config (effective) or /api/config
  if cfg["deviceConfigVersion"] != last_applied_version:
      apply_device_physical(cfg)         # orientation -> xrandr (env escape hatch wins)
      last_applied_version = cfg["deviceConfigVersion"]
  reconcile_schedule(cfg, now)           # existing on/off logic, now per-kiosk
  sleep(until next boundary or refresh)

docs.title: Testing (dd9.9)
docs.text: Reuse the existing dependency-injection test pattern (run(..., fetch=fake, sleep=fake, iterations=N), inject a fake applier): - orientation change (version bump) → applier called once with the mapped xrandr value; portrait→left, landscape→normal, flipped→inverted. - unchanged version across polls → applier NOT called again (version-gating works). - CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env set → env value applied, server orientation ignored. - applyDisplayRotation=false → no apply. - fetch failure → loop continues, no crash (existing behavior preserved). - CALVIN_KIOSK_ID set → fetch_config targets /api/kiosks/{id}/config; unset → /api/config.

docs.title: dd9.5 — multi-output content routing (outline only; own spec later)
docs.text: Reuses this loop + effective-config fetch, and adds a distinct, larger dimension: - An outputScreenMap override, e.g. {"HDMI-1": "screen-home", "HDMI-2": "screen-agenda"}. - The agent configures the X multi-output layout (xrandr per output) and launches a Chromium per output, each pointed at its assigned screen (URL carries the kiosk id + which screen/output). - This is meatier (multi-Chromium lifecycle + X layout + content routing) and gets its own brainstorm → spec → plan when we reach it. The only commitment here: the apply loop and the effective-config fetch are the foundation it builds on.

docs.title: Affected code (dd9.9)
docs.text:
Area Path Effective-config fetch (kiosk-id aware) deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py (fetch_config) Version-gated apply + apply_device_physical deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py (run, new fn) Reuse rotation apply apply_rotation / detect_primary_output (existing) Tests deploy/kiosk-agent/test_display_agent.py Docs docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md (agent now applies per-kiosk orientation)

No server/API change (dd9.3 already serves everything). No new dependency (stdlib).

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• POST-back last_applied_version to the server (management-UI/confirmation slice).
  • Brightness / output-selection / resolution apply (follow-on; overlaps dd9.1; brightness needs backlight sysfs or ddcutil).
  • The full dd9.5 multi-output build (own spec/plan).

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. Brightness/output and the POST-back are deliberately deferred; dd9.5 is outlined and will get its own detailed design.

docs.title: Kiosks management UI (list + orientation editor) — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-12
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issue: epic calvin-dd9 (the management-UI surface; new child to file)
  • Base branch: develop (this design lives on feature/kiosks-management-ui)
  • Builds on: dd9.2 (GET /api/kiosks), dd9.3 (GET/PUT /api/kiosks/{id}/overrides), dd9.6/dd9.9 (orientation is a per-kiosk override the display-agent applies).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Everything to configure a kiosk exists in the API, but there is no UI: per-kiosk overrides can only be set with curl. This slice adds a Kiosks settings view that lists known kiosks and lets an operator set the selected kiosk's orientation override — the first, end-to-end-usable increment of per-kiosk management. Content assignment (availableScreens/defaultScreenId) and the confirmed apply-status are follow-ons.

docs.title: Design principle (frontend-design)
docs.text: This view lives inside Calvin's existing settings shell (CategoryRail, SettingsSection, SettingRow, SegmentedControl, ToggleSwitch) — reuse the existing design tokens/components; do not introduce a new palette or type. The one considered, subject-true element is the apply-status signature: this UI manages physical screens over a network, so it makes each kiosk's connection state visible rather than pretending config is applied instantly.

docs.title: Components / files
docs.text: Unit Path Responsibility Kiosks store frontend/src/stores/kiosks.js (new) fetch list + per-kiosk overrides; save overrides; network-first + cache fallback Kiosks category view frontend/src/components/settings/categories/KiosksSettings.vue (new) master–detail: kiosk list + selected-kiosk orientation editor Category registration frontend/src/components/settings/settingsRegistry.js, frontend/src/views/Settings.vue add the kiosks category entry + id→component mapping Tests frontend/tests/unit/stores/kiosks.spec.js, frontend/tests/unit/components/KiosksSettings.spec.js (new) store + view behavior

docs.title: 1. Kiosks store (stores/kiosks.js)
docs.text: Pinia store, axios, following stores/webServices.js's network-first + utils/cache.js fallback pattern: - kiosks (ref, list) + loadKiosks() → axios.get("/api/kiosks") → {kiosks:[...]}; on network failure fall back to cached list (TTL cache), on success update cache. - fetchOverrides(id) → axios.get(/api/kiosks/${id}/overrides) → {id, overrides}; returns the raw override layer (or {}). 404 (unknown kiosk) → treat as {} (not yet overridden). - saveOverrides(id, overrides) → axios.put(/api/kiosks/${id}/overrides, {overrides}) (replaces the whole layer). Updates the store's cached copy on success. - IDs are URL-path components — encodeURIComponent(id) in the URLs.

docs.title: 2. Kiosks category view (KiosksSettings.vue) — master–detail
docs.text:
Kiosks ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  ┌ kitchen-3f9a2c ───────────────────── ● Online ┐   ← select
  │ raspberrypi · seen 4s ago                      │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌ hallway-b71e04 ──────────────────── ○ Offline ┐
  │ pi-hallway · seen 6h ago                       │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ▸ kitchen-3f9a2c — Orientation ─────────────────────   ← editor (selected)
     Orientation    [ Landscape | Portrait ]  ‹inherited from global›
     Flip 180°      ( ●──  off )
     Apply rotation ( ──● on )
                                        [ Reset to global ]
     Saved. This kiosk applies orientation at its next check-in (~30s).
  • List: one card per kiosk (from loadKiosks()): id (primary), reported hostname (secondary), relative last-seen ("seen 4s ago"), and the status pill. Selecting a card loads its overrides and reveals the editor.
  • Apply-status (v1): derived from lastSeen recency only — ● Online when last-seen is within a freshness window (≤ 2 minutes), else ○ Offline. (The confirmed ◐ Applying… → ● Up to date state needs the agent to POST back its applied deviceConfigVersion; that is a follow-on — see Non-goals. Do not fake it.)
  • Empty state: "No kiosks have connected yet. A kiosk registers itself the first time it loads the dashboard."
  • Load/error states: a fetch error shows the cached list with a quiet "Showing last known kiosks (offline)" note, matching the store's cache-fallback.

docs.title: 3. Orientation editor (selected kiosk)
docs.text:
Edits the kiosk's override layer using the effective value + Reset model (decision A):

  • Effective value shown = the kiosk's override if present, else the global default (from the config store: orientation / orientationFlipped / applyDisplayRotation).
  • Controls: SegmentedControl Orientation (Landscape / Portrait); ToggleSwitch Flip 180° (orientationFlipped); ToggleSwitch Apply rotation (applyDisplayRotation).
  • Inherited vs set clarity: each control shows ‹inherited from global› when the kiosk has no override for that key, and ‹set for this kiosk› once it does. This keeps model A honest — the operator always knows whether they're seeing the global default or a per-kiosk value.
  • On change: read-modify-write — merge the changed orientation key(s) into the kiosk's existing overrides and saveOverrides(id, merged). (dd9.3's PUT replaces the layer, so we send the full merged object; other override keys, e.g. future availableScreens, are preserved.)
  • Reset to global: a quiet secondary action, enabled only when an orientation override exists; it removes the three orientation keys from the override layer and saves, so the kiosk inherits the global default again.
  • Honest async copy (the physical rotation genuinely lags the save):
  • after save (online kiosk): "Saved. This kiosk applies orientation at its next check-in (~30s)."
  • after save (offline kiosk): "Saved. Changes apply when this kiosk reconnects."
  • No "Done ✓" — the server accepted the config; the screen hasn't necessarily turned yet.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
open Kiosks category → store.loadKiosks() (network-first, cache fallback) → render list + status
select kiosk → store.fetchOverrides(id) → editor shows effective orientation (override ?? global)
change a control → merge into overrides → store.saveOverrides(id, merged) → status→"Saved…" copy
Reset to global → drop orientation keys → saveOverrides → controls show ‹inherited from global›
(display-agent, dd9.9, applies the new orientation on the Pi within a poll cycle)

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• loadKiosks network failure → cached list + offline note (never a blank screen).
  • saveOverrides failure → keep the editor's edited values, show "Couldn't save to the server. Check the connection and try again." (interface voice; actionable), do not silently drop the edit.
  • Unknown-kiosk 404 on fetchOverrides → treated as empty overrides (a just-seen kiosk with no overrides yet).

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text:
• Store (kiosks.spec.js): loadKiosks returns the list and caches it; network failure falls back to cache; fetchOverrides maps 404 → {}; saveOverrides PUTs {overrides} and updates the cache; URL encoding of ids.
  • View (KiosksSettings.spec.js): renders the list + relative last-seen; empty state when no kiosks; status pill Online vs Offline by last-seen window; selecting a kiosk shows the editor with the effective orientation (override over global); changing orientation calls saveOverrides with the merged layer (preserving unrelated keys); Reset to global removes only the orientation keys and is disabled when no override exists; inherited/set tags reflect override presence; post-save copy shown.
  • All new tests via Vitest; the view uses the existing shell components (already tested).

docs.title: Non-goals (follow-ons)
docs.text:
• Content assignment editor (availableScreens/defaultScreenId, incl. a screen multi-select + default picker) — the next UI slice.
  • Confirmed apply-status (◐ Applying… → ● Up to date) — needs the display-agent to POST back its applied deviceConfigVersion and a server endpoint to record it (the deferred confirmation loop). File as a follow-on; v1 ships Online/Offline + honest post-save copy.
  • Editing global config from here (that's the existing Device/Display categories), and multi-screen.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. The apply-status is deliberately scoped to Online/Offline for v1; the confirmed-apply upgrade is a filed follow-on so the signature can grow without faking state now.

docs.title: Device-local output + resolution via the display-agent — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-13
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issue: calvin-dd9.1 (Tier 1: device-local display settings via /etc/default/calvin-kiosk + display-agent)
  • Base branch: develop (this design lives on feature/dd9.1-device-display)
  • Builds on: the shipped rotation path (dd9.9) — apply_device_physical / apply_rotation in deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py, gated on deviceConfigVersion.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: In Mode B (central server + dumb kiosks) the backend cannot run local xrandr, so device-physical display settings are applied on the Pi by the display-agent. Rotation already works this way. This slice extends the same pattern to the two remaining xrandr-applied settings — which output is primary and screen resolution/mode — so an operator can set them per-Pi without SSH. Brightness (a different mechanism: backlight sysfs / ddcutil) is a separate follow-on.

docs.title: Design principle
docs.text: Mirror the shipped rotation path exactly — same dual source (device-local env var wins over server config), same deviceConfigVersion-gated apply, same one-shot-at-startup + on-change trigger, same monkeypatched-subprocess test idiom. Add small, independently tested apply functions; do not restructure the agent. No backend changes are required: displayOutput and displayResolution are already members of DEVICE_PHYSICAL_KEYS (backend/app/services/kiosk_registry.py), so the version hash already covers them.

docs.title: Locked context (verified in develop)
docs.text:
• apply_device_physical(cfg, *, applier=apply_rotation, env=None) runs when deviceConfigVersion changes (and once at startup via main()); it currently resolves the target output from CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT and applies rotation via apply_rotation(rotation, output=None) → ["xrandr", "--output", out, "--rotate", rotation], auto-detecting the output with detect_primary_output() when none is given.
  • cfg_get(cfg, "snake_case", "camelCase", default=…) reads both key spellings.
  • CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env wins over server orientation; CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT env supplies the output name. Both are read from /etc/default/calvin-kiosk (systemd EnvironmentFile).
  • DEVICE_PHYSICAL_KEYS already includes displayOutput, displayResolution (and displayBrightness, reserved for the brightness follow-on).
  • Tests live in deploy/kiosk-agent/test_display_agent.py (pytest, pure stdlib): they monkeypatch agent.subprocess.run to capture the command list and assert the exact xrandr … argv, and inject fetch/sleep/iterations/apply_device/applier for the loop and apply seams.
  • There is no setup-kiosk.sh; the env file is documented in docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md.

docs.title: Keys + precedence
docs.text:
Setting Server key (camelCase / snake) Env override (/etc/default/calvin-kiosk) Value format Primary output displayOutput / display_output CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT (already read) xrandr output name, e.g. HDMI-1 Resolution/mode displayResolution / display_resolution CALVIN_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION (new) WIDTHxHEIGHT or WIDTHxHEIGHT@RATE, e.g. 1920x1080 or 1920x1080@60

Precedence for each setting (mirrors rotation): env override → server config → (output only) auto-detect. An absent/empty value means skip that setting and leave the hardware as-is — never force a default.

docs.title: Apply
docs.text:
Extend apply_device_physical to, on each device-physical apply:

  1. Resolve the target output once: CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT env → server displayOutput → detect_primary_output(). Call this out.
  2. Apply output + mode first (before rotation), via a new apply_mode(output, resolution):
  3. Parse resolution: split on @ into mode (e.g. 1920x1080) and optional rate (e.g. 60). The mode must match ^\d+x\d+$; rate (if present) must be a positive number. If resolution is set but malformed, log a warning and skip the mode (do not run xrandr with a bad argument).
  4. Build argv:
    • resolution present + valid: ["xrandr", "--output", out, "--primary", "--mode", mode] (+ ["--rate", rate] when a rate was given);
    • output configured but no resolution: ["xrandr", "--output", out, "--primary"];
    • neither configured: do nothing (return a skip marker).
  5. Run it with the existing X11_ENV; a non-zero exit or exception is logged and swallowed (returns a skip/failure marker) — it must not raise out of apply_device_physical.
  6. Apply rotation last via the existing apply_rotation(rotation, output=out), so rotation wins if a mode change reset it.

Setting an output (env or server) marks it --primary. This is a deliberate, documented extension of today's behavior, where CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT only targeted rotation; under this design, configuring the output also selects it as primary — which is the dd9.1 goal ("which HDMI output is primary").

apply_mode returns a small result (the applied argv, or a skip/failure marker) so the loop can log it, mirroring how apply_rotation returns the output name or None.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• Malformed resolution (fails the WxH[@RATE] parse) → warn + skip the mode; still apply output-primary and rotation.
  • xrandr non-zero / raises (unknown output, unsupported mode) → warn + skip; the loop continues and retries on the next device-config change. A failing mode apply must never crash run() or blank the screen (the agent's existing resilience contract — covered by a test).
  • Absent output and absent resolution → no xrandr call for this feature (rotation path unchanged).

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
deviceConfigVersion changes (or startup) → apply_device_physical(cfg, env):
    out = CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT | cfg.displayOutput | detect_primary_output()
    res = CALVIN_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION | cfg.displayResolution
    apply_mode(out, res):   xrandr --output out --primary [--mode WxH [--rate R]]   (parse-guarded, error-safe)
    apply_rotation(rotation, output=out):   xrandr --output out --rotate …          (unchanged, runs last)

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text:
Add to deploy/kiosk-agent/test_display_agent.py (pytest, monkeypatch agent.subprocess.run to capture argv), mirroring the rotation tests:

  • apply_mode builds ["xrandr","--output","HDMI-1","--primary","--mode","1920x1080"] for ("HDMI-1", "1920x1080").
  • @RATE variant appends ["--rate","60"] for 1920x1080@60.
  • output-only (resolution=None) → ["xrandr","--output","HDMI-1","--primary"].
  • neither output-config nor resolution → no xrandr mode call (skip marker), rotation path untouched.
  • malformed resolution ("1080p", "1920x", "1920x1080@x") → no --mode argv, warning path, no raise.
  • xrandr returns non-zero for the mode → apply_mode returns a failure marker and does not raise.
  • precedence: CALVIN_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION env wins over server displayResolution; CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT env wins over server displayOutput.
  • ordering: within one apply_device_physical, the mode xrandr call is captured before the rotate call.
  • version-gating unchanged: apply_device_physical still fires once at startup and on deviceConfigVersion change, not on unrelated config changes (existing tests keep passing).

All tests pure-stdlib; run with pytest deploy/kiosk-agent/test_display_agent.py.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: In docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md, extend the /etc/default/calvin-kiosk env-key documentation to list CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT (output name, marks it primary) and CALVIN_DISPLAY_RESOLUTION (WxH / WxH@RATE), noting env overrides server config and that both are applied by the display-agent via xrandr at startup and on change.

docs.title: Non-goals (follow-ons)
docs.text:
• Brightness (backlight sysfs / ddcutil) — a different, hardware-variable mechanism that can black out a panel; its own slice. File as a dd9.1 follow-on.
  • A per-kiosk UI for output/resolution in the Kiosks settings view — the server keys already exist; authoring UI is a later slice (like the orientation/content editors).
  • Multi-output / multi-screen mapping (one Pi driving several outputs with different content) — that is dd9.5.
  • Refresh-rate discovery / validation against xrandr modes — v1 passes the mode/rate through and lets xrandr reject invalid combinations (logged, skipped); it does not pre-validate against available modes.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None blocking. The env+server dual-path (mirroring rotation) and marking the configured output --primary were approved in brainstorming.

docs.title: Kiosk region-focus targets the effective active screen — design
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-07-13
  • Status: Approved (brainstorm), pending implementation plan
  • Issue: calvin-dd9.8 (BUG — kiosk region-focus targets global active screen; read/write asymmetry). Discovered in the dd9.4 whole-branch review.
  • Base branch: develop (this design lives on feature/dd9.8-region-focus)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: In kiosk mode the active screen is local (kioskActiveScreenId), and reads honor it — getActiveRegion() resolves through effectiveDashboardScreens (which overrides activeScreenId with kioskActiveScreenId in kiosk mode). But the region-focus writes don't: cycleActiveDashboardRegionBy, updateRegionView, focusRegion, and the region_next/region_prev keyboard actions all pass the raw global dashboardScreens.value to layout helpers that locate the active screen from screensConfig.activeScreenId (the global field).
